title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
聖天子御極之二年丁卯天下例
當大比江西省臣具其事白
于前巡按監察御史臧〔鳳〕凡
科場中隘者闢之廢者舉之
污者疕之缺者剔之百度爲
之一新預期走書幣四方禮
===
聘儒紳以司考較既而教諭
范〔邦彥〕周〔瀾〕潘〔中矩〕訓導陳
〔允諸〕熊〔永昌〕郭〔懿〕自京畿至
教諭范〔魯〕訓導吳〔彰德〕自兩
浙至訓導范〔璟〕胡〔崇易〕自中
州至而〔禎〕則至自關中焉及
期巡按監察御史弓〔元〕奉
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

聖天子御極之二年丁卯，天下例當大比。江西省臣具其事，白于前巡按監察御史臧〔鳳〕。凡科場中隘者闢之，廢者舉之，污者疕之，缺者剔之，百度爲之一新。預期走書幣四方，禮聘儒紳以司考較。既而教諭范〔邦彥〕、周〔瀾〕、潘〔中矩〕，訓導陳〔允諸〕、熊〔永昌〕、郭〔懿〕自京畿至；教諭范〔魯〕、訓導吳〔彰德〕自兩浙至；訓導范〔璟〕、胡〔崇易〕自中州至；而〔禎〕則至自關中焉。及期，巡按監察御史弓〔元〕奉
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the second year of the sagely Son of Heaven’s reign, the dingmao year (1507), the triennial examinations were due to be held throughout the empire according to established practice. The provincial officials of Jiangxi prepared the arrangements and reported them to the previous Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Zang Feng. Within the examination compound, cramped spaces were opened up, disused facilities were restored, fouled areas were cleaned [?], and deficiencies were remedied [?]. All arrangements were thereby renewed. Well before the appointed time, letters and gifts were dispatched in every direction to invite learned gentlemen with due ceremony to oversee the examination and assessment.

Thereupon Instructors Fan Bangyan, Zhou Lan, and Pan Zhongju, and Assistant Instructors Chen Yunzhu, Xiong Yongchang, and Guo Yi arrived from the capital region; Instructor Fan Lu and Assistant Instructor Wu Zhangde arrived from Liangzhe; and Assistant Instructors Fan Jing and Hu Chongyi arrived from Zhongzhou. I, Zhen, arrived from Guanzhong. When the appointed time came, Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Gong Yuan respectfully received…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
命來代八月七日戊寅鎖院己卯
夜分出題〔禎〕等焚香相與誓
告曰科目興賢在
國家爲第一大事在天下爲第
一公道隸兹事者苟急以私
明有法律幽有鬼神可不念
哉可不慎哉誓畢合副使蔡
===
清〔〕所取十三郡之士九三千
有奇而群試之庚辰初試癸
未再試丙戌三試既試而分
經較卷范〔璟〕胡〔崇易〕郭〔懋〕較
易范〔邦彥〕陳〔允諧〕較書周〔瀾〕
熊〔永昌〕吳〔彰德〕潘〔中㷡〕較詩
范〔魯〕較春秋〔禎〕則較禮記而
punctuated: 命來代。八月七日戊寅，鎖院。己卯夜分出題，〔禎〕等焚香，相與誓告曰：「科目興賢，在國家爲第一大事，在天下爲第一公道。隸兹事者，苟急以私，明有法律，幽有鬼神，可不念哉！可不慎哉！」誓畢，合副使蔡清〔〕所取十三郡之士九三千有奇，而群試之。庚辰初試，癸未再試，丙戌三試。既試，而分經較卷。范〔璟〕、胡〔崇易〕、郭〔懋〕較《易》，范〔邦彥〕、陳〔允諧〕較《書》，周〔瀾〕、熊〔永昌〕、吳〔彰德〕、潘〔中㷡〕較《詩》，范〔魯〕較《春秋》，〔禎〕則較《禮記》，而
translation_en: …orders to come and take over. On the seventh day of the eighth month, wuyin, the examination compound was sealed. At midnight on jimao, the questions were issued. Zhen and the others burned incense and together solemnly swore: “Bringing forward worthy men through the examinations is the foremost affair of state and the foremost expression of impartiality under Heaven. If those entrusted with this undertaking pursue private interests, there are laws in the visible world and ghosts and spirits in the unseen world. Can we fail to bear this in mind? Can we fail to exercise caution?” When the oath was concluded, the candidates selected from the thirteen prefectures by Vice Commissioner Cai Qing were assembled and examined together. Their number was over ‘nine-three thousand’ [?]. The first session was held on gengchen, the second on guiwei, and the third on bingxu. After the examinations, the scripts were divided by Classic for assessment. Fan Jing, Hu Chongyi, and Guo Mao assessed the Book of Changes; Fan Bangyan and Chen Yunxie assessed the Book of Documents; Zhou Lan, Xiong Yongchang, Wu Zhangde, and Pan Zhongjiong [?] assessed the Book of Odes; Fan Lu assessed the Spring and Autumn Annals; and Zhen assessed the Book of Rites, and…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
又與范〔邦彥〕總較各經焉其
較閱亦可謂精矣較後而定
去取本之初試以取其經學
之醇粲之再試以取其識見
之博又粲之三試以取其時
務之通敏必理路明鬯者取
之必趣味雋永者取之必氣
===
昌而大辭順而美者取之然
其間或冗而泛者必黜懼其
有以汩文之源〔也〕或鑿而深
者必黜懼其有以晦文之理
也或弱而淺者必黜懼其有
以索文之氣也或尖新而怪
險者必黜懼其有以壞文之
punctuated: 又與范〔邦彥〕總較各經焉。其較閱亦可謂精矣。較後而定去取，本之初試，以取其經學之醇；粲之再試，以取其識見之博；又粲之三試，以取其時務之通敏。必理路明鬯者取之，必趣味雋永者取之，必氣昌而大、辭順而美者取之。然其間或冗而泛者必黜，懼其有以汩文之源〔也〕；或鑿而深者必黜，懼其有以晦文之理也；或弱而淺者必黜，懼其有以索文之氣也；或尖新而怪險者必黜，懼其有以壞文之
translation_en: …and, together with Fan〔Bangyan〕, also conducted an overall assessment of the papers on all the Classics. Their scrutiny may indeed be called meticulous. After assessing the papers, they determined whom to reject and whom to select. They took the first session as their basis, selecting for purity of classical learning; they further examined [?] the second session, selecting for breadth of knowledge and judgment; and they further examined [?] the third session, selecting for thorough understanding and acuity in current affairs. They selected only those whose reasoning was clear and fluent, whose thought had depth and enduring savor, and whose writing possessed abundant, expansive vigor and smooth, elegant expression. Yet any papers that were prolix and diffuse were invariably rejected, lest they muddy the wellspring of writing; any that were strained and abstruse were invariably rejected, lest they obscure the principles of writing; any that were feeble and shallow were invariably rejected, lest they drain writing of its vitality; and any that pursued contrived novelty and bizarre, precarious expression were invariably rejected, lest they damage writing’s…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
體也其去取亦可謂嚴矣旣
精且嚴而又本之以公濟之
以明宜其去取罔有不當者
然以蘇軾反遺李廌歐陽脩
誤取劉煇況區區藻鑑之下
安能保其去取一一之當耶
第求諸心無愧而已夫是舉
===
也作興則有鎮守太監姚〔舉〕
贊相則有清戎御史吳〔堂〕而
南京戶部主事談〔倫〕適以公
事至省其提調於內則有左
布政使戈〔瑄〕左參議董〔威〕監
試於內則有按察使陸〔完〕副
使楊〔錦〕其防範維持於外則
punctuated:
體也。其去取亦可謂嚴矣。旣精且嚴，而又本之以公，濟之以明，宜其去取罔有不當者。然以蘇軾反遺李廌，歐陽脩誤取劉煇，況區區藻鑑之下，安能保其去取一一之當耶？第求諸心無愧而已。
夫是舉也，作興則有鎮守太監姚〔舉〕，贊相則有清戎御史吳〔堂〕，而南京戶部主事談〔倫〕適以公事至省。其提調於內則有左布政使戈〔瑄〕、左參議董〔威〕，監試於內則有按察使陸〔完〕、副使楊〔錦〕，其防範維持於外則
translation_en:
…the form of writing. Our decisions to reject or accept may indeed be called strict. Since our scrutiny was both meticulous and strict, grounded moreover in impartiality and aided by discernment, one might expect every decision to have been appropriate. Yet even Su Shi overlooked Li Zhi, and Ouyang Xiu mistakenly selected Liu Hui. How, then, could our own modest powers of literary judgment guarantee that every rejection and acceptance was correct? We seek only to examine our hearts and find nothing to be ashamed of.
For this examination, the Grand Defender, Eunuch Director Yao Ju, provided encouragement and support, while Wu Tang, the censor charged with inspecting military affairs, assisted with its conduct. Tan Lun, a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, also happened to arrive in the provincial capital on official business. Serving as Proctors within the examination compound were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Ge Xuan and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Dong Wei. Overseeing the examination within were Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Lu Wan and Vice Surveillance Commissioner Yang Jin. As for guarding against irregularities and maintaining order outside, there were…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
有右布政使馬〔龍〕左叅政楊
〔守隅〕右叅政陳〔鎬〕右叅議李
〔□〕副使周〔□〕僉事王〔純〕王〔啓〕
何〔俊〕沈〔煉〕都指揮同知何〔昇〕
與夫百執事亦皆遴選以充
而御史〔元〕實監臨之自鎻院
至撤棘凡二十有一日咸以
日繼夜殫厥心力罔敢怠忽
===
事竣當有録以
獻中乃次第其所取士之姓名
九十有五人并刻其文之粹
者二十篇與有事于場屋者
五十有七人録當有序〔□〕敢
僭一言于首嗚呼自成周里
punctuated:
有右布政使馬〔龍〕、左叅政楊〔守隅〕、右叅政陳〔鎬〕、右叅議李〔□〕、副使周〔□〕、僉事王〔純〕、王〔啓〕、何〔俊〕、沈〔煉〕、都指揮同知何〔昇〕，與夫百執事，亦皆遴選以充。而御史〔元〕實監臨之。自鎻院至撤棘，凡二十有一日，咸以日繼夜，殫厥心力，罔敢怠忽。
事竣，當有録以獻。中乃次第其所取士之姓名，九十有五人，并刻其文之粹者二十篇，與有事于場屋者五十有七人。録當有序，〔□〕敢僭一言于首。嗚呼！自成周里
translation_en:
…there were Ma Long 馬龍, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Yang Shouyu 楊守隅, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Chen Hao 陳鎬, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Li □ 李□, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zhou □ 周□, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Wang Chun 王純, Wang Qi 王啓, He Jun 何俊, and Shen Lian 沈煉, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; and He Sheng 何昇, Associate Regional Military Commissioner. All the other functionaries, too, were carefully selected to fill their posts. Censor Yuan 元 exercised overall supervision. From the sealing of the examination compound to the removal of its thorn barriers, twenty-one days elapsed. All worked through the nights as well as the days, exhausting their mental and physical strength; none dared be negligent.
Once the proceedings were concluded, a record was required for presentation to the throne. Zhong 中 [?] therefore arranged in order the names of the ninety-five selected candidates and had printed twenty of their finest compositions, together with the names of the fifty-seven men who had served in the examination compound. The record required a preface, so I, □, venture to presume to place a few words at its beginning. Alas! Ever since the village selection system of the fully established Zhou dynasty…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
選之法廢而科目興論者皆病
其人惟口耳浮華是習而於
身心性命之理或不之講殊
不知科目爲
昭代之制而科目中亦未必無人
姑以江西諸先達言之有文
章事業名冠天下者有孤忠
大節與烈日爭光者有道學
===
淵粹著書萬言老而不倦者
彼獨非科目中士乎諸士子
登名斯錄者蓋有不出於鄉
而得師焉俾天下後世指而
稱之曰若某若某此正德
龍飛第一科所取士也豈不偉哉
punctuated: 選之法廢而科目興，論者皆病其人惟口耳浮華是習，而於身心性命之理或不之講。殊不知科目爲昭代之制，而科目中亦未必無人。姑以江西諸先達言之：有文章事業名冠天下者，有孤忠大節與烈日爭光者，有道學淵粹、著書萬言、老而不倦者。彼獨非科目中士乎？諸士子登名斯錄者，蓋有不出於鄉而得師焉。俾天下後世指而稱之曰：「若某若某，此正德龍飛第一科所取士也。」豈不偉哉！
translation_en: …the method of selection was abandoned and the examination system arose. Critics all deplore the fact that its men cultivate only superficial learning passed from ear to mouth and empty literary ornament, while perhaps neglecting to investigate the principles of the person and the mind, human nature and Heaven’s endowment. They fail to understand that the examination system is an institution of our illustrious dynasty, and that it is by no means necessarily devoid of worthy men. Take, for example, the eminent predecessors of Jiangxi: some have won foremost renown throughout the realm for their writings and public achievements; some, steadfast in solitary loyalty and lofty integrity, have rivaled the blazing sun in brilliance; some have been profound and pure in their learning of the Way, writing tens of thousands of words and remaining tireless into old age. Were these not also men who came through the examinations? The candidates whose names appear in this record can surely find teachers among them without leaving their native province. May they cause people throughout the realm and in later generations to point to them and say: “Such-and-such men were selected in the first examination following the Zhengde Emperor’s accession.” Would that not be magnificent!

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
陝西慶陽府儒學教授田〔禎〕
謹序
punctuated: 陝西慶陽府儒學教授田〔禎〕謹序。
translation_en: Preface respectfully written by Tian Zhen, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
正德二年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史弓元〔大方應天府江浦縣人 丙辰進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使戈瑄〔廷玉直隸景州人 乙未進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議董威〔德隅直隸威縣人 丁未進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司按察使陸完〔全卿直隸長洲縣人 丁未進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司副使楊錦〔尚絅直隸嘉定縣人 丁未進士〕
===
考試官
陝西慶陽府儒學教授田禎〔世隆山東利津縣人 己酉貢士〕
直隸河間府任丘縣儒學教諭范羿彥〔時望應天府江寧縣人 乙卯貢士〕
同考試官
直隸保定府清苑縣儒學教諭周瀾〔文源浙江慈谿縣人 甲子貢士〕
浙江紹興府餘姚縣儒學教諭范魯〔得之四川巴縣人 丙午貢士〕
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒學教諭范璟〔子溫山東沂州人 辛酉貢士〕
直隸河間府河間縣儒學教諭潘中矩〔儀之河南澠池縣人 甲子貢士〕
直隸蘇州府長洲縣儒學訓導熊永智〔以謙四川酆都縣人 庚子貢士〕
punctuated:
正德二年江西鄉試

監臨官：
巡按江西監察御史弓元〔大方，應天府江浦縣人，丙辰進士〕。

提調官：
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使戈瑄〔廷玉，直隸景州人，乙未進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議董威〔德隅，直隸威縣人，丁未進士〕。

監試官：
江西等處提刑按察司按察使陸完〔全卿，直隸長洲縣人，丁未進士〕。
江西等處提刑按察司副使楊錦〔尚絅，直隸嘉定縣人，丁未進士〕。

考試官：
陝西慶陽府儒學教授田禎〔世隆，山東利津縣人，己酉貢士〕。
直隸河間府任丘縣儒學教諭范羿彥〔時望，應天府江寧縣人，乙卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
直隸保定府清苑縣儒學教諭周瀾〔文源，浙江慈谿縣人，甲子貢士〕。
浙江紹興府餘姚縣儒學教諭范魯〔得之，四川巴縣人，丙午貢士〕。
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒學教諭范璟〔子溫，山東沂州人，辛酉貢士〕。
直隸河間府河間縣儒學教諭潘中矩〔儀之，河南澠池縣人，甲子貢士〕。
直隸蘇州府長洲縣儒學訓導熊永智〔以謙，四川酆都縣人，庚子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, Second Year of Zhengde (1507)

Supervising Official
Gong Yuan, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Jiangxi, courtesy name Dafang, was from Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingchen year.

Proctors
Ge Xuan, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Tingyu, was from Jingzhou, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the yiwei year.
Dong Wei, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Deyu, was from Wei County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Examination Monitoring Officials
Lu Wan, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Quanqing, was from Changzhou County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Yang Jin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi, courtesy name Shangjiong, was from Jiading County, Zhili. He was a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.

Examiners
Tian Zhen, Professor at the Confucian School of Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi, courtesy name Shilong, was from Lijin County, Shandong. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiyou year.
Fan Yiyan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Shiwang, was from Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a tribute scholar of the yimao year.

Associate Examiners
Zhou Lan, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qingyuan County, Baoding Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Wenyuan, was from Cixi County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.
Fan Lu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Dezhi, was from Ba County, Sichuan. He was a tribute scholar of the bingwu year.
Fan Jing, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shangshui County, Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Ziwen, was from Yizhou, Shandong. He was a tribute scholar of the xinyou year.
Pan Zhongju, Instructor at the Confucian School of Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Yizhi, was from Mianchi County, Henan. He was a tribute scholar of the jiazi year.
Xiong Yongzhi, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, courtesy name Yiqian, was from Fengdu County, Sichuan. He was a tribute scholar of the gengzi year.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
順天府儒學訓導陳光詔〔舜卿福建莆田縣人　丙午貢士〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子謂韶盡美矣又盡善也
能盡其性則能盡人之性能盡人之性則
能盡物之性
賢者在位能者在職
易
以祉元吉中以行願也
君子以勞民勸相
===
見乃謂之象形乃謂之器制而用之謂之
法利用出入民咸用之謂之神
吉人之辭寡
書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣
立愛惟親立敬惟長
方行天下至于海表罔有不服
德威惟畏德明惟明乃命三后恤功于民
伯夷降典折民惟刑禹平水土主名山
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
子謂韶：「盡美矣，又盡善也。」
能盡其性，則能盡人之性；能盡人之性，則能盡物之性。
賢者在位，能者在職。

易
以祉元吉，中以行願也。
君子以勞民勸相。
見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。
吉人之辭寡。

書
萬邦黎獻，共惟帝臣。
立愛惟親，立敬惟長。
方行天下，至于海表，罔有不服。
德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后恤功于民：伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The Master said of the Shao music: “It is perfectly beautiful, and also perfectly good.”
One who can fully realize his own nature can fully realize the nature of others; one who can fully realize the nature of others can fully realize the nature of things.
The worthy occupy positions of authority, and the capable hold office.

Book of Changes
“Blessings bring supreme good fortune”: through maintaining the mean, one fulfills one's aspirations.
The gentleman accordingly comforts the people and encourages them to assist one another.
What becomes manifest is called an image; what takes shape is called a concrete object; what is fashioned for use is called a method. What facilitates use in coming and going, and is employed by all the people, is called numinous.
The words of an auspicious person are few.

Book of Documents
The many worthy men of the myriad states are all servants of the emperor.
In establishing love, begin with one's parents; in establishing respect, begin with one's elders.
He went freely throughout the realm, reaching beyond the seas; none failed to submit.
His virtue inspired awe and was held in awe; his virtue shone brightly and was recognized as bright. He then charged the three lords to devote themselves to beneficial work for the people: Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, guiding the people by proper standards; Yu put the waters and land in order, taking charge of the great mountains …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
川稷降播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷
于民士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
詩
彼姝者子何以畀之
如月之恒如日之升如南山之壽
天監有周昭假于下保茲天子生仲山甫
濟濟多士克廣德心桓桓于征狄彼東南
烝烝皇皇不吳不揚不告于訩在泮獻
功角弓其觩束矢其搜戎車孔博徒御
===
無斁既克淮夷孔淑不逆式固爾猶淮
夷卒獲翩彼飛鴞集于泮林食我桑黮
懷我好音憬彼淮夷來獻其琛元龜象
齒大賂南金
春秋
春正月公會宋公蔡侯衛侯于曹　夏四
月公會宋公衛侯陳侯蔡侯伐鄭　秋
七月公至自伐鄭〔桓公十六年〕
紀季以酅入于齊〔莊公三年〕
punctuated:
川，稷降播種，農殖嘉穀，三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。

詩
彼姝者子，何以畀之？
如月之恒，如日之升，如南山之壽。
天監有周，昭假于下，保茲天子，生仲山甫。
濟濟多士，克廣德心，桓桓于征，狄彼東南。
烝烝皇皇，不吳不揚，不告于訩，在泮獻功。角弓其觩，束矢其搜，戎車孔博，徒御無斁。既克淮夷，孔淑不逆，式固爾猶，淮夷卒獲。翩彼飛鴞，集于泮林，食我桑黮，懷我好音。憬彼淮夷，來獻其琛，元龜象齒，大賂南金。

春秋
春正月，公會宋公、蔡侯、衛侯于曹。夏四月，公會宋公、衛侯、陳侯、蔡侯伐鄭。秋七月，公至自伐鄭。〔桓公十六年〕
紀季以酅入于齊。〔莊公三年〕
translation_en:
…rivers. Ji imparted the sowing of seed, cultivating fine grains. These three lords accomplished their work and richly benefited the people. The officer of justice regulated the people through balanced punishments, teaching them to revere virtue.

Book of Odes
That beautiful young man—what shall be given to him?
Like the waxing moon, like the rising sun, like the enduring Southern Mountain.
Heaven watched over Zhou; its brightness reached down below. To protect this Son of Heaven, it brought forth Zhongshan Fu.
The many worthy men could broaden their virtuous resolve. Martial in their campaigns, they brought the southeast into submission.
Advancing in multitudes, imposing in bearing, they neither clamored nor boasted, nor made contentious accusations; at the Pan school they presented their achievements. Their horn bows were curved, their bundles of arrows orderly; their war chariots were very large, their foot soldiers and charioteers tireless. Having overcome the Huai Yi, they were thoroughly good and not defiant. Firmly uphold your plans, and the Huai Yi will finally be taken. Those fluttering owls alight in the woods by the Pan school; they eat our mulberries and offer us pleasant calls. Those distant Huai Yi come to present their treasures: great tortoise shells and elephant tusks, and abundant gifts of southern gold.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, in the first month, the duke met with the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, and the Marquis of Wei at Cao. In summer, in the fourth month, the duke joined the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Marquis of Chen, and the Marquis of Cai in attacking Zheng. In autumn, in the seventh month, the duke returned from the attack on Zheng. 〔Sixteenth year of Duke Huan〕
Ji Ji brought Xi under the authority of Qi. 〔Third year of Duke Zhuang〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽〔僖公三十三年〕
侯及秦師戰于彭衙秦師敗績　晉人
宋人陳人鄭人伐秦〔文公二年〕秦人伐
晉〔文公三年〕
蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于柏舉　吳入郢
〔定公四年〕
禮記
博聞強識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
洞洞乎其敬也屬屬乎其忠也勿勿乎其
欲其饗之也
===
昔者舜作五絃之琴以歌南風
吾語女禮猶有九焉大饗有四焉
第貳場
論
聖人以天下才治天下事
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢却千里馬詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以陸贄為翰林學士誥〔建中四年〕
punctuated:
晉人及姜戎敗秦于殽。〔僖公三十三年〕
侯及秦師戰于彭衙，秦師敗績。晉人、宋人、陳人、鄭人伐秦。〔文公二年〕秦人伐晉。〔文公三年〕
蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于柏舉。吳入郢。〔定公四年〕
禮記
博聞強識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。
洞洞乎其敬也，屬屬乎其忠也，勿勿乎其欲其饗之也。
昔者舜作五絃之琴，以歌南風。
吾語女禮，猶有九焉；大饗有四焉。
第貳場
論
聖人以天下才治天下事。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢却千里馬詔。〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以陸贄為翰林學士誥。〔建中四年〕
translation_en:
The men of Jin and the Jiang Rong defeated Qin at Yao. 〔Thirty-third year of Duke Xi.〕
The marquis [of Jin?] fought the army of Qin at Pengya, and the army of Qin suffered a crushing defeat. The men of Jin, Song, Chen, and Zheng attacked Qin. 〔Second year of Duke Wen.〕 The men of Qin attacked Jin. 〔Third year of Duke Wen.〕
The Marquis of Cai, with the Viscount of Wu, fought the men of Chu at Boju. Wu entered Ying. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding.〕
Record of Rites
One who is widely learned, has a strong memory, yet remains modest, and earnestly practices good conduct without flagging is called a gentleman.
Profound is his reverence, unbroken his devotion, and eager his desire that the spirits enjoy his offerings.
In ancient times, Shun made a five-stringed zither to sing the song “South Wind.”
In what I tell you of ritual, there are still nine aspects; in the great sacrificial feast, there are four.
Second Session
Discourse
The sage employs the talents of all under Heaven to administer the affairs of all under Heaven.
Edicts, Appointments, and Memorials 〔One topic from among these [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor declining a horse capable of traveling a thousand li. 〔First year of Emperor Wen.〕
Compose a letter of appointment in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Lu Zhi as a Hanlin Academician. 〔Fourth year of the Jianzhong reign.〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
擬纂修
孝宗敬皇帝實錄成
進呈表
判語〔五條〕
收養孤老
違禁取利
同姓為婚
褻瀆神明
詐為瑞應
===
第叁場
第五道
問自古帝王之繼世必有心法相傳若堯
舜禹相傳心法之要載諸典謨卓乎其
不可尚已後世如大風之歌天馬之什
非不雄也第不知於心法果有所關歟
帝範之篇崇儒之論非不偉也第不知
於心法果有所補歟
天啓
punctuated:
擬纂修孝宗敬皇帝實錄成進呈表。

判語〔五條〕：收養孤老；違禁取利；同姓為婚；褻瀆神明；詐為瑞應。

第叁場。

第五道。

問：自古帝王之繼世，必有心法相傳。若堯、舜、禹相傳心法之要，載諸典謨，卓乎其不可尚已。後世如《大風》之歌、《天馬》之什，非不雄也，第不知於心法果有所關歟？《帝範》之篇、《崇儒》之論，非不偉也，第不知於心法果有所補歟？天啓
translation_en:
Draft a memorial submitting the completed Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong Jing.

Legal judgments 〔five items〕: Taking in and supporting orphans and the elderly; obtaining profit in violation of prohibitions; marriage between persons of the same surname; desecrating divine powers; fabricating auspicious portents.

Third Session

Fifth Question

Question: From antiquity, whenever emperors and kings succeeded to rule, there were essential teachings of the mind transmitted from one to another. The essentials of these teachings transmitted by Yao, Shun, and Yu are recorded in the Canons and Counsels of the Book of Documents; their excellence cannot be surpassed. In later ages, compositions such as the Song of the Great Wind and the verses on the Heavenly Horse were certainly majestic, yet did they truly have any connection with these teachings of the mind? The chapters of the Model for Emperors (Di fan) and the discourse on Honoring Confucian Learning (Chong ru) were certainly impressive, yet did they truly contribute anything to these teachings of the mind? Heaven inaugurated…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
皇明文運亨泰我
太宗文皇帝稟
上聖之資當
萬幾之暇
親洒宸翰製爲聖學心法一書歷叙古昔帝王
相傳心法之要至詳且備有非臣下一
時之所能殫述姑舉其大者與諸士子
言之心法所載有君道篇有臣道篇君
道莫大於敬天法祖用人理財四事而
已今可得而陳其槩歟抑不知漢唐宋
之君其於四事果有能行之者歟臣道
莫大於忠勤廉謹四德而已今可得而
舉其畧歟抑不知漢唐宋之臣其於四
德亦有能盡之者歟堯言萬世如見周
禮千古所崇諸士子之於
===
聖訓莊誦有年矣請敷對于篇用觀留心
昭代之學
問將者三軍之司命故古之用武者不急
punctuated:
皇明文運亨泰。我太宗文皇帝稟上聖之資，當萬幾之暇，親洒宸翰，製爲《聖學心法》一書，歷叙古昔帝王相傳心法之要，至詳且備，有非臣下一時之所能殫述。姑舉其大者，與諸士子言之。心法所載，有君道篇，有臣道篇。君道莫大於敬天、法祖、用人、理財四事而已。今可得而陳其槩歟？抑不知漢唐宋之君，其於四事果有能行之者歟？臣道莫大於忠、勤、廉、謹四德而已。今可得而舉其畧歟？抑不知漢唐宋之臣，其於四德亦有能盡之者歟？堯言萬世如見，周禮千古所崇。諸士子之於聖訓，莊誦有年矣。請敷對于篇，用觀留心昭代之學。

問：將者，三軍之司命，故古之用武者不急
translation_en:
…the literary fortunes of our august Ming have flourished. Our Emperor Taizong Wen, endowed with the qualities of a supreme sage, personally wielded the imperial brush during intervals amid his myriad affairs to compose the book Essential Teachings of Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). It recounts in succession, with the utmost detail and completeness, the essentials of the teachings of the mind transmitted among the emperors and kings of antiquity—more than a subject could fully expound on a single occasion. Let us therefore take up its major points and discuss them with you candidates. The work contains a chapter on the way of the ruler and a chapter on the way of the minister. In the ruler’s way, nothing is greater than these four matters: revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, employing men, and managing finances. Can you now set forth their general principles? Furthermore, were there rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song who truly put these four matters into practice? In the minister’s way, nothing is greater than these four virtues: loyalty, diligence, integrity, and circumspection. Can you now outline them? Furthermore, were there ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song who fully realized these four virtues? Yao’s words remain as though before our eyes through ten thousand generations; the rites of Zhou have been revered throughout the ages. You candidates have solemnly recited these sagely instructions for years. Please expound your answers in writing, so that we may see the attention you have devoted to the learning of this illustrious dynasty.

Question: A general holds the lives of the armies in his charge. Thus those who employed military force in antiquity did not give priority to…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
於馭軍而急於選將有以也第將有不
同而論之者不一試舉其槩與諸士子
商之將有五德而何以又有八弊歟將
有三善而何以又有八惡歟推轂而遣
者何義登壇而拜者何名將維鷹揚何
以不謂之飛將而數奇者反冐其名單
騎見虜何以不謂之驕將而浪戰者反
竊其號謂智將不如福將必若燕頷虎
頭斯謂之福將而運籌決勝者非智將
乎謂猛將不如謀將必若料敵設奇斯
===
謂之謀將而擁盾入侍者非猛將乎爵
位蟬聯不失為世將也而讀父書者何
以有長平之坑雅歌投壺不失為名將
也而工詞賦者何以有河陽之敗將老
則怯而據鞍跨馬者何矍鑠也將少則
驕而棄繻請纓者何英妙也方今
聖明御宇海内承平第北虜不恭時或犯我邊
疆擦鉢之勢無常而烽火之紅未熄一
punctuated:
於馭軍而急於選將，有以也。第將有不同，而論之者不一，試舉其槩，與諸士子商之。將有五德，而何以又有八弊歟？將有三善，而何以又有八惡歟？推轂而遣者何義？登壇而拜者何名？將維鷹揚，何以不謂之飛將，而數奇者反冐其名？單騎見虜，何以不謂之驕將，而浪戰者反竊其號？謂智將不如福將，必若燕頷虎頭，斯謂之福將，而運籌決勝者非智將乎？謂猛將不如謀將，必若料敵設奇，斯謂之謀將，而擁盾入侍者非猛將乎？爵位蟬聯，不失為世將也，而讀父書者何以有長平之坑？雅歌投壺，不失為名將也，而工詞賦者何以有河陽之敗？將老則怯，而據鞍跨馬者何矍鑠也？將少則驕，而棄繻請纓者何英妙也？

方今聖明御宇，海内承平，第北虜不恭，時或犯我邊疆，擦鉢之勢無常，而烽火之紅未熄。一
translation_en:
… in controlling armies, but instead gave priority to selecting generals: there was a reason for this. Yet generals differ, and judgments of them vary. Let us raise the main points for discussion with you examination candidates. Generals have five virtues; why, then, are they also said to have eight faults? Generals have three good qualities; why, then, are they also said to have eight evils? What was the meaning of pushing a general’s carriage wheel when sending him forth? Who was appointed after ascending a ceremonial platform? The general soared like a hawk: why was he not called the “Flying General,” while the man dogged by ill fortune instead bore that name? The man who rode alone to meet the enemy: why was he not called the “Proud General,” while the reckless fighter instead appropriated that title?

It is said that a wise general is inferior to a fortunate general. Must one have a swallow’s jaw and a tiger’s head to be called a fortunate general? And was the man who devised strategies and determined victories not a wise general? It is said that a fierce general is inferior to a resourceful general. Must one assess the enemy and devise surprise tactics to be called a resourceful general? And was the man who entered bearing a shield to attend his lord not a fierce general?

When noble rank and office pass down in succession, a man may indeed be called a general from a hereditary military family. Yet why did the man who read his father’s military writings bring about the burial of troops at Changping? Singing refined songs and playing pitch-pot need not prevent a man from being a distinguished general. Yet why did the man skilled in lyric poetry and rhapsodies suffer defeat at Heyang? Generals supposedly become timid in old age; why, then, was the man who mounted his horse and sat firmly in the saddle so vigorous? Young generals supposedly grow arrogant; why, then, were the men who discarded the silk token and requested a cord to bind the enemy so outstanding in their youthful prowess?

Now our sagely and enlightened sovereign rules the realm, and all within the seas enjoys peace. Yet the northern foes are insubordinate and sometimes violate our frontiers. The disposition of their encampments [?] is unpredictable, and the red glow of beacon fires has not died away. At this …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
時堪克將領者頗難其人此所以屢
當宁興拊髀之嘆而不能忘西顧之憂也迺
者
廷臣集議欲以廣求將材明揚之
詔屢下惜無以應其選者竊意側陋之中豈無
飛熊伏龍而深知將畧者乎我懷若人
適其有遇用將轉而薦之于
上庶竭區區以入事君之忠
===
問帝舜命契敷五教命臯陶明五刑教刑
並用其必有由矣竊疑古之聖人以德
化教民宜無俟於刑之用也茲必兼舉
而並行之豈以徒教之不足恃而必有
假於刑者歟至孔子則曰道之以政齊
之以刑民免而無耻道之以德齊之以
禮有耻且格孟子曰善政不如善教之
得民也則又似與帝舜之意相背馳何
歟且古之聖人宜莫如舜以大聖人之
作爲尚不可徒恃其教况後世者歟抑
punctuated:
時堪克將領者，頗難其人。此所以屢當宁興拊髀之嘆，而不能忘西顧之憂也。迺者，廷臣集議，欲以廣求將材，明揚之詔屢下，惜無以應其選者。竊意側陋之中，豈無飛熊伏龍而深知將畧者乎？我懷若人，適其有遇，用將轉而薦之于上，庶竭區區，以入事君之忠。

問：帝舜命契敷五教，命臯陶明五刑，教刑並用，其必有由矣。竊疑古之聖人以德化教民，宜無俟於刑之用也。茲必兼舉而並行之，豈以徒教之不足恃，而必有假於刑者歟？至孔子則曰：「道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無耻；道之以德，齊之以禮，有耻且格。」孟子曰：「善政不如善教之得民也。」則又似與帝舜之意相背馳，何歟？且古之聖人宜莫如舜，以大聖人之作爲，尚不可徒恃其教，况後世者歟？抑
translation_en:
…at present, men fit to serve as military commanders [?] are quite difficult to find. This is why His Majesty repeatedly sighs and slaps his thigh in regret, unable to put aside his concern as he looks westward. Recently, the court officials deliberated together on seeking military talent far and wide. Edicts calling for the recognition and advancement of worthy men have repeatedly been issued; regrettably, no one has come forward to meet the requirements for selection. I venture to think: among men living in humble obscurity, surely there are flying bears and hidden dragons—men of extraordinary talent who deeply understand military strategy? I long for such men. Should I happen to encounter one, I shall recommend him to His Majesty, hoping thereby to exert my modest abilities in loyal service to my sovereign [?].

Question: Emperor Shun commanded Xie to disseminate the Five Teachings and Gao Yao to make clear the Five Punishments. There must have been a reason for employing instruction and punishment together. Yet I venture to wonder: since the sages of antiquity taught and transformed the people through virtue, surely they should have had no need to employ punishment. If both had to be instituted and put into practice together, was it because instruction alone could not be relied upon, and recourse to punishment was indispensable? Confucius, however, said: “Guide them through governmental measures and bring them into line through punishments, and the people will evade punishment but have no sense of shame. Guide them through virtue and bring them into line through ritual propriety, and they will have a sense of shame and also correct themselves.” Mencius said: “Good government does not win the people as effectively as good instruction.” These statements, in turn, seem to run counter to Emperor Shun’s intentions. Why is this? Moreover, surely none of the sages of antiquity equaled Shun. If even the achievements of so great a sage could not rest on instruction alone, how much less could those of later ages? Or …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
其所謂教與刑者別有其說歟五教足
矣而何以周之制復有所謂十二教三
物之教五刑足矣而何以周之制復有
所謂八刑八辟八成之條聖人之立教
制刑以治天下固其所也然竊意周之
繁不若虞之簡聖人又豈樂爲是不一
之教不一之刑者哉後世之所謂教所
謂刑要皆法古而爲治何民協于中之
化比屋可封之俗卒不可復見歟諸生
必有其說願明著于篇以觀用世之學
===
問爲文無定體論文有定說然欲論諸子
之文當折衷於六經之說文而不本乎
六經則詞溢縹囊不外月露之形卷盈
緗帙盡出風雲之狀其亦何補於世而
何貴於文哉然自漢唐宋以來登名文
章之錄者何啻數十百家茲不暇縷陳
姑舉其尤者言之如賢良王命文非不
佳也而何獨取於天人之三策豈其言
punctuated:
其所謂教與刑者，別有其說歟？五教足矣，而何以周之制復有所謂十二教、三物之教？五刑足矣，而何以周之制復有所謂八刑、八辟、八成之條？聖人之立教制刑以治天下，固其所也。然竊意周之繁不若虞之簡，聖人又豈樂爲是不一之教、不一之刑者哉？後世之所謂教、所謂刑，要皆法古而爲治，何民協于中之化、比屋可封之俗，卒不可復見歟？諸生必有其說，願明著于篇，以觀用世之學。

問：爲文無定體，論文有定說。然欲論諸子之文，當折衷於六經之說。文而不本乎六經，則詞溢縹囊，不外月露之形；卷盈緗帙，盡出風雲之狀。其亦何補於世，而何貴於文哉？然自漢唐宋以來，登名文章之錄者，何啻數十百家？茲不暇縷陳，姑舉其尤者言之。如《賢良》《王命》，文非不佳也，而何獨取於《天人》之三策？豈其言
translation_en:
…is there some other explanation of what he meant by teaching and punishment? The five teachings suffice; why, then, did the institutions of Zhou also include the so-called twelve teachings and instruction in the three categories? The five punishments suffice; why, then, did the institutions of Zhou also include provisions for the eight punishments, the eight grounds for deliberation in criminal cases, and the eight established procedures? It was certainly proper for the sages to establish teachings and institute punishments to govern all under Heaven. Yet I venture to think that the complexity of Zhou was inferior to the simplicity of Yu. Surely the sages did not delight in such multiplicity of teachings and punishments? The teaching and punishment of later ages were, in essence, all modeled on antiquity as means of government. Why, then, have we never again seen the transforming influence that brought the people into accord with the mean, or customs so virtuous that every household merited enfeoffment? You candidates must have an explanation. Set it out clearly in your essays, so that we may assess your learning for service in the world.

Question: Composition has no fixed form, but the appraisal of writing has definite principles. To appraise the writings of the various masters, one should take the teachings of the Six Classics as the standard of judgment. If writing is not rooted in the Six Classics, its phrases may overflow pale-blue silk book bags yet extend no further than descriptions of moonlight and dew; its scrolls may fill pale-yellow silk wrappers yet consist entirely of depictions of wind and clouds. What benefit does such writing bring the world, and what makes it worthy of esteem as literature? Since the Han, Tang, and Song, surely the authors whose names have entered the annals of literature number in the scores and hundreds. There is no time here to enumerate them in detail; let us discuss just a few outstanding examples. Writings such as Worthy and Good (Xianliang) [?] and The King's Mandate (Wangming) are certainly fine; why, then, single out the three policy essays on Heaven and Humanity (Tianren)? Could it be that their words…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
有同於六經之說歟過秦羨新文非不
美也而何獨取於出師之一表豈其說
有合於六經之旨歟捕龍蛇搏虎豹文
章巍然爲一代之山斗不知於六經何
所本歟軋漢周凌晋宋文章凛然爲一
王之法不知於六經何所自歟至若本
論之陳買燈之疏待漏院六經閣之記
文皆醇正典雅抑不知果於六經之言
有所符合歟諸士子游歌學宫以經爲
===
業者也其於諸子之文品題有日不知
操觚染翰之間果以何人爲可效法歟
幸明以告我
問今天下治平所事乎兵者夷狄盜賊而
已夷狄未服
當宁留意而士大夫講之亦詳惟盜賊竊發
非躬履其地而目擊其事者多以爲不
足恤禁過之策踈消弭之方欽委大患
於不言甚可慮也他未暇論姑舉江西
punctuated:
有同於六經之說歟？過秦、羨新，文非不美也，而何獨取於出師之一表？豈其說有合於六經之旨歟？捕龍蛇，搏虎豹，文章巍然爲一代之山斗，不知於六經何所本歟？軋漢周，凌晋宋，文章凛然爲一王之法，不知於六經何所自歟？至若本論之陳、買燈之疏、待漏院、六經閣之記，文皆醇正典雅，抑不知果於六經之言有所符合歟？諸士子游歌學宫，以經爲業者也，其於諸子之文，品題有日，不知操觚染翰之間，果以何人爲可效法歟？幸明以告我。
問：今天下治平，所事乎兵者，夷狄盜賊而已。夷狄未服，當宁留意，而士大夫講之亦詳。惟盜賊竊發，非躬履其地而目擊其事者，多以爲不足恤。禁過之策踈，消弭之方欽，委大患於不言，甚可慮也。他未暇論，姑舉江西
translation_en:
…accord with the teachings of the Six Classics? The compositions On the Faults of Qin and Admiring the Xin [?] are certainly fine; why, then, single out the Memorial on Dispatching the Army? Is it because its arguments accord with the purport of the Six Classics? Capturing dragons and serpents, grappling with tigers and leopards—such writing towers as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of an age; yet upon what in the Six Classics is it founded? Surpassing Han and Zhou, rising above Jin and Song—such writing stands august as a model for a sovereign’s rule; yet from what in the Six Classics does it derive? As for the arguments set forth in Discourse on Fundamentals, the memorial on purchasing lanterns, and the accounts of the Court for Awaiting the Water Clock and the Pavilion of the Six Classics, their writing is uniformly pure, correct, dignified, and elegant. Yet do they truly accord with the words of the Six Classics? You candidates study and sing in the schools, taking the Classics as your vocation. You have long been appraising the writings of these various authors. When you take up your writing tablets and dip your brushes in ink, whom do you actually consider worthy of emulation? Kindly explain this clearly to me.
Question: Today the realm is peaceful and well governed. The only matters requiring military action concern foreign peoples and bandits. The foreign peoples have not yet submitted: His Majesty attends to this, and scholar-officials have also discussed it in detail. But when bandits rise unexpectedly, those who have not personally visited the places concerned and witnessed events mostly consider them unworthy of concern. Plans for preventing offenses are lax, and methods for quelling disturbances are deficient [?]. To leave a great danger unspoken of is deeply troubling. There is no time to discuss other matters; let us take up, for now, Jiangxi …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之患與諸士子商確之贛州南安地達
閩廣三省之民蓋雜居焉賊發欲捕不
逃之閩則逃之廣而其發於彼也亦然
是以嘯聚山林卒難撲滅不知將何術
以處之瑞州臨江地接湖廣二府之盜
蓋屢發焉緝捕稍急則逃之湖廣緩則
復來是以騷擾良民靡有寧歲不知用
何道以遏之古人治盜如龔遂在渤海
虞詡在朝歌張詠在蜀卓乎不可及矣
===
又有村樓置鼓與新鄭義營之法令賊
自相糾告以其資產賞之與出庫錢以
賞告捕之法不知何者為最善歟尚可
行之於今歟抑別有長策歟諸士子生
長於斯又切鄉井之慮其必講之熟矣
試為我言之將轉告于司兵計者
punctuated: 之患，與諸士子商確之。贛州、南安地達閩廣，三省之民蓋雜居焉。賊發欲捕，不逃之閩，則逃之廣；而其發於彼也亦然。是以嘯聚山林，卒難撲滅。不知將何術以處之？瑞州、臨江地接湖廣，二府之盜蓋屢發焉。緝捕稍急，則逃之湖廣；緩則復來。是以騷擾良民，靡有寧歲。不知用何道以遏之？古人治盜，如龔遂在渤海、虞詡在朝歌、張詠在蜀，卓乎不可及矣。又有村樓置鼓與新鄭義營之法，令賊自相糾告、以其資產賞之，與出庫錢以賞告捕之法。不知何者為最善歟？尚可行之於今歟？抑別有長策歟？諸士子生長於斯，又切鄉井之慮，其必講之熟矣。試為我言之，將轉告于司兵計者。
translation_en: …the troubles there, and discuss them with you candidates to reach a considered judgment. Ganzhou and Nan’an have routes leading into Fujian and Guangdong, and people of the three provinces live intermingled there. When bandits rise and attempts are made to capture them, they flee either to Fujian or to Guangdong; the same happens when they rise in those provinces. Thus they gather in bands in the mountains and forests and are ultimately difficult to eradicate. By what means might this be dealt with? Ruizhou and Linjiang adjoin Huguang, and bandit outbreaks have repeatedly occurred in these two prefectures. When pursuit becomes somewhat pressing, the bandits flee to Huguang; when it slackens, they return. Thus they harass the law-abiding inhabitants, leaving no year of peace. By what means might they be checked? Among men of antiquity who dealt with banditry, Gong Sui in Bohai, Yu Xu in Chaoge, and Zhang Yong in Shu were outstanding beyond compare. There are also the methods of placing drums in village towers and establishing volunteer militia camps at Xinzheng [?], of having bandits denounce one another and rewarding informants with their property, and of disbursing treasury funds to reward those who report or capture bandits. Which of these is best? Can they still be put into practice today? Or is there some other effective long-term policy? You candidates were born and raised here and are deeply concerned for your native communities; surely you have discussed these matters thoroughly. Set out your views for me, and I shall convey them to those responsible for military planning.

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said of the Shao music: “It is perfectly beautiful, and also perfectly good.”

Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “All seven essays in this examination script excel in both expression and reasoning, while the essay on the Analects is particularly sound and elegant. Moreover, its concluding words range through the various Classics, amply demonstrating broad learning. Surely this candidate stands foremost among the many scholars!”

Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The essay portrays the atmosphere of music-making at Shun’s court so vividly that it seems before our eyes. Only someone who has grasped the significance of the Master’s forgetting the taste of food while in Qi could accomplish this. Who but you could rank first among the candidates assigned to this examining room?”

Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the expression fluent. Essays on the Analects like this one are rare indeed. It should be recorded as a model.”

Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “Candidates are quite capable of elaborating on ‘perfectly beautiful,’ but when they reach ‘perfectly good,’ they often become constrained and awkward. This essay alone stands apart from the others; hence it is recorded here.”

Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.”

Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: “Its exposition of perfect goodness and perfect beauty is excellent indeed.”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
斯哉門人記吾夫子之論韶樂如此其意蓋謂
帝王之道莫大於樂帝王之樂莫備於韶惟夫
帝舜紹堯以致治恭己而無爲厥功懋矣韶之
作所以象功也蓋以風動之休而播之於聲音
以績熙之美而形之於干羽故九德之歌迭奏
于堂之上下洋洋乎其盈耳九韶之舞屢舞於
階之東西秩秩乎其有章以詠也以間也自一
成至於九成而清濁高下之不紊再始也復亂
也自一變至於九變而綴兆疾徐之可觀其盡
===
美也何如然不獨盡美而又盡善焉惟夫帝舜
性本於天全位由於帝禪厥德懋矣韶之作所
以昭德也蓋以渾全之性而爲之根柢以揖遜
之風而爲之胚胎故九歌之播非特其聲美而
美之實者殆無罅隙之可議九舞之形非特其
容盛而盛之實者殊無疵纇之可指非矯揉非
造作而聲容之作止一從容乎和順之天無發
揚無蹈厲而歌舞之始終一優游乎平淡之境
其盡善也又何如吁盡美者樂之文也盡善者
punctuated: 斯哉？門人記吾夫子之論韶樂如此，其意蓋謂：帝王之道莫大於樂，帝王之樂莫備於韶。惟夫帝舜紹堯以致治，恭己而無爲，厥功懋矣。韶之作，所以象功也。蓋以風動之休而播之於聲音，以績熙之美而形之於干羽。故九德之歌迭奏于堂之上下，洋洋乎其盈耳；九韶之舞屢舞於階之東西，秩秩乎其有章。以詠也，以間也，自一成至於九成，而清濁高下之不紊；再始也，復亂也，自一變至於九變，而綴兆疾徐之可觀。其盡美也何如？然不獨盡美，而又盡善焉。惟夫帝舜性本於天全，位由於帝禪，厥德懋矣。韶之作，所以昭德也。蓋以渾全之性而爲之根柢，以揖遜之風而爲之胚胎。故九歌之播，非特其聲美，而美之實者殆無罅隙之可議；九舞之形，非特其容盛，而盛之實者殊無疵纇之可指。非矯揉，非造作，而聲容之作止，一從容乎和順之天；無發揚，無蹈厲，而歌舞之始終，一優游乎平淡之境。其盡善也又何如？吁！盡美者，樂之文也；盡善者，
translation_en:
…such a level? Thus the disciples recorded our Master's discussion of the Shao music. His meaning was surely this: nothing in the Way of emperors and kings is greater than music, and no imperial or royal music is more complete than the Shao. Emperor Shun succeeded Yao and brought about good government; holding himself reverently, he governed without deliberate action. Great indeed were his achievements! The Shao was composed to represent those achievements. The blessings of his transforming influence were disseminated through its sounds, and the beauty of his glorious accomplishments was embodied in dances with shields and feathers. Thus songs of the nine virtues were performed in succession above and below the hall, their abundant sound filling the ears; the dances of the ninefold Shao were repeatedly performed east and west of the steps, their orderly movements displaying clear patterns. With singing and instrumental interludes, from the first completed movement to the ninth, the clear and deep, high and low tones remained in order. With renewed beginnings and concluding passages, from the first change to the ninth, the dancers' positions and formations, their quick and slow movements, offered a spectacle to behold. How consummate was its beauty!

Yet it was not only consummately beautiful; it was also consummately good. Emperor Shun's nature was endowed with Heaven's completeness, and his throne came to him through the emperor's abdication. Great indeed was his virtue! The Shao was composed to manifest that virtue. It took his wholly perfect nature as its foundation and the spirit of courteous yielding as the source from which it developed. Thus, when the nine songs were performed, it was not merely their sound that was beautiful: the substance underlying that beauty left virtually no gap open to criticism. When the nine dances took shape, it was not merely their appearance that was magnificent: the substance underlying that magnificence left no blemish to be pointed out. Without forced shaping or contrivance, the sounds and movements, in their beginnings and pauses, were entirely at ease within Heaven-given harmony and compliance. Without exuberant displays or martial stamping, the songs and dances, from beginning to end, moved freely within a realm of serenity and simplicity. How consummate, too, was its goodness! Ah! Consummate beauty is the outward form of music; consummate goodness is…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
樂之情也情文兼備此舜之樂所以為大備之
樂冠百王而獨盛也歟抑夫子稱舜之樂不特
此也他日在齊聞韶又曰不圖為樂之至於斯
至答顏子為邦之問亦曰樂則韶舞而季札聘
魯見舞韶箾者亦曰德至矣盡矣盡矣如天地之無
不覆載雖甚盛德蔑以加矣夫韶信非大舜不
能作非吾夫子之聖季札之賢亦不能知也彼
端冕而聽古樂則惟恐卧者何足以語此
能盡其性則能盡人之性能盡人之性則
能盡物之性
===
同考試官訓導郭　批　此章發明天道先儒論之
詳矣然盡人盡物處作者欲言而文不逮盖性學之
難言如此理明而詞不費者僅見此篇
同考試官訓導胡　批　中庸題作者多為盡人物
之性處窘束難講此篇通貫條暢盖從容於理路之
中者健美健美
同考試官教諭范　批　認理親切遣詞明順其亦
punctuated:
樂之情也。情文兼備，此舜之樂所以為大備之樂，冠百王而獨盛也歟！抑夫子稱舜之樂，不特此也。他日在齊聞韶，又曰：「不圖為樂之至於斯。」至答顏子為邦之問，亦曰：「樂則韶舞。」而季札聘魯，見舞韶箾者，亦曰：「德至矣！盡矣，盡矣！如天地之無不覆載，雖甚盛德，蔑以加矣。」夫韶信非大舜不能作，非吾夫子之聖、季札之賢，亦不能知也。彼端冕而聽古樂，則惟恐卧者，何足以語此？
能盡其性，則能盡人之性；能盡人之性，則能盡物之性。
同考試官訓導郭，批：此章發明天道，先儒論之詳矣。然盡人盡物處，作者欲言而文不逮，盖性學之難言如此。理明而詞不費者，僅見此篇。
同考試官訓導胡，批：中庸題，作者多為盡人物之性處窘束難講。此篇通貫條暢，盖從容於理路之中者。健美，健美！
同考試官教諭范，批：認理親切，遣詞明順，其亦
translation_en:
…the inner substance of music. With both inner substance and outward refinement fully present, was this not why Shun’s music was supremely complete, surpassing that of all other kings in its singular excellence? Yet the Master’s praise of Shun’s music was not confined to this. On another occasion, when he heard the Shao music in Qi, he said, “I never imagined that music could reach such heights.” When answering Yanzi’s question about governing a state, he likewise said, “For music, use the Shao dance.” And when Ji Zha visited Lu on a diplomatic mission and saw the Shao-xiao dance performed, he too said, “Virtue has reached its utmost! Complete indeed, complete indeed! Like Heaven and Earth, which leave nothing uncovered or unsupported—even the most flourishing virtue could add nothing to this.” Truly, none but the great Shun could have composed the Shao; nor could anyone without our Master’s sagehood or Ji Zha’s worthiness have understood it. As for the man who, listening to ancient music in ceremonial robes and cap, feared only that he would fall asleep—how could one discuss this with him?
“Being able fully to realize his own nature, he can fully realize the nature of others; being able fully to realize the nature of others, he can fully realize the nature of things.”
Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: This chapter elucidates the Way of Heaven, which earlier Confucian scholars have discussed in detail. Yet when writers reach the full realization of the nature of others and of things, their prose fails to convey what they wish to say. Such is the difficulty of expressing the learning concerning human nature. Only in this essay have I seen the principles made clear without wasting words.
Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: In writing on topics from the Doctrine of the Mean, authors are often constrained by the passages on fully realizing the nature of people and things and find them difficult to explain. This essay connects everything throughout and develops its argument fluently and coherently: its author evidently moves at ease through the reasoning. Vigorous and elegant, vigorous and elegant!
Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: His grasp of principle is intimate and precise, and his wording clear and fluent. Might he also be one who…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
嘗留心於性學者歟
考試官教諭范　批〔性理文字貴典實此作得之〕
考試官教授田　批〔說盡性處得章句意〕
能全一己之固有斯全一世之同有天下至誠
然也蓋性者一己之固有而一世人物之所同
也至誠能盡其性則人物之性豈有不能盡之
者哉中庸二十二章子思子發明天道至此蓋
謂人之性有不能盡者良由己之德有未能實
也惟夫天下之至誠德無不實故虛靈之府私
===
欲不留而天之命於我者察之有以極其詳神
明之舍物欲不染而我之所以賦於天者由之
有以至於熟若巨若細全之而無毫髮之或遺
曰精曰粗體之而無纖芥之少歉可謂能盡其
性矣夫人物之性亦我之性但以所賦形氣不
同而有異耳既能盡己之性則於人之性必知
之無不明而處之無不當大過者抑之不及者
引之勞來匡直而俾遠近之各得其頤品節曲
成而使小大之各全其天必至於黎民於變時
punctuated:
嘗留心於性學者歟？
考試官教諭范批〔性理文字貴典實，此作得之。〕
考試官教授田批〔說盡性處得章句意。〕
能全一己之固有，斯全一世之同有，天下至誠然也。蓋性者，一己之固有，而一世人物之所同也。至誠能盡其性，則人物之性豈有不能盡之者哉？《中庸》二十二章，子思子發明天道至此，蓋謂人之性有不能盡者，良由己之德有未能實也。惟夫天下之至誠，德無不實，故虛靈之府，私欲不留，而天之命於我者，察之有以極其詳；神明之舍，物欲不染，而我之所以賦於天者，由之有以至於熟。若巨若細，全之而無毫髮之或遺；曰精曰粗，體之而無纖芥之少歉，可謂能盡其性矣。夫人物之性，亦我之性，但以所賦形氣不同而有異耳。既能盡己之性，則於人之性，必知之無不明，而處之無不當。大過者抑之，不及者引之，勞來匡直，而俾遠近之各得其頤；品節曲成，而使小大之各全其天。必至於黎民於變時
translation_en:
…someone who has devoted attention to the study of human nature?
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔Writing on human nature and principle should be grounded in the classics and substantial in content. This composition achieves that.〕
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔Its explanation of fully realizing one’s nature captures the meaning of the Commentary in Chapters and Sentences.〕
To bring to completeness what is inherently possessed by oneself is thereby to bring to completeness what is shared by all in the world. This is true of one who possesses the utmost sincerity under Heaven. For nature is inherent in oneself and shared by all people and things in the world. If one of utmost sincerity can fully realize his own nature, how could he fail to realize fully the natures of other people and things?
In chapter twenty-two of the Doctrine of the Mean, Master Zisi elucidates the Way of Heaven to this point. His meaning is that people’s failure to realize their nature fully truly stems from their own virtue not yet being entirely genuine. Only one of utmost sincerity under Heaven has virtue that is genuine in every respect. Thus, in the seat of his empty and numinous awareness, selfish desires do not linger, and he examines what Heaven has ordained for him in the fullest detail. In the dwelling of his spiritual intelligence, material desires leave no stain, and he follows what he has received as his endowment from Heaven until his practice becomes thoroughly mature. Whether great or small, he brings it all to completeness, omitting not so much as a hair’s breadth; whether refined or coarse, he embodies it all, without the slightest deficiency. He may indeed be said to realize his nature fully.
The natures of other people and things are also my own nature; their differences arise only from differences in the bodily forms and vital energies with which they are endowed. Having fully realized his own nature, he must understand the natures of others with complete clarity and deal with them with complete propriety. Those who go too far he restrains; those who fall short he guides forward. He encourages and comforts them, corrects and rectifies them, so that those near and far each receive their nourishment. He regulates them appropriately and brings them to fulfillment in accordance with their particular circumstances, so that the small and the great each fully preserve their Heaven-endowed nature. He must reach the point at which “the common people are transformed, and thus…”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
盡己人之性有不能盡乎既能盡人之性
則於物之性必知之無不明而處之無不當所
欲者順之所惡者遠之材質有不同也因其材
質之宜以致其用取用有不一也制其取用之
節以遂其生必至於鳥獸魚鱉咸若而後已物
之性有不能盡乎吁盡一己之性因而盡一世
人物之性聖人至誠之功用如此子思子以是
發明天道其旨不既深乎抑此乃自誠而明者
之事也推而至於贊化育者此也參天地者此
===
也至誠之功用備矣聖人之能事畢矣下此則
流於管子功利之學則以功利迷其心而不能
盡己之性也流於揚氏爲我之學則以爲我汨
其見而不能盡人物之性也噫若人不過塊然
於天地之間而已何足以收參贊之功抑何足
以語誠明之事
賢者在位能者在職
同考試官訓導陳　批　〔題本冠冕但作者不泛則拘〕
punctuated:
盡己，人之性有不能盡乎？既能盡人之性，則於物之性必知之無不明，而處之無不當。所欲者順之，所惡者遠之。材質有不同也，因其材質之宜以致其用；取用有不一也，制其取用之節以遂其生。必至於鳥獸魚鱉咸若而後已，物之性有不能盡乎？吁！盡一己之性，因而盡一世人物之性，聖人至誠之功用如此。子思子以是發明天道，其旨不既深乎？抑此乃自誠而明者之事也。推而至於贊化育者，此也；參天地者，此也。至誠之功用備矣，聖人之能事畢矣。下此，則流於管子功利之學，則以功利迷其心，而不能盡己之性也；流於揚氏爲我之學，則以爲我汨其見，而不能盡人物之性也。噫！若人不過塊然於天地之間而已，何足以收參贊之功？抑何足以語誠明之事？

賢者在位，能者在職。

同考試官訓導陳，批：〔題本冠冕，但作者不泛則拘。〕
translation_en:
…fully realize oneself [?]. Could the natures of other people then remain unrealized? Once one can fully realize human nature, one must understand the natures of things with complete clarity and deal with them with complete propriety. One accommodates what they desire and keeps away what they dislike. Their material qualities differ: one brings their usefulness to fruition in accordance with what suits those qualities. The ways of taking and using them vary: one regulates their use so that they may fulfill their lives. Only when birds, beasts, fish, and turtles all flourish in accordance with their natures does one stop. Could the natures of things then remain unrealized? Ah! Fully realizing one’s own nature and thereby fully realizing the natures of all people and things in the world—such is the efficacy of the sage’s utmost sincerity. Master Zisi uses this to elucidate the Way of Heaven. Is his meaning not profound? Yet this is the work of one who proceeds from sincerity to understanding. Extended further, this is what assists the transforming and nourishing processes; this is what enables one to form a triad with Heaven and Earth. The efficacy of utmost sincerity is complete, and all that the sage can accomplish is fulfilled. Below this level, one slips into Guanzi’s learning of achievement and profit: achievement and profit bewilder the mind, preventing one from fully realizing one’s own nature. Or one slips into Yang’s learning of acting for oneself: self-interest confounds one’s perceptions, preventing one from fully realizing the natures of people and things. Alas! Such a person merely exists like an inert clod between Heaven and Earth. How could he achieve the work of forming a triad with them and assisting their transforming processes? How could he even discuss sincerity and understanding?

“The worthy occupy positions of authority; the capable hold offices.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently dignified, but those who write on it are either diffuse or constrained.〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
此篇獨能寫出孟子勉進時君彊仁之意殆無餘蘊矣其
傑作也宜錄以式後學
考試官教諭范　批　措詞蒼古筆力老健其積
學之士歟
考試官教授田　批　得孟子意思
有德者任之重有才者任之專此彊仁之事也
甚矣位重而職專也有德者可不任之重而有
才者可不任之專乎此孟子因時君惡辱之情
而進之以彊仁之事也想其意謂夫賢能之有
===
益於人國家也尚矣人君之欲彊仁者可不從
事於斯耶彼有人焉釀仁蓄義而德量之深沉
執禮秉智而德望之隆重可謂賢者矣賢而不
使之在位則君無由而正俗無由而善可乎必
也翕受敷施托之以心膂旁招簡拔寄之以股
肱而使賢者之在位如爵級已尊上大夫之位
也階資稍次下大夫之位也俾皆有人以克之
而位不空由是上足以格君之非心而君可正
下足以挽俗之陋習而俗可善矣復有人焉有
punctuated:
此篇獨能寫出孟子勉進時君彊仁之意，殆無餘蘊矣。其傑作也，宜錄以式後學。

考試官教諭范批：措詞蒼古，筆力老健，其積學之士歟！

考試官教授田批：得孟子意思。

有德者任之重，有才者任之專，此彊仁之事也。

甚矣，位重而職專也！有德者可不任之重，而有才者可不任之專乎？此孟子因時君惡辱之情，而進之以彊仁之事也。想其意謂，夫賢能之有益於人國家也尚矣，人君之欲彊仁者，可不從事於斯耶？彼有人焉，釀仁蓄義，而德量之深沉；執禮秉智，而德望之隆重，可謂賢者矣。賢而不使之在位，則君無由而正，俗無由而善，可乎？必也翕受敷施，托之以心膂；旁招簡拔，寄之以股肱。而使賢者之在位，如爵級已尊，上大夫之位也；階資稍次，下大夫之位也。俾皆有人以克之，而位不空。由是，上足以格君之非心，而君可正；下足以挽俗之陋習，而俗可善矣。復有人焉，有
translation_en:
… This essay alone brings out Mencius’s intention to encourage the rulers of his day to strive to practice benevolence, leaving scarcely anything unexpressed. It is a masterly work and should be recorded as a model for later students.

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor in a county Confucian school: The phrasing is vigorous and antique, and the writing mature and robust. Surely its author is a man of accumulated learning!

Comment by Examiner Tian, Instructor in a prefectural Confucian school: It captures Mencius’s meaning.

Those with virtue should be entrusted with weighty responsibilities; those with talent should be entrusted with specialized responsibilities. This is what striving to practice benevolence entails.

How weighty are positions of authority, and how specialized are official duties! Can those with virtue fail to be entrusted with weighty responsibilities, or those with talent with specialized responsibilities? Here Mencius takes the rulers’ aversion to disgrace as his starting point and urges them onward to strive to practice benevolence. We may imagine his meaning thus: the benefits that worthy and capable men bring to a ruler’s state have long been recognized. Can a ruler who wishes to strive to practice benevolence fail to attend to this?

Consider a man who nurtures benevolence and stores up righteousness, whose moral capacity is profound; who holds fast to ritual propriety and maintains wisdom, whose reputation for virtue is exalted. Such a man may be called worthy. If he is worthy but is not placed in a position of authority, the ruler has no means of being set right, and popular customs have no means of improving. Can this be acceptable? Such men must be welcomed and employed, entrusted to serve as the ruler’s heart and backbone; they must be sought far and wide, selected and promoted, relied upon as his arms and legs. Thus worthy men are placed in positions of authority: those whose rank is already exalted occupy the positions of senior grand masters, while those whose standing is somewhat lower occupy the positions of junior grand masters. Let every position have someone capable of fulfilling it, so that none is occupied in vain. In this way, above, they will be able to correct the ruler’s errant mind, and the ruler can be set right; below, they will be able to reform debased popular habits, and customs can be improved. Then there is another man who possesses …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
猷有爲而才名之烜赫善謀善斷而才氣之雄
偉可謂能者矣能而不使之在職則政無自而
脩事無自而立可乎必也因能授任不私於愁
惡隨才器使不求其全備而使能者之在職如
辨上下而和神人典禮樂之職也治軍旅而明
法律司兵刑之職也俾皆有人以任之而職不
曠由是大足以致八政之齊而政可脩細足以
致庶事之康而事可立矣吁賢者之在位則有
德者任之不可謂不重能者之在職則有才者
===
任之不可謂不專人君惡辱而彊仁之事尚何
以加於此哉大抵賢能國家之楨榦非特國君
用之可以安富尊榮而已君天下者能用之則
沛德澤於當時垂休光於後世而真足以媲美
於唐虞三代之君矣荀子曰明主尚賢使能而
饗其盛正此意也然則孟子之言雖以曉當時
之君而實爲後世君天下者發也有志於圖治
者尚致於斯
易
punctuated:
猷有爲，而才名之烜赫；善謀善斷，而才氣之雄偉，可謂能者矣。能而不使之在職，則政無自而脩，事無自而立，可乎？必也因能授任，不私於愁惡；隨才器使，不求其全備。而使能者之在職，如辨上下而和神人，典禮樂之職也；治軍旅而明法律，司兵刑之職也。俾皆有人以任之，而職不曠。由是，大足以致八政之齊，而政可脩；細足以致庶事之康，而事可立矣。吁！賢者之在位，則有德者任之，不可謂不重；能者之在職，則有才者任之，不可謂不專。人君惡辱而彊仁之事，尚何以加於此哉？大抵賢能，國家之楨榦，非特國君用之可以安富尊榮而已。君天下者能用之，則沛德澤於當時，垂休光於後世，而真足以媲美於唐虞三代之君矣。荀子曰：「明主尚賢使能而饗其盛。」正此意也。然則孟子之言，雖以曉當時之君，而實爲後世君天下者發也。有志於圖治者，尚致於斯。

易
translation_en:
…possessing plans and accomplishments, with a brilliant reputation for talent; skilled in deliberation and decision, with imposing ability and spirit—such men may be called capable. If capable men are not given official duties, government will have no means of being put in order, and undertakings no means of being accomplished. Can this be acceptable? One must assign responsibilities according to ability, without allowing personal aversion [?] to cause partiality; employ men according to their particular talents, without demanding that they possess every excellence. Thus capable men should hold the appropriate offices: distinguishing superior from inferior and bringing spirits and men into harmony are the duties of those administering rites and music; directing armies and making laws clear are the duties of those responsible for military affairs and punishments. Let every office have someone to discharge its responsibilities, so that no duties are neglected. In this way, on the larger scale, the eight branches of government can be brought into order and administration perfected; in particulars, the many affairs can proceed smoothly and undertakings be accomplished.

Ah! When the worthy occupy positions, men of virtue fill them: one cannot say that their responsibilities lack weight. When the capable hold office, men of talent discharge its duties: one cannot say that their responsibilities are insufficiently focused. If a ruler abhors disgrace and strives to practice benevolence, what could he do beyond this? In general, the worthy and capable are the pillars of the state. Employing them does more than enable a ruler to enjoy security, wealth, honor, and glory. If one who rules all under Heaven can employ them, he will shower the blessings of his virtue upon his own age and leave a splendid legacy to later generations. He will truly be able to rival the rulers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties. Xunzi said: “An enlightened ruler honors the worthy, employs the capable, and enjoys the flourishing that results.” This is precisely the meaning. Thus, although Mengzi’s words were intended to enlighten the rulers of his day, they were really uttered for those who would rule all under Heaven in later ages. May those intent upon achieving good government devote their efforts to this.

Book of Changes

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
以祉元吉中以行願也
同考試官訓導郭　批〔中以行願處作者多體認不明此篇獨能融會傳義發揮詳盡蓋深於易者〕
同考試官訓導胡　批〔如此作則二五同德之義始明學易至此可與論精微之旨矣〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔體認明白宜錄之以爲學易者法〕
考試官教諭范　批〔易義正如此作〕
考試官教授田　批〔得旨〕
===
論主泰而致福之盛由虛已而下賢之誠夫五
以柔中而應九二之剛中是能虛已而以下賢
爲願者也中以行願其以祉元吉也不亦宜哉
周公繫泰六五之辭曰帝乙歸妹以祉元吉吾
夫子小象舉以祉元吉之辭而申爲中以行願
之義意謂凡物之盛則有將衰之理故泰之日
常有否來之憂今五曰以祉元吉則是有以承
天休於上下既協之餘而吉无不利不至警城
punctuated:
以祉元吉，中以行願也。

同考試官訓導郭，批〔中以行願處，作者多體認不明。此篇獨能融會傳義，發揮詳盡，蓋深於易者。〕
同考試官訓導胡，批〔如此作，則二五同德之義始明。學易至此，可與論精微之旨矣。〕
同考試官教諭范，批〔體認明白，宜錄之以爲學易者法。〕
考試官教諭范，批〔易義正如此作。〕
考試官教授田，批〔得旨。〕

論主泰而致福之盛，由虛已而下賢之誠。夫五以柔中而應九二之剛中，是能虛已而以下賢爲願者也。中以行願，其以祉元吉也，不亦宜哉？周公繫泰六五之辭曰：「帝乙歸妹，以祉元吉。」吾夫子小象舉「以祉元吉」之辭，而申爲「中以行願」之義。意謂凡物之盛，則有將衰之理，故泰之日常有否來之憂。今五曰「以祉元吉」，則是有以承天休於上下既協之餘，而吉无不利，不至警城
translation_en:
“Thereby blessed: supremely auspicious”—through centrality, he carries out his wish.

Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Most writers fail to grasp clearly the passage “through centrality, he carries out his wish.” This essay alone integrates the meanings of the commentaries and develops them fully and thoroughly. Its author surely has a profound understanding of the Book of Changes.〕
Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Only with an essay written in this way does the meaning of the second and fifth lines sharing the same virtue become clear. With someone whose study of the Book of Changes has reached this level, one may discuss its subtle and profound purport.〕
Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔Its understanding is clear. It should be recorded as a model for students of the Book of Changes.〕
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔An exposition of the meaning of the Book of Changes should be written precisely in this way.〕
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔It captures the purport.〕

The argument is that presiding over Peace and bringing blessings to their fullness depend upon sincerely setting oneself aside and humbling oneself before the worthy. The fifth line, yielding and central, responds to the firm centrality of the nine in the second place. Thus it represents one who can set himself aside and make deference to the worthy his wish. Through centrality he carries out this wish: is it not fitting that he should thereby be blessed and enjoy supreme auspiciousness? The Duke of Zhou appended these words to the six in the fifth place of Peace (Tai): “Di Yi gives the maiden in marriage. Thereby blessed: supremely auspicious.” In the Lesser Image Commentary, our Master Confucius cites the words “thereby blessed: supremely auspicious” and expands upon them with the meaning “through centrality, he carries out his wish.” His meaning is that whenever things reach their fullness, there is a principle by which they are about to decline. Thus, in times of Peace, there is always concern that Obstruction (Pi) will come. Now, when the fifth line says “thereby blessed: supremely auspicious,” this means that, once those above and below are in harmony, there is a means of receiving Heaven’s favor, with auspiciousness and nothing unfavorable, without reaching the warning concerning the city wall…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
復于隍矣有以享天祿於四方無虞之際而永
保終吉不至於初吉終亂矣五能保有其泰如
此是果何修何爲而得此哉亦惟中以行願而
已蓋五以柔遜之德而居上卦之中是有虛已
之義二有剛中之德而五與之相應是有下賢
之義殆必君臣同德臣有善君舍已而從之而
其從之也一本於吾心之所欲上下合志下有
能上虛心而用之而其用之道一出於吾心之
所願任之以包荒任之以用憑河君之所以任
===
其臣者專矣使或非其所欲能任之弗替如此
乎信之以朋亡信之以不遐遺上之所以信其
下者篤矣設或非其所願能信之弗疑如此乎
夫能中以行願則泰可以長保其以祉元吉亦
必然之理也不然則有所謂賢人在下位而輔
者矣泰其有不轉而之否者哉抑虛已下賢之
義豈唯此爻之象有之吾觀泰之爲卦乾下坤
上固自含此義也故曰上下交而其志同在昔
堯舜三王所以孳孳於明揚汲汲於咨諏以共
punctuated: 復于隍矣，有以享天祿於四方無虞之際，而永保終吉，不至於初吉終亂矣。五能保有其泰如此，是果何修何爲而得此哉？亦惟中以行願而已。蓋五以柔遜之德而居上卦之中，是有虛已之義；二有剛中之德，而五與之相應，是有下賢之義。殆必君臣同德，臣有善，君舍已而從之，而其從之也，一本於吾心之所欲；上下合志，下有能，上虛心而用之，而其用之道，一出於吾心之所願。任之以包荒，任之以用憑河，君之所以任其臣者專矣。使或非其所欲，能任之弗替如此乎？信之以朋亡，信之以不遐遺，上之所以信其下者篤矣。設或非其所願，能信之弗疑如此乎？夫能中以行願，則泰可以長保，其以祉元吉，亦必然之理也。不然，則有所謂賢人在下位而輔者矣，泰其有不轉而之否者哉？抑虛已下賢之義，豈唯此爻之象有之？吾觀泰之爲卦，乾下坤上，固自含此義也。故曰：「上下交而其志同。」在昔堯舜三王所以孳孳於明揚、汲汲於咨諏，以共
translation_en:
…falling back into the moat. He can enjoy Heaven’s bounty when the four quarters are free from trouble and preserve good fortune to the end, without an auspicious beginning ending in disorder. How, then, does the fifth line cultivate itself and act so as to preserve its peace in this way? It does so simply by “carrying out its wishes through centrality.” For the fifth line, possessing the virtue of yielding humility and occupying the central position in the upper trigram, embodies setting oneself aside. The second line possesses the virtue of strength and centrality, and the fifth responds to it: this embodies humbling oneself before the worthy.

Surely ruler and minister must share the same virtue. When the minister has something good to offer, the ruler sets himself aside and follows it; his following it is rooted entirely in what his own heart desires. Superior and subordinate unite their purposes. When those below possess ability, the one above employs them with an open mind; the way he employs them proceeds entirely from what his own heart wishes. He entrusts his minister with “embracing the uncultivated” and “using those who would ford the river on foot”: the ruler’s reliance on his minister is undivided. If this were not what he desired, could he rely on him so unswervingly? He trusts him to “forsake factions” and “not neglect the distant”: the superior’s trust in his subordinate is profound. If this were not what he wished, could he trust him so unquestioningly?

If he can carry out his wishes through centrality, peace can be preserved for long; that he thereby obtains “blessings and supreme good fortune” is likewise a necessary principle. Otherwise, there would be what is called “a worthy man in a subordinate position who assists” [?]. Could peace then fail to turn into obstruction? Yet is this principle of setting oneself aside and humbling oneself before the worthy found only in the image of this line? I observe that the hexagram Peace (Tai), with Qian below and Kun above, inherently contains this meaning. Thus it says: “Those above and below interact, and their purposes are the same.” In antiquity, Yao, Shun, and the Three Kings worked tirelessly to bring worthy men to prominence and urgently sought counsel, so as jointly to…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
成雍熙泰和之治者用此義耳由百世之後等
百世之王得此義則治失此義則亂斷斷乎莫
之能違也嗚呼聖人傳易片言之間而其旨如
此然則易何止性命之源其亦治亂之龜鑑也
夫
見乃謂之象形乃謂之器制而用之謂之
法利用出入民咸用之謂之神

===

同考試官教諭范　批〔有定見無冗詞非泛然說易〕〔易者錄之以一衆論〕
〔者比故錄之〕
考試官教諭范　批〔潔爭精微之旨此作得之〕
考試官教授田　批〔易義精潔〕
造化有生物之序聖人有成物之功大傳之義
punctuated:
成雍熙泰和之治者，用此義耳。由百世之後，等百世之王，得此義則治，失此義則亂，斷斷乎莫之能違也。嗚呼！聖人傳易，片言之間，而其旨如此。然則易何止性命之源，其亦治亂之龜鑑也夫！
見乃謂之象，形乃謂之器，制而用之謂之法，利用出入，民咸用之謂之神。

造化有生物之序，聖人有成物之功，大傳之義
translation_en:
…brought about harmonious, prosperous, and peaceful government simply by applying this principle. Looking back from a hundred generations later and judging the kings of a hundred generations, those who grasped this principle achieved order, while those who lost it brought disorder. Most assuredly, none could depart from this rule. Ah! In transmitting the Changes, the sage conveyed such profound meaning in just a few words. Thus the Changes is more than the source of our understanding of human nature and destiny: it is also a mirror by which to judge order and disorder!

“What becomes manifest is called an image; what takes form is called a concrete object. Fashioning it and putting it to use is called a method. Making its use beneficial in going out and coming in, so that all the people use it, is called numinous efficacy.”

Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Writers certainly know that this concerns divination by turtle shell and milfoil, yet they inevitably become entangled in other interpretations and find it difficult to achieve clarity. This essay’s argument is solid and precise, and its language concise.”

Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “To argue in this way is truly to understand that divination is no trivial matter. This certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.”

Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “It presents a definite interpretation without superfluous words; it is unlike a merely general discussion of the Changes … [the annotation is disordered: ‘those who … the Changes, include it to unify the various views’ [?]] … comparable to such writers; therefore it is included.”

Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “This work grasps the purifying [?] and subtle import.”

Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: “Its interpretation of the Changes is precise and concise.”

The creative transformations of Heaven and Earth have their sequence for bringing things into being; the sages have their achievement in bringing things to completion. The meaning of the Great Commentary …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
然也蓋見象形器者生物之序也制之而為法
用之而為神者成物之功也卜筮之作孰非自
然之次第哉大傳此章專言卜筮及此謂夫庶
物之錣並生於天地之間而蓍龜之生獨神於
庶物之表是故自其端倪方動於乾坤變通之
餘胚胎始受於闔闢往來之後斯時也條幹未
具軀殼未凝非若有形之可執者比也其不謂
之象乎迨夫端倪者達而條幹為之畢具胚胎
者實而軀殼為之既凝斯時也大和保合體質
===
完固則非若有象而無形者比矣其不謂之器
乎造化生物之序如此於是聖人者出因蓍有
陰陽老少之數也制為分掛揲扐之法而用之
以筮所以冒天下之道者在是因龜有雨霽蒙
驛克之兆也制為鑽灼之法而用之以卜所以
斷天下之疑者在是此則聖人脩道之所為也
不謂之法而何由是二物者備民之出也用之
以出而咨焉以斷其吉凶有不知誰之所為者
民之入也用之以入而咨焉以決其趨避有莫
punctuated: 然也。蓋見象形器者，生物之序也；制之而為法，用之而為神者，成物之功也。卜筮之作，孰非自然之次第哉？大傳此章專言卜筮，及此謂夫庶物之錣，並生於天地之間，而蓍龜之生，獨神於庶物之表。是故自其端倪方動於乾坤變通之餘，胚胎始受於闔闢往來之後，斯時也，條幹未具，軀殼未凝，非若有形之可執者比也，其不謂之象乎？迨夫端倪者達，而條幹為之畢具；胚胎者實，而軀殼為之既凝。斯時也，大和保合，體質完固，則非若有象而無形者比矣，其不謂之器乎？造化生物之序如此。於是聖人者出，因蓍有陰陽老少之數也，制為分掛揲扐之法，而用之以筮，所以冒天下之道者在是；因龜有雨霽蒙驛克之兆也，制為鑽灼之法，而用之以卜，所以斷天下之疑者在是。此則聖人脩道之所為也，不謂之法而何？由是二物者備，民之出也，用之以出而咨焉，以斷其吉凶，有不知誰之所為者；民之入也，用之以入而咨焉，以決其趨避，有莫
translation_en:
…is indeed so. For the manifestation of images and the formation of concrete objects constitute the sequence by which things are generated; establishing procedures for them and employing them with spiritual efficacy constitute the achievement of bringing things to completion. What part of the creation of turtle-shell and milfoil divination does not follow a natural sequence? This chapter of the Great Commentary deals specifically with these forms of divination. At this point it says that the myriad things [?] all arise between Heaven and Earth, yet milfoil and turtles, in their generation, possess a spiritual efficacy surpassing that of other things. Thus, when their first beginnings stir in the wake of the transformations and interchanges of Qian and Kun, and their embryos first take shape following the closing and opening, coming and going, their branches and stems are not yet complete, and their bodies and shells have not yet solidified. At this stage they cannot be compared to things possessing tangible forms that can be grasped. Should they not be called images? When these beginnings develop, their branches and stems become fully formed; when their embryos mature, their bodies and shells solidify. At this stage, supreme harmony is preserved and united within them, and their physical constitution is complete and firm. They can no longer be compared to things that possess images but lack form. Should they not be called concrete objects? Such is the sequence by which the transforming powers of nature generate things.

Then the sages arose. Because milfoil possesses the numbers of old and young yin and yang, they established procedures for dividing the stalks, setting one aside, counting them off, and placing the remainders between the fingers, and used these for milfoil divination. Herein lay the means of encompassing the Way of all under Heaven. Because turtle shells possess the signs of rain, clearing skies, cloudiness, dispersal [?], and crossing, they established procedures for drilling and scorching them and employed these for turtle-shell divination. Herein lay the means of resolving the doubts of all under Heaven. This is what the sages accomplished in cultivating the Way. What could it be called but a method?

With these two things thus made ready, when the people go out, they use and consult them in going out to determine their good or ill fortune, without knowing who brings this about. When the people come in, they use and consult them in coming in to decide what to pursue and what to avoid, and there is no one …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
知誰之所使者此則百姓自然之日用也不謂
之神而何是法也神也所以成夫象器之利而
全夫造化之功者也非聖人其孰能與於此哉
嗟夫聖人非天地則無以開其先天地非聖人
則無以成其能觸類而長之凡聖人因天地之
所生而制之以利民用者獨著龜乎哉範圍天
地之化而不過曲成萬物而不遺通乎晝夜之
道而知斯言盡之矣信乎易與天地準而聖人
又與天地參者也
===
書
萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣
同考試官訓導陳　批〔敷錫伯禹告君之意殆盡非潛心於壁經者不能是用錄出〕
考試官教諭范　批〔理明詞贍書經義如此作者不多〕
考試官教授田　批〔通暢〕
蓋夫一世之賢願為一人之輔蓋賢者非不欲
punctuated:
知誰之所使者。此則百姓自然之日用也，不謂之神而何？是法也，神也，所以成夫象器之利而全夫造化之功者也。非聖人，其孰能與於此哉？嗟夫！聖人非天地則無以開其先，天地非聖人則無以成其能。觸類而長之，凡聖人因天地之所生而制之以利民用者，獨著龜乎哉？範圍天地之化而不過，曲成萬物而不遺，通乎晝夜之道而知，斯言盡之矣。信乎！《易》與天地準，而聖人又與天地參者也。

書

萬邦黎獻共惟帝臣
