考試官教授田，批〔通暢。〕

蓋夫一世之賢，願為一人之輔。蓋賢者非不欲
translation_en:
…knows at whose prompting this occurs. This is the natural everyday practice of the common people: how could it not be called numinous? These methods and their numinous efficacy bring to fruition the benefits of images and implements and complete the work of creation. Who but the sages could participate in this?

Ah! Without Heaven and Earth, the sages would have nothing to prepare the way for them; without the sages, Heaven and Earth would have no means of fully realizing their capacities. Extending this by analogy, could the things that the sages fashioned from what Heaven and Earth produce, for the benefit of the people's use, be limited to yarrow stalks [?] and tortoise shells? “Encompassing the transformations of Heaven and Earth without exceeding them; bringing the myriad things to completion in all their particulars without omitting any; comprehending the way of day and night and knowing it”—these words say it all. Truly, the Book of Changes accords with Heaven and Earth, and the sages form a triad with Heaven and Earth.

Book of Documents

“The worthy men among the people of the myriad states are all the emperor's subjects.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The intent of Bo Yu in addressing his ruler is expounded [?] almost completely. No one who had not devoted himself deeply to the classic recovered from the wall could accomplish this. It is therefore selected for inclusion.”

Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and the language ample. Few writers produce interpretations of the Book of Documents of this quality.”

Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: “Coherent and fluent.”

The worthy men of an entire age desire to serve as assistants to the One Man, the sovereign. For it is not that worthy men do not wish to…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
仕而亦不苟仕也盡一世之賢而皆欲爲君輔
焉非君德之遠著而能致是哉昔大禹欲舜明
德以化頑讒及此若曰帝德光輝既有以達天
下之大則風聲鼓動自有以感天下之賢彼大
小殊封邦以萬計也其間鍾間氣而挺生於黎
民之中者孰非忠貞之吉士遠近異服邦以萬
言也其間負奇才而超出於群黎之上者孰非
直亮之吉人含英咀實飽吾道於畎畝之中先
明正大其存心也韞玉藏珍養吾德於林泉之
===
下公平正直其制行也是賢也向固以道自樂
若將終身矣今則感帝德於遠被之餘莫不幡
然興起而懷致身之願昔固以德自重若將志
世矣今則挹帝德於清光之下靡不勃然感發
而萌用世之心或願爲帝之股肱也或願爲帝
之耳目也蓋不待弓旌之招皆將效忠國家矣
孰肯自棄於明時哉將以備帝之翼爲也將以
備帝之明聽也蓋不必玉帛之聘皆欲獻直朝
廷矣誰肯自負於明世哉夫以群賢嚮用之同
punctuated:
仕，而亦不苟仕也。盡一世之賢而皆欲爲君輔焉，非君德之遠著而能致是哉？昔大禹欲舜明德以化頑讒，及此若曰：帝德光輝，既有以達天下之大，則風聲鼓動，自有以感天下之賢。彼大小殊封，邦以萬計也，其間鍾間氣而挺生於黎民之中者，孰非忠貞之吉士？遠近異服，邦以萬言也，其間負奇才而超出於群黎之上者，孰非直亮之吉人？含英咀實，飽吾道於畎畝之中，先明正大，其存心也；韞玉藏珍，養吾德於林泉之下，公平正直，其制行也。
是賢也，向固以道自樂，若將終身矣。今則感帝德於遠被之餘，莫不幡然興起，而懷致身之願。昔固以德自重，若將志世矣。今則挹帝德於清光之下，靡不勃然感發，而萌用世之心。或願爲帝之股肱也，或願爲帝之耳目也。蓋不待弓旌之招，皆將效忠國家矣，孰肯自棄於明時哉？將以備帝之翼爲也，將以備帝之明聽也。蓋不必玉帛之聘，皆欲獻直朝廷矣，誰肯自負於明世哉？夫以群賢嚮用之同
translation_en:
…to serve in office, yet neither will they take office indiscriminately. If all the worthy men of an age wish to assist their ruler, could this come about unless the ruler’s virtue were renowned far and wide? Long ago, Yu the Great wished Shun to make his virtue manifest so as to transform the obstinate and the slanderous. Reaching this point, he spoke as though to say: Once the radiance of the emperor’s virtue reaches throughout the vast realm, its stirring influence will naturally move the worthy men of the world. The domains differ in size, and their states number in the tens of thousands. Among them, those endowed with the exceptional vital energies of Heaven and Earth, who emerge outstanding from among the common people—are they not all loyal and steadfast gentlemen? Near and far, the zones of service differ, and their states are counted by the tens of thousands. Among them, those possessing extraordinary talents, who rise above the multitude—are they not all upright and trustworthy men? Savoring the blossoms and chewing the fruits of learning, they nourish themselves fully on our Way amid the fields; clarity and upright greatness [?] characterize the intentions they cherish. Concealing their jade and storing away their treasures, they nurture their virtue amid woods and streams; fairness, impartiality, integrity, and rectitude govern their conduct.
These worthy men formerly delighted in the Way, as though they would spend their whole lives thus. Now, moved by the far-reaching influence of the emperor’s virtue, every one of them rises with renewed purpose and cherishes the wish to devote himself to service. Formerly they prized their own virtue, as though intending to set their minds upon the world [?]. Now, receiving the emperor’s virtue beneath its pure radiance, every one of them is deeply stirred and begins to think of serving the age. Some wish to become the emperor’s arms and legs; others wish to become his ears and eyes. Indeed, without awaiting a summons with bow and banner, all are ready to render loyal service to the state. Who would willingly cast himself aside in an enlightened age? They would assist the emperor’s actions [?] and support his clear hearing. Indeed, without requiring an invitation accompanied by jade and silk, all wish to offer forthright counsel at court. Who would willingly fail his own aspirations in an enlightened age? Now, given the unanimity with which all these worthy men turn toward service…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
如此則賢俊之登庸也日廣德化之感孚也日
深彼頑讒者將久而自化矣帝何必徒恃乎刑
威哉考之虞時重華協帝帝舜之德固無遠而
不著九德咸事萬邦之賢亦無有不臣者而禹
之告舜必拳拳及此者何哉蓋聖人之心不以
君已聖而忘儆戒之心不以賢已用而忽致賢
之道惟恐君德有未至天下有遺賢也此有虞
之時所以君明臣良而雍熈泰和之治萬世鮮
儷也歟
===
德威惟畏德明惟明乃命三后恤功于民
伯夷降典折民惟刑禹平水土主名山川
稷降播種農殖嘉穀三后成功惟殷于民
士制百姓于刑之中以教祗德
同考試官訓導陳 批〔呂刑一篇本無異說但題長難於收拾作者多繁冗可厭獨此篇詞不費而意自足錄之〕
考試官教諭范 批〔得大舜制刑本意〕
punctuated:
如此，則賢俊之登庸也日廣，德化之感孚也日深，彼頑讒者將久而自化矣。帝何必徒恃乎刑威哉？考之虞時，重華協帝，帝舜之德固無遠而不著；九德咸事，萬邦之賢亦無有不臣者。而禹之告舜必拳拳及此者，何哉？蓋聖人之心，不以君已聖而忘儆戒之心，不以賢已用而忽致賢之道，惟恐君德有未至、天下有遺賢也。此有虞之時所以君明臣良，而雍熈泰和之治萬世鮮儷也歟？

德威惟畏，德明惟明。乃命三后恤功于民。伯夷降典，折民惟刑；禹平水土，主名山川；稷降播種，農殖嘉穀。三后成功，惟殷于民。士制百姓于刑之中，以教祗德。

同考試官訓導陳批〔呂刑一篇本無異說，但題長難於收拾，作者多繁冗可厭，獨此篇詞不費而意自足，錄之。〕

考試官教諭范批〔得大舜制刑本意。〕
translation_en:
…with such unanimity, the advancement of worthy and talented men to office would grow daily more extensive, and the transforming influence of virtue would daily inspire deeper trust. Those who were obstinate and slanderous would, in time, reform of themselves. Why should the emperor rely solely upon the威 force of punishments? Examining the age of Yu, we find that Chonghua accorded with the emperor: Emperor Shun’s virtue was manifest even in the most distant places. Those possessing the nine virtues all served in office, and among the worthy men of the myriad states there were none who did not serve as his subjects. Why, then, did Yu, in addressing Shun, so earnestly insist upon this matter? Because the sage’s heart does not forget the need for admonition merely because the ruler is already sagely, nor neglect the means of attracting worthy men merely because worthy men are already employed. He fears only that the ruler’s virtue may still fall short, or that worthy men in the realm may remain overlooked. Was this not why, in the age of Yu, the ruler was enlightened and his ministers excellent, and their harmonious, flourishing, and peaceful government had few equals through all the ages?

Virtue’s majesty alone inspires awe; virtue’s illumination alone brings enlightenment. He therefore commanded the three lords to devote themselves to accomplishing works for the people. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, guiding the people by models; Yu regulated the waters and land and presided over the renowned mountains and rivers; Ji disseminated the practice of sowing, cultivating fine grains. The three lords accomplished their work, bringing abundance to the people. The Director of Trials restrained the common people through punishments that struck the proper mean, thereby teaching them to revere virtue.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: 〔There are no divergent interpretations of the chapter “The Punishments of Lü,” but this topic is long and difficult to bring into a coherent whole. Most writers produce tiresomely verbose answers. This essay alone wastes no words while fully conveying its meaning; hence its inclusion.〕

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔It captures the great Shun’s original intention in establishing punishments.〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授田　批
〔書經義整潔〕
王者叙聖世君臣必本於德以成治而左□□
以補治焉蓋德者治之本而刑則資之以輔治
者也此聖世君臣之爲治所以必本之以德而
後資之以刑歟昔穆王命吕侯訓刑以詰四方
首舉舜之事以見其用刑之本未意謂人知有
虞之治用乎刑不知有虞之刑本乎德彼苗以
虐爲威也帝則布重華之神武而以德爲威但
見天下皆震懾於雷霆奮擊之中無一人之不
===
畏焉苗以察爲明也帝則廣四方之視聽而以
德爲明但見萬方皆昭融於日月照臨之下無
一人之不明焉帝既以德爲化民之本乃命三
后致憂民之功民心有未正也伯夷降天地人
之三禮以折民邪妄出禮者入於刑焉民居有
未奠也伯禹平九州之水土而主名山川昏墊
者得其所焉民生有未厚也稷降播種之方農
殖嘉穀之利是則三后職守雖異而協同成功
有以致民之殷盛責任雖殊而賛襄凝績有以
punctuated:
考試官教授田，批：〔書經義整潔〕

王者叙聖世君臣必本於德以成治，而左□□以補治焉。蓋德者治之本，而刑則資之以輔治者也。此聖世君臣之爲治，所以必本之以德，而後資之以刑歟！昔穆王命吕侯訓刑，以詰四方，首舉舜之事，以見其用刑之本未。意謂人知有虞之治用乎刑，不知有虞之刑本乎德。彼苗以虐爲威也，帝則布重華之神武，而以德爲威，但見天下皆震懾於雷霆奮擊之中，無一人之不畏焉。苗以察爲明也，帝則廣四方之視聽，而以德爲明，但見萬方皆昭融於日月照臨之下，無一人之不明焉。帝既以德爲化民之本，乃命三后致憂民之功。民心有未正也，伯夷降天地人之三禮，以折民邪妄，出禮者入於刑焉。民居有未奠也，伯禹平九州之水土，而主名山川，昏墊者得其所焉。民生有未厚也，稷降播種之方、農殖嘉穀之利。是則三后職守雖異，而協同成功，有以致民之殷盛；責任雖殊，而賛襄凝績，有以
translation_en:
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔The exposition of the Book of Documents is orderly and polished.〕

The king recounts how the ruler and ministers of a sage age necessarily grounded themselves in virtue to achieve good government, and employed [illegible passage] to supplement it [?]. Virtue is the foundation of government, while punishments are a resource used to assist it. Is this not why the ruler and ministers of a sage age necessarily based their government on virtue and only afterward drew upon punishments?

Formerly, King Mu commanded the Marquis of Lü to issue instructions on punishments so as to bring order to the four quarters. He began by citing the deeds of Shun to show the foundations and workings [?] of his use of punishments. His meaning was that people knew that the government of Youyu employed punishments, but did not know that Youyu’s punishments were rooted in virtue. The Miao used cruelty to inspire awe; the emperor instead manifested the divine martial power of Chonghua—Shun—and made virtue the source of his awe. All under Heaven stood trembling amid its thunderous force; there was not one person who did not fear it. The Miao took intrusive scrutiny for discernment; the emperor instead extended his sight and hearing throughout the four quarters and made virtue the source of his discernment. All regions were bathed in radiance beneath the light of sun and moon; there was not one person who was not enlightened.

Having made virtue the foundation for transforming the people, the emperor then commanded the three lords to accomplish the work of caring for them. Where the people’s hearts were not yet upright, Bo Yi promulgated the three categories of rites concerning Heaven, Earth, and humanity to check their perversity and waywardness; those who stepped outside the rites came within the scope of punishments. Where the people’s dwellings were not yet secure, Bo Yu brought order to the waters and lands of the Nine Provinces and took charge of the principal mountains and rivers; those submerged by the floods obtained places to settle. Where the people’s livelihoods were not yet ample, Ji imparted methods of sowing and the benefits of cultivating fine grains. Thus, although the three lords differed in their official duties, they cooperated in accomplishing their work and thereby brought the people prosperity. Although their responsibilities differed, they assisted one another in consolidating their achievements, thereby enabling …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
致民之富庶夫以德爲治如此而民尤有未化
者則刑其可已耶於是命臯陶爲士師之官專
掌刑之責民有弗若於政者則制刑之惟刑之
中非依勢作威也民有弗化于訓者則約之於
惟辟之中非倚法以削也所以撿束其心使惟
德是祗篤倫理於安居樂業之中耳防閑其志
使惟德是敬敦秉彝於生養安全之地耳是則
本之以德所以治乎民者至繼之以刑所以防
乎民者周有虞制刑之本末如此宜穆王舉之
===
以訓刑歟雖然穆王能言帝舜用刑之本末而
不知帝舜制刑之本末其所以制爲贖刑者特
以鞭朴之刑情法有可矜疑者乃聽其贖穆王
欲藉此以爲足國之計雖大辟亦聽贖焉其畔
舜也亦甚矣夫子録之以爲後世戒且以其能
拳拳乎折民惟刑教以祗德之語尤見當時用
刑專以德爲刑也君子可以人廢其言哉
詩
如月之恒如日之升如南山之壽
punctuated:
致民之富庶。夫以德爲治如此，而民尤有未化者，則刑其可已耶？於是命臯陶爲士師之官，專掌刑之責。民有弗若於政者，則制刑之惟刑之中，非依勢作威也；民有弗化于訓者，則約之於惟辟之中，非倚法以削也。所以撿束其心，使惟德是祗，篤倫理於安居樂業之中耳；防閑其志，使惟德是敬，敦秉彝於生養安全之地耳。是則本之以德，所以治乎民者至；繼之以刑，所以防乎民者周。有虞制刑之本末如此，宜穆王舉之以訓刑歟！雖然，穆王能言帝舜用刑之本末，而不知帝舜制刑之本末。其所以制爲贖刑者，特以鞭朴之刑，情法有可矜疑者，乃聽其贖。穆王欲藉此以爲足國之計，雖大辟亦聽贖焉，其畔舜也亦甚矣！夫子録之以爲後世戒，且以其能拳拳乎「折民惟刑，教以祗德」之語，尤見當時用刑專以德爲刑也。君子可以人廢其言哉？

詩

如月之恒，如日之升，如南山之壽。
translation_en:
…to bring the people prosperity and abundance. When government through virtue had reached this degree, yet some among the people remained untransformed, could punishments possibly be dispensed with? Accordingly, he appointed Gao Yao as Judge, giving him sole responsibility for punishments. When people failed to comply with government, he established punishments for them, ensuring that these struck the proper balance; he did not exploit his power to intimidate. When people failed to respond to instruction, he restrained them through properly measured penalties; he did not rely on the law to oppress them. His purpose was simply to discipline their hearts, so that they would revere virtue alone and strengthen ethical relationships while dwelling in peace and pursuing their livelihoods contentedly; to guard their intentions, so that they would honor virtue alone and cultivate their innate moral nature amid secure conditions of life and nurture. Thus, with virtue as the foundation, his means of governing the people were consummate; with punishments following upon it, his means of guarding against their wrongdoing were comprehensive. Such were the foundations and workings of the penal system established by the ruler of Yu, Shun. How fitting that King Mu should invoke them in his instructions on punishments!

Nevertheless, although King Mu could describe the foundations and workings of Emperor Shun’s use of punishments, he did not understand the foundations and workings of Shun’s establishment of them. Shun instituted redemption of punishment only for penalties of whipping and beating with a rod, allowing redemption when the circumstances and legal considerations warranted compassion or raised doubts. King Mu wished to use this as a means of replenishing the state’s resources, allowing redemption even for capital offenses. How far he departed from Shun! The Master recorded this as a warning to later generations. Moreover, King Mu’s earnest attachment to the words, “Restrain the people through punishments; teach them to revere virtue,” particularly reveals that the use of punishments at that time took virtue alone as punishment [?]. Could a gentleman reject these words on account of the man who spoke them?

Book of Odes

“As the moon waxes, as the sun rises, as enduring as the Southern Mountain.”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導吳　批〔小雅義連日閱卷率多紛　舊說令人厭觀曉得此卷獨能體認真切而發揮明整〕
〔令人心目爲之豁然〕
同考試官訓導熊　批〔天保一題學者多惑於小註　講月恒日升處殊背朱傳此作見理既明而詞又足以發〕
〔之是用錄出以破群疑〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔此作能揄揚臣子忠愛其君　之意殆無餘藴取之〕
同考試官教諭周　批〔理明詞贍蔚然經中之翹楚者〕
===
考試官教諭范　批〔作雅義正當如此〕
考試官教授田　批〔得温柔敦厚之旨〕
臣子答君有擬其福之盛大者有擬其福之悠
久者夫人君之福莫難於盛大尤莫難於悠久
也臣子擬是以答君忠愛之心不其至乎人君
以鹿鳴以下五詩燕其臣臣受賜者歌此詩以
答其君意謂君之於我燕禮之恩累加我之於
君報答之心難已彼多福之詒神福吾君爲已
punctuated:
同考試官訓導吳　批〔小雅義，連日閱卷，率多紛　舊說，令人厭觀，曉得此卷獨能體認真切，而發揮明整，〕〔令人心目爲之豁然。〕
同考試官訓導熊　批〔天保一題，學者多惑於小註，講月恒日升處，殊背朱傳。此作見理既明，而詞又足以發〕〔之，是用錄出，以破群疑。〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔此作能揄揚臣子忠愛其君之意，殆無餘藴，取之。〕
同考試官教諭周　批〔理明詞贍，蔚然經中之翹楚者。〕
考試官教諭范　批〔作雅義，正當如此。〕
考試官教授田　批〔得温柔敦厚之旨。〕
臣子答君，有擬其福之盛大者，有擬其福之悠久者。夫人君之福，莫難於盛大，尤莫難於悠久也。臣子擬是以答君，忠愛之心不其至乎？人君以《鹿鳴》以下五詩燕其臣，臣受賜者歌此詩以答其君。意謂：君之於我，燕禮之恩累加；我之於君，報答之心難已。彼多福之詒，神福吾君爲已
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wu, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔In interpreting the Lesser Odes, the papers I have read over the past several days mostly entangle themselves in old explanations [?], making them tiresome to read. I find [?] that this paper alone grasps the meaning truly and precisely, and develops it clearly and coherently,〕〔opening the reader’s mind and eyes.〕
Associate Examiner Xiong, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔On the topic from “Heaven Protects You” (Tian bao), students are often misled by the minor annotations. Their explanations of the waxing moon and rising sun markedly contradict Zhu Xi’s commentary. This composition understands the principle clearly, and its language is fully adequate to express〕〔it. It is therefore selected for inclusion to dispel the many doubts.〕
Associate Examiner Pan, an Instructor, comments: 〔This composition extols the loyal affection that a subject bears his ruler, leaving scarcely anything unexpressed. Accept it.〕
Associate Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: 〔Clear in principle and rich in expression, this is a conspicuously outstanding essay on this Classic.〕
Examiner Fan, an Instructor, comments: 〔This is precisely how an interpretation of the Odes should be written.〕
Examiner Tian, a Professor, comments: 〔It captures the purport of gentleness, sincerity, generosity, and kindness.〕
When subjects respond to their ruler, some draw comparisons for the greatness of his blessings, and others for their enduring duration. For a ruler’s blessings, nothing is harder to attain than greatness, and harder still is enduring duration. When subjects use such comparisons in responding to their ruler, is their loyal affection not at its utmost? The ruler entertains his subjects at a banquet with the five poems beginning with “The Deer Cry” (Lu ming); the subjects who receive this favor sing this poem in reply to their ruler. Their meaning is: “You have repeatedly bestowed upon us the gracious favor of ceremonial banquets; our desire to repay you cannot cease. As for that bestowal of many blessings, the spirits’ blessing of our ruler has already …”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
至矣然福多而盈無虧欠也有如月之恒焉蓋
月乃秉陰之精月上弦而就盈玉弓之勢方張
於天而清輝已透氷輪之彩雖受於日而素體
本圓君福之方膺而即盈者實似之福多而明
無昏塞也有如日之升焉蓋日乃秉陽之精日
始出而就明羲馭方賓於暘谷而輝光即被乎
八紘烏輪乍轉於咸池而靈曜已騰乎四海君
福之始受而即明者實似之若此者非其福之
盛大而何至若萬壽之卜神禱吾君爲已隆矣
===
玆龜齡鶴筭未足以比君之壽也必如南山之
壽巖巖巀巀拔上逼穹蒼與天地之同久吾君承
天統而享遐齡蓋與之等焉如岡如陵未足以
擬君之壽也必若南山之壽屹屹盤據下鎮坤
軸亘宇宙之常存吾君養天倪而躋上壽蓋與
之齊焉若此者非其福之悠久而何吁既以日
月擬其盛大而又以南山擬其悠久天保臣子
以是而答君忠愛之心何其至歟嗟夫卑高之
位定而堂陛之分嚴明良之歌息而上下之情
punctuated: 至矣。然福多而盈，無虧欠也，有如月之恒焉。蓋月乃秉陰之精，月上弦而就盈，玉弓之勢方張於天，而清輝已透；氷輪之彩雖受於日，而素體本圓。君福之方膺而即盈者，實似之。福多而明，無昏塞也，有如日之升焉。蓋日乃秉陽之精，日始出而就明，羲馭方賓於暘谷，而輝光即被乎八紘；烏輪乍轉於咸池，而靈曜已騰乎四海。君福之始受而即明者，實似之。若此者，非其福之盛大而何？至若萬壽之卜，神禱吾君爲已隆矣。玆龜齡鶴筭，未足以比君之壽也，必如南山之壽，巖巖巀巀，拔上逼穹蒼，與天地之同久。吾君承天統而享遐齡，蓋與之等焉。如岡如陵，未足以擬君之壽也，必若南山之壽，屹屹盤據，下鎮坤軸，亘宇宙之常存。吾君養天倪而躋上壽，蓋與之齊焉。若此者，非其福之悠久而何？吁！既以日月擬其盛大，而又以南山擬其悠久，《天保》臣子以是而答君，忠愛之心何其至歟！嗟夫！卑高之位定，而堂陛之分嚴；明良之歌息，而上下之情
translation_en: …have reached their utmost. Yet these abundant blessings are full, without deficiency, like the waxing moon. The moon embodies the essence of yin: upon reaching its first quarter, it approaches fullness. Its jade bow has only just been drawn across the heavens, yet its clear radiance already shines through; though its icy wheel receives its brilliance from the sun, its pale substance is inherently round. Our lord’s blessings, full as soon as he receives them, truly resemble this. His blessings are abundant and bright, without darkness or obstruction, like the rising sun. The sun embodies the essence of yang: as soon as it emerges, it shines brightly. Xi’s solar chariot has only just been welcomed at Yanggu, yet its radiance already spreads to the eight limits of the world; the crow-bearing solar wheel has barely begun to turn at Xianchi, yet its divine brilliance already rises over the Four Seas. Our lord’s blessings, bright from the moment he receives them, truly resemble this. What is this but the grandeur of his blessings? As for the divination of myriad years of life, the spirits’ prayers for our lord are already exalted indeed [?]. Yet the lifespans of tortoises and cranes cannot adequately compare with our lord’s longevity. It must resemble the longevity of the Southern Mountain: lofty and towering, rising toward the vault of heaven, enduring as long as Heaven and Earth. Our lord inherits Heaven’s succession and enjoys length of years, surely matching the mountain in this. Neither ridges nor hills suffice to represent our lord’s longevity. It must resemble the longevity of the Southern Mountain: firmly rooted and towering, securing the earth’s axis below, abiding forever throughout the universe. Our lord nurtures his heavenly endowment and attains the greatest longevity, surely equaling the mountain in this. What is this but the enduring nature of his blessings? Ah! Having likened their grandeur to the sun and moon, they further liken their endurance to the Southern Mountain. The ministers who address their lord in “Heaven Protects” (Tianbao) respond to him with these words: how consummate is their loyal affection! Alas! Once the positions of low and high are fixed, the distinction between hall and steps becomes strict; once the song of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers falls silent, the feelings of those above and below…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
隔元首股肱相待一體義存休戚之君臣者耶
求教有燕燕勞遣有燕燕以至於兄弟朋舊莫不有
燕遇下之恩亦既渥矣爲之臣者沾被之餘不
曰壽則曰福忠愛之誠有加而報答之情無已
此所以爲泰之時而有非後世之所能及也猗
歟盛哉
天監有周昭假于下保兹天子生仲山甫
同考試官訓導吳　批〔塲中作此題者於昭假保佑處多含糊欠明獨此篇體認親切且文氣舂融筆力〕
===
老健非稚作所能到是宜錄出
同考試官訓導熊　批〔此篇寫出周家世德相承而天人相與之意較然明白當是作者〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔形容尹吉甫送仲山甫之意殫蓋且詞理明暢可嘉可嘉〕
同考試官教諭周　批〔大雅義能如此作蓋絕無而僅有者殆龍經中之巨擘歟〕
考試官教諭范　批〔按註立說而辭足以達意其〕
punctuated:
隔，元首股肱相待一體，義存休戚之君臣者耶？求教有燕，燕勞遣有燕，燕以至於兄弟朋舊，莫不有燕，遇下之恩亦既渥矣。爲之臣者，沾被之餘，不曰壽則曰福，忠愛之誠有加，而報答之情無已。此所以爲泰之時，而有非後世之所能及也。猗歟盛哉！
天監有周，昭假于下，保兹天子，生仲山甫。
同考試官訓導吳，批〔塲中作此題者，於昭假保佑處多含糊欠明，獨此篇體認親切，且文氣舂融，筆力〕老健，非稚作所能到，是宜錄出。
同考試官訓導熊，批〔此篇寫出周家世德相承，而天人相與之意較然明白，當是作者。〕
同考試官教諭潘，批〔形容尹吉甫送仲山甫之意殫蓋，且詞理明暢，可嘉可嘉！〕
同考試官教諭周，批〔大雅義能如此作，蓋絕無而僅有者，殆龍經中之巨擘歟！〕
考試官教諭范，批〔按註立說，而辭足以達意，其〕
translation_en:
…become estranged. Are ruler and ministers then still related as head and limbs, depending upon one another as a single body, with a bond of shared fortune and adversity [?]? There were banquets when seeking instruction, and banquets to reward service and mark departures; even brothers and old friends all received banquets [?]. The favor shown to those below was indeed abundant. Having received such bounty, his ministers wished him either longevity or blessings. Their sincere loyalty and affection increased, and their desire to repay him knew no end. This is what made it an age of Grand Harmony, possessing something that later ages could not attain. Ah, how flourishing it was!
Heaven watched over Zhou; its radiant virtue reached up from below. To protect this Son of Heaven, Heaven brought forth Zhong Shanfu.
Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Among those who addressed this topic in the examination, most were vague and unclear about radiant virtue reaching Heaven and Heaven’s protection. This essay alone grasps these matters intimately. Moreover, its literary flow is harmonious [?], and its brushwork mature and vigorous—beyond the reach of an immature composition. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”
Associate Examiner Xiong, Assistant Instructor, comments: “This essay portrays the transmission of virtue through successive generations of the house of Zhou, making thoroughly clear the meaning of the mutual relationship between Heaven and humanity. Its author must be an accomplished writer.”
Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor, comments: “It fully captures [?] Yin Jifu’s sentiments in sending off Zhong Shanfu. Its language and reasoning are also lucid and fluent. Admirable, admirable!”
Associate Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “An exposition of the meaning of the Greater Odes written like this is exceedingly rare. Might he be a leading master of the ‘Dragon Classic’ [?]?”
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “He establishes his argument according to the commentary, and his language adequately conveys his meaning. Perhaps he…”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
留心於經學者歟
考試官教授田　批〔得詩人立言之意〕
惟天視一代也能格以明德故天佑一人也爲
生以賢佐甚矣天之生賢不偶然也今視有周
以明德感於下則眷之以生賢佐也烏容已哉
昔周宣王命樊侯仲山甫築城于齊而尹吉甫
作詩以送之至此蓋謂天人之勢若遼邈而天
人之理實感通彼蒼者天監視有周緝熙其敬
世有明德也而傳之今日其德爲靡悔皇矣上
===
帝顧視周家斤斤其明世有顯德也而傳之斯
世其德爲愈彰側身脩行以新中興之化者明
德之本也而有周能以是感格於下何昭昭乎
脩政攘夷以振中興之業者顯德之發也而周
家能以是感格於下何炳炳乎然惟德動天惟
天眷德故冲漠之中隆天子以保佑之休不生
乎祥麟也威鳳也而爲之生此賢佐曰仲山甫
焉穹窿之表申一人以敷錫之命不生乎醴泉
也芝草也而爲之生此賢輔曰仲山甫焉然是
punctuated:
留心於經學者歟？
考試官教授田　批〔得詩人立言之意〕
惟天視一代也，能格以明德，故天佑一人也，爲生以賢佐。甚矣，天之生賢不偶然也！今視有周，以明德感於下，則眷之以生賢佐也，烏容已哉？昔周宣王命樊侯仲山甫築城于齊，而尹吉甫作詩以送之。至此，蓋謂天人之勢若遼邈，而天人之理實感通。彼蒼者天，監視有周，緝熙其敬，世有明德也，而傳之今日，其德爲靡悔。皇矣上帝，顧視周家，斤斤其明，世有顯德也，而傳之斯世，其德爲愈彰。側身脩行，以新中興之化者，明德之本也，而有周能以是感格於下，何昭昭乎！脩政攘夷，以振中興之業者，顯德之發也，而周家能以是感格於下，何炳炳乎！然惟德動天，惟天眷德，故冲漠之中，隆天子以保佑之休，不生乎祥麟也、威鳳也，而爲之生此賢佐曰仲山甫焉。穹窿之表，申一人以敷錫之命，不生乎醴泉也、芝草也，而爲之生此賢輔曰仲山甫焉。然是
translation_en:
…one who devotes himself to the study of the Classics?

Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔He has grasped the poet’s intention in composing these words.〕

When Heaven watches over a dynasty, that dynasty can reach Heaven through luminous virtue; thus, when Heaven protects the sovereign, it brings forth worthy assistants for him. How profoundly true it is that Heaven’s bringing forth worthy men is no accident! Now, observing Zhou, which moves Heaven from below through luminous virtue, how could Heaven refrain from favoring it by bringing forth worthy assistants?

Formerly, King Xuan of Zhou ordered Zhong Shanfu, Marquis of Fan, to build a city wall in Qi, and Yin Jifu composed a poem to send him off. At this point in the poem, his meaning is that although Heaven and humanity seem far apart in their respective positions, the principle uniting them truly permits mutual influence and communication. Blue Heaven watches over Zhou: its reverence has been continually cultivated and made radiant, and every generation has possessed luminous virtue. Transmitted down to the present day, that virtue is without regret [?]. August is the Lord on High, who looks upon the house of Zhou: discerning in its illumination, it has possessed manifest virtue in every generation. Transmitted down to this age, that virtue has become still more resplendent.

To conduct oneself with circumspection and cultivate one’s behavior, thereby renewing the transforming influence of the dynastic restoration, is the foundation of luminous virtue. How brightly Zhou shines in its ability thereby to move and reach Heaven from below! To reform government and repel the Yi peoples, thereby invigorating the work of the dynastic restoration, is the expression of manifest virtue. How brilliantly the house of Zhou shines in its ability thereby to move and reach Heaven from below!

Yet it is virtue that moves Heaven, and Heaven that favors virtue. Thus, amid its silent formlessness, Heaven exalts the Son of Heaven with the blessing of protection. It does not bring forth an auspicious qilin or a majestic phoenix, but instead brings forth for him this worthy assistant named Zhong Shanfu. Beyond the vault of the sky, it renews for the sovereign its mandate bestowing blessings. It does not bring forth springs of sweet water or numinous mushrooms, but instead brings forth for him this worthy helper named Zhong Shanfu. Yet this…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
山甫也鍾氣之秀而稟巽乎凡民全德之美而
卓出乎流輩蓋將賴之以輔中興之化而王臣
是式王躬是保也祥麟威鳳云乎哉將資之以
佐中興之業而王命是司王政是賦也醴泉芝
草云乎哉吁保天子正所以監明德也生賢佐
正所以保天子也尹吉甫送山甫之行而言及
此其旨淵乎微矣抑論君以代天理物而臣以
代君宣化故有周文武之創業成康之守成宣
王之中興而皆資賢才以爲之輔此所以綿綿
===
延延而衍八百年之運祚誠有自也今尹吉甫
送仲山甫城齊之行而首以是爲言其意端在
是矣讀是詩者尚其味之
春秋
春正月公會宋公蔡侯衛侯于曹　夏四
月公會宋公衛侯陳侯蔡侯伐鄭　秋七
月公至自伐鄭〔桓公十六年〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔題本一事而二傳相承各〕
punctuated:
山甫也，鍾氣之秀而稟巽乎凡民，全德之美而卓出乎流輩。蓋將賴之以輔中興之化，而王臣是式，王躬是保也，祥麟威鳳云乎哉？將資之以佐中興之業，而王命是司，王政是賦也，醴泉芝草云乎哉？吁！保天子，正所以監明德也；生賢佐，正所以保天子也。尹吉甫送山甫之行而言及此，其旨淵乎微矣！抑論君以代天理物，而臣以代君宣化，故有周文武之創業、成康之守成、宣王之中興，而皆資賢才以爲之輔。此所以綿綿延延而衍八百年之運祚，誠有自也。今尹吉甫送仲山甫城齊之行，而首以是爲言，其意端在是矣。讀是詩者，尚其味之！

春秋

春正月，公會宋公、蔡侯、衛侯于曹。夏四月，公會宋公、衛侯、陳侯、蔡侯伐鄭。秋七月，公至自伐鄭。〔桓公十六年〕

同考試官教諭范，批〔題本一事，而二傳相承，各〕
translation_en:
…Shanfu concentrated within himself the finest vital essence, and his endowment surpassed that of ordinary people [?]; possessing the beauty of complete virtue, he stood far above his contemporaries. He was to be relied upon to assist the transformative influence of the restoration, serving as a model for the king’s ministers and protecting the king’s person. Could an auspicious qilin or a majestic phoenix compare with this? He was to be enlisted to assist the work of the restoration, taking charge of the king’s commands and administering the king’s government. Could sweet springs or auspicious fungi compare with this? Ah! Protecting the Son of Heaven is precisely how Heaven shows regard for illustrious virtue; bringing forth a worthy assistant is precisely how it protects the Son of Heaven. Yin Jifu spoke of this when sending Shanfu on his journey: how profound and subtle was his meaning!

Further, the ruler orders affairs on Heaven’s behalf, while ministers spread transforming influence on the ruler’s behalf. Thus, the founding achievements of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou, the preservation of their inheritance under Kings Cheng and Kang, and the restoration under King Xuan all depended upon worthy men to assist them. There was indeed a reason why the dynasty’s allotted fortune continued unbroken for eight hundred years. When Yin Jifu sent Zhong Shanfu off to fortify Qi and began by speaking of this, his intention lay precisely here. May those who read this ode savor its meaning!

Spring and Autumn Annals

In spring, in the first month, the duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, and the Marquis of Wei at Cao. In summer, in the fourth month, the duke joined the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Marquis of Chen, and the Marquis of Cai in attacking Zheng. In autumn, in the seventh month, the duke returned from the campaign against Zheng. 〔The sixteenth year of Duke Huan.〕

Associate Examiner Fan, School Instructor, comments: 〔The topic concerns a single affair, and the two commentaries follow upon one another, each…〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
發其旨聖經自是明白固非牽合而成場中作者
類能言之然融會傳意斷制明盡者僅見此篇故
錄之
文最是
考試官教諭范　批〔以禮義與王制王法體貼成〕
考試官教授田　批〔春秋責宋魯之意發明殆盡真傑作也宜錄出以式〕
春秋紀諸侯兵好既責序爵之非禮者以謹王
制尤責與隣之非義者以正王法此會曹伐鄭
之事宋之抑蔡魯之納突皆非也考其所書意
自見矣昔我魯桓之十有六年春正月紀四國
之會曹夏四月錄五國之伐鄭兵好繼舉宋莊
主之列國從之觀其春之會也蔡衛來固先
蔡于衣裳之列夏之伐也蔡後衛至乃先衛于
兵車之間宋固自以升降諸侯為能事然不知
王制諸侯之爵次尊卑有等猶天建地設禮所
定者豈可以至之先後易之乎今者蔡以文昭
之裔武王所封衛以武穆之亂成王所建不以
punctuated:
發其旨，聖經自是明白，固非牽合而成。場中作者類能言之，然融會傳意，斷制明盡者，僅見此篇，故錄之。
文最是。
考試官教諭范，批〔以禮義與王制王法體貼成〕
考試官教授田，批〔春秋責宋魯之意，發明殆盡，真傑作也。宜錄出以式〕
春秋紀諸侯兵好，既責序爵之非禮者以謹王制，尤責與隣之非義者以正王法。此會曹伐鄭之事，宋之抑蔡、魯之納突，皆非也。考其所書，意自見矣。昔我魯桓之十有六年，春正月紀四國之會曹，夏四月錄五國之伐鄭。兵好繼舉，宋莊主之，列國從之。觀其春之會也，蔡衛來，固先蔡于衣裳之列；夏之伐也，蔡後衛至，乃先衛于兵車之間。宋固自以升降諸侯為能事，然不知王制諸侯之爵次，尊卑有等，猶天建地設。禮所定者，豈可以至之先後易之乎？今者蔡以文昭之裔，武王所封；衛以武穆之亂，成王所建。不以
translation_en:
… expound its purport. The sage’s classic is thereby made clear; this certainly is no forced reconciliation. Most candidates in the examination hall could discuss this, but this essay alone integrates the meanings of the commentaries and reaches judgments that are clear and thorough. It is therefore included.
The writing is most sound. [?]
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔It develops its argument through close consideration of ritual propriety and righteousness, together with royal institutions and royal law …〕[?]
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔It elucidates almost completely the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals in censuring Song and Lu. Truly an outstanding work! It should be included to serve as a model.〕
In recording the warfare and friendly relations of the feudal lords, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures breaches of ritual propriety in ordering noble ranks, thereby safeguarding royal institutions. It especially censures unrighteous conduct toward neighboring states, thereby upholding royal law. In these events—the meeting at Cao and the campaign against Zheng—Song’s demotion of Cai and Lu’s installation of Tu were both wrong. Examine what the Annals records, and its meaning becomes apparent.
In the sixteenth year of Duke Huan of our state of Lu, the Annals records a meeting of four states at Cao in the first month of spring, and a campaign by five states against Zheng in the fourth month, in summer. Friendly relations and warfare followed in succession: Duke Zhuang of Song led, and the other states followed. Consider the spring meeting: when Cai and Wei arrived, Cai was indeed placed first in the ranks of those assembled in ceremonial robes. In the summer campaign, Cai arrived after Wei, so Wei was placed first among the war chariots. Song certainly regarded raising and lowering the standing of the feudal lords as an accomplishment. Yet it failed to understand that, under royal institutions, the noble ranks of the feudal lords have prescribed degrees of superiority and inferiority, as firmly established as heaven and earth. How could what ritual propriety has fixed be altered according to the order of arrival?
Now Cai descended from King Wen’s zhao line and was enfeoffed by King Wu; Wei descended from King Wu’s mu line [?] and was established by King Cheng. Without taking this into account …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
此計尊卑而一惟至焉是序是以利率人而不
要諸禮矣如王制何哉況宋以賔禮立國而肆
爲非禮如此厥後有以醲賞誘人之私以重罰
沮人之正者蓋此啓之也春秋防微杜漸尤嚴
於名分兩書蔡衛之序而不革者以見二國之
先後迭爲之主在宋也所以彰其失而謹王制
矣迨夫秋之七月列國各還其師我公始返其
國兵戎久役雖宋之謀亦魯之謀考其忽之歸
鄭也曰以弱必逐之爰是捐勞于師突之入櫟
===
也曰以彊必納之用玆告成于廟魯固自以廢
置諸侯爲常事然不知王法諸侯之繼嗣正邪
有辨猶天冠地履義所重者豈可以勢之強弱
桑之乎今者忽以嫡冢之貴鄭莊所立突以庶
孽之賤祭仲所援不以此論邪正而一惟勢焉
是與是以惡比人而不審諸義矣如王法何哉
顧桓以不義得國而恣爲非義如此厥後有内
交以稔其禍外結以朋其奸者蓋此階之也春
秋討賊誅亂必先於黨與特書我公之至而不
punctuated:
此計尊卑，而一惟至焉是序，是以利率人而不要諸禮矣，如王制何哉？況宋以賔禮立國，而肆爲非禮如此，厥後有以醲賞誘人之私、以重罰沮人之正者，蓋此啓之也。《春秋》防微杜漸，尤嚴於名分，兩書蔡衛之序而不革者，以見二國之先後迭爲之，主在宋也，所以彰其失而謹王制矣。
迨夫秋之七月，列國各還其師，我公始返其國。兵戎久役，雖宋之謀，亦魯之謀。考其忽之歸鄭也，曰以弱必逐之，爰是捐勞于師；突之入櫟也，曰以彊必納之，用玆告成于廟。魯固自以廢置諸侯爲常事，然不知王法，諸侯之繼嗣，正邪有辨，猶天冠地履，義所重者，豈可以勢之強弱桑之乎？今者忽以嫡冢之貴，鄭莊所立；突以庶孽之賤，祭仲所援。不以此論邪正，而一惟勢焉是與，是以惡比人而不審諸義矣，如王法何哉？顧桓以不義得國，而恣爲非義如此，厥後有内交以稔其禍、外結以朋其奸者，蓋此階之也。《春秋》討賊誅亂，必先於黨與，特書我公之至而不
translation_en:
…this in determining precedence, but orders them solely by their arrival. This is to lead others through advantage without holding them to ritual propriety. What, then, becomes of the royal institutions? Moreover, Song was established as a state accorded the ritual treatment of a guest, yet acted so wantonly against ritual propriety. Later instances of enticing people’s selfish desires with lavish rewards and thwarting their upright conduct with severe punishments surely began here. The Spring and Autumn Annals guards against the slightest beginnings of wrongdoing and checks its gradual development; it is especially strict about titles and the distinctions of status. It records the order of Cai and Wei on both occasions without altering it, thereby showing that responsibility for making the two states alternate in precedence lay with Song. Thus it exposes Song’s fault and upholds the royal institutions.
When the seventh month of autumn came, the various states each withdrew their armies, and only then did our duke return to his state. The prolonged military campaign was planned by Lu as well as Song. Consider their response to Hu’s return to Zheng: they said that because he was weak, they must expel him, and accordingly expended their armies’ toil. At Tu’s entry into Yue, they said that because he was strong, they must install him, and on this account announced their success in the ancestral temple. Lu indeed regarded deposing and installing feudal lords as routine affairs. Yet it did not understand that royal law distinguishes legitimate from illegitimate successors to feudal lords. Like Heaven above one’s head and Earth beneath one’s feet, this is a distinction upon which righteousness places great weight. How could it be altered [?] according to relative strength and weakness? Hu possessed the honored status of eldest son of the principal wife and had been designated by Duke Zhuang of Zheng; Tu possessed the lowly status of a son of a concubine and was supported by Ji Zhong. Instead of judging legitimacy by this distinction, they supported power alone. This was to associate with others in wrongdoing without examining the requirements of righteousness. What, then, becomes of royal law? Consider, too, that Duke Huan had gained his state through unrighteousness, yet acted so unrestrainedly against righteousness. Later instances of forming connections within to bring calamity to fruition and forging alliances abroad to abet treachery surely took their first step here. In chastising traitors and punishing disorder, the Spring and Autumn Annals necessarily begins with their accomplices. It expressly records our duke’s arrival and does not…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
削者以見三時之勤動始息之危在魯也所以
著其罪而正王法矣吁以禮責宋而先王封國
之制秩不可渝以義責魯而先王傳國之法凜
不可犯垂訓之義大矣哉雖然抑蔡助突豈特
宋魯之罪使爲蔡拒者能以禮自辨則衛將退
讓不暇諸侯亦無敢附會之者宋雖彊安得而
獨抑之爲鄭忽者能以義自立則突將退避弗
遑諸侯亦無敢庇翼之者魯雖大烏得而獨逐
之是則蔡也忽也自取之也何憾乎衛突何恠
===
乎宋魯何尤乎諸侯
蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于柏舉 吳入郢
定公四年
同考試官教諭范 批〔此題傳二事已犂然塲中士子多以前傳語意牽繞入講殊戾褒貶本義〕
〔是篇脫出衆見說理造辭嚴整明從而其氣亦充〕
〔固佳士也良用敬服〕
考試官教諭范 批〔講聖人順天命奉天討〕
punctuated:
削者，以見三時之勤、動始息之危在魯也，所以著其罪而正王法矣。吁！以禮責宋，而先王封國之制秩不可渝；以義責魯，而先王傳國之法凜不可犯。垂訓之義大矣哉！雖然，抑蔡助突，豈特宋魯之罪？使爲蔡拒者能以禮自辨，則衛將退讓不暇，諸侯亦無敢附會之者，宋雖彊，安得而獨抑之？爲鄭忽者能以義自立，則突將退避弗遑，諸侯亦無敢庇翼之者，魯雖大，烏得而獨逐之？是則蔡也、忽也，自取之也。何憾乎衛突？何恠乎宋魯？何尤乎諸侯？
蔡侯以吳子及楚人戰于柏舉，吳入郢。
定公四年。
同考試官教諭范，批〔此題傳二事已犂然，塲中士子多以前傳語意牽繞入講，殊戾褒貶本義。〕〔是篇脫出衆見，說理造辭嚴整明從，而其氣亦充。〕〔固佳士也，良用敬服。〕
考試官教諭范，批〔講聖人順天命、奉天討〕
translation_en:
…was not expunged, thereby showing that the exertions over three seasons and the peril attending movement and repose [?] lay with Lu. This exposes its guilt and upholds the royal law. Ah! In holding Song accountable according to ritual propriety, it shows that the institutions and ranks established by the former kings when enfeoffing states cannot be altered; in holding Lu accountable according to righteousness, it shows that the former kings’ laws governing succession to states are inviolable in their solemn authority. How profound is the significance of this instruction for posterity!
Nevertheless, were Song and Lu alone guilty of suppressing Cai and assisting Tu? Had Cai Ju [?] been able to vindicate himself according to ritual propriety, Wei would have hastened to yield, and none of the other feudal lords would have dared join in. Though Song was powerful, how could it alone have suppressed him? Had Hu of Zheng been able to establish himself according to righteousness, Tu would have hastened to withdraw, and none of the other feudal lords would have dared protect him. Though Lu was great, how could it alone have driven him out? Thus Cai and Hu brought this upon themselves. Why resent Wei and Tu? Why blame Song and Lu? Why reproach the other feudal lords?
“The Marquis of Cai, with the Viscount of Wu, fought the men of Chu at Boju. Wu entered Ying.”
Fourth year of Duke Ding.
Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔The commentary on this topic already distinguishes the two events clearly. Many candidates in the examination hall entangle their explanations with the wording and ideas of the preceding commentary, seriously contravening the original intent of its praise and blame.〕〔This essay rises above commonplace interpretations. Its reasoning and phrasing are rigorous, orderly, and clear [?], and its rhetorical force is also abundant.〕〔He is indeed an excellent scholar, deserving sincere respect and admiration.〕
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔In explaining how the Sage follows Heaven’s mandate and carries out Heaven’s punishments…〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
處精微可取
考試官教授田　批　得謹嚴之體
遠人始攘外以恤患春秋之所褒繼雲外以肆
暴春秋之所貶此吳於柏舉稱爵入郢舉號一
進一黜而聖人賞善罰惡之公見矣慨自召陵
罷侵蔡之請救于吳也急矣今焉吳師伐楚柏
舉交鋒夫吳乃僭號而變於夷者經以爵稱聖
人其有譽耶蓋春秋天子之事五服五章所當
命也彼蔡圍未解晉救無功楚橫自若當是時
===
膺懲之法固已不可申矣使吳也怠於恤鄰卻
小國雲霓之望而坐視之亦奚足道乃志能自
卑仗義往救闔閭執討楚之詞子胥問拘蔡之
故控師奪將大創其威此中國之事非變於夷
者之所能爲於此無褒焉則善不蒙賞將使人
之改轍者弗得由自新之路果何以示勸哉
故於柏舉之戰進而稱爵特書曰子非有心於
與之順天命也聖人賞善之權其公如是然自
囊瓦告敗楚之受禍於吳也殆矣今焉吳人挾
punctuated:
處精微可取。
考試官教授田，批：得謹嚴之體。
遠人始攘外以恤患，春秋之所褒；繼雲外以肆暴，春秋之所貶。此吳於柏舉稱爵，入郢舉號，一進一黜，而聖人賞善罰惡之公見矣。慨自召陵罷侵，蔡之請救于吳也急矣。今焉吳師伐楚，柏舉交鋒。夫吳乃僭號而變於夷者，經以爵稱，聖人其有譽耶？蓋春秋，天子之事，五服五章所當命也。彼蔡圍未解，晉救無功，楚橫自若。當是時，膺懲之法固已不可申矣。使吳也怠於恤鄰，卻小國雲霓之望而坐視之，亦奚足道？乃志能自卑，仗義往救。闔閭執討楚之詞，子胥問拘蔡之故，控師奪將，大創其威。此中國之事，非變於夷者之所能爲。於此無褒焉，則善不蒙賞，將使人之改轍者弗得由自新之路，果何以示勸哉？故於柏舉之戰，進而稱爵，特書曰子，非有心於與之，順天命也。聖人賞善之權，其公如是。然自囊瓦告敗，楚之受禍於吳也殆矣。今焉吳人挾
translation_en:
…the passage is subtle and merits approval.

Examiner Tian, Prefectural School Professor, comments: It achieves a careful and rigorous style.

When people from a distant land initially repel an external power to relieve distress, the Spring and Autumn Annals praises them; when they subsequently turn outward [?] to perpetrate violence, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures them. Thus, in the battle at Boju, Wu is designated by its ruler’s noble rank, whereas in the entry into Ying, it is named by its state designation. In this advancement and this demotion, the impartiality with which the Sage rewards good and punishes evil becomes manifest.

Alas, after the invasion was called off at Shaoling, Cai’s appeal to Wu for rescue became urgent. Now Wu’s army attacked Chu, and the forces clashed at Boju. Wu had usurped a royal title and adopted barbarian ways; yet the Classic names its ruler by his noble rank. Was the Sage offering praise? The Spring and Autumn Annals concerns the affairs of the Son of Heaven: the five grades of ceremonial robes and their five sets of insignia are his to confer. Cai’s siege had not been lifted, Jin’s rescue had achieved nothing, and Chu remained as overbearing as ever. At that time, the prescribed means of chastisement could no longer be enforced. Had Wu neglected its distressed neighbor, disappointed the small state’s hopes—as eager as longing for rain clouds in a drought—and merely stood by watching, what would have been worthy of mention? Instead, Wu humbled its aspirations and went to the rescue in the cause of righteousness. Helü proclaimed the grounds for chastising Chu, and Zixu demanded to know why the ruler of Cai had been detained. Wu checked Chu’s army and seized its commander, dealing a severe blow to its might. This was conduct befitting the central states, beyond what one who had adopted barbarian ways could accomplish. If there were no praise here, goodness would go unrewarded, and those who changed their course would be denied a path to reform themselves. How, then, could encouragement truly be offered?

Therefore, in recording the battle at Boju, the Sage advances Wu by naming its ruler’s noble rank, expressly writing “Viscount.” This was no deliberate favoritism toward him, but obedience to Heaven’s mandate. Such was the impartiality of the Sage’s authority to reward goodness. Yet after Nang Wa reported defeat, the calamity inflicted on Chu by Wu became grave. Now the men of Wu, taking advantage of…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
勝長驅入郢夫吳乃救蔡而進於夏者經以號
舉聖人其有毀耶蓋春秋天子之事五刑弗用
所當討也彼蔡圍既解伯討有成楚氛頓息當
是時安攘之功固已不可少矣使吳也謹於伐
國拯斯民水火之困而鳩集之亦奚足議乃志
不在大乘約肆淫吳王舍楚君之室子山處令
尹之宮毀廟遷器益深其禍此夷狄之道非進
於夏者之所可爲於此無貶焉則惡不蒙罰將
使人之恃小功者或得掩莫大之過又何以示
懲哉故於入郢之役黜而舉號止書曰吳非有
===
心於貶之奉天討也聖人罰惡之權其公如是
吁一吳子也進之則同於中國黜之則比於夷
狄功不少掩而罪不少貸其嚴矣乎大抵賞罰
天子之大權雖堯舜之治天下舍是亦不可爲
也況春秋時乎而是非不明賞罰不公敗度縱
欲崇日將淪胥於亡矣吾夫子位不在而道在
也於斯世斯民有惻然不能忘者故假史修經
以其權是非天下事而賞罰加焉撥亂反正亦
punctuated:
勝長驅入郢。夫吳乃救蔡而進於夏者，經以號舉，聖人其有毀耶？蓋《春秋》，天子之事，五刑弗用，所當討也。彼蔡圍既解，伯討有成，楚氛頓息，當是時，安攘之功固已不可少矣。使吳也謹於伐國，拯斯民水火之困而鳩集之，亦奚足議？乃志不在大，乘約肆淫，吳王舍楚君之室，子山處令尹之宮，毀廟遷器，益深其禍。此夷狄之道，非進於夏者之所可爲。於此無貶焉，則惡不蒙罰，將使人之恃小功者或得掩莫大之過，又何以示懲哉？故於入郢之役，黜而舉號，止書曰「吳」，非有心於貶之，奉天討也。聖人罰惡之權，其公如是。
吁！一吳子也，進之則同於中國，黜之則比於夷狄，功不少掩，而罪不少貸，其嚴矣乎！大抵賞罰，天子之大權，雖堯舜之治天下，舍是亦不可爲也，況《春秋》時乎？而是非不明，賞罰不公，敗度縱欲，崇日將淪胥於亡矣。吾夫子位不在而道在也，於斯世斯民有惻然不能忘者，故假史修經，以其權是非天下事，而賞罰加焉，撥亂反正，亦
translation_en:
…pressing its victory, it advanced swiftly and entered Ying. Now Wu had rescued Cai and thereby advanced to the standing of the civilized Xia; yet the Classic refers to it by its state designation. Did the Sage intend to disparage it? The Spring and Autumn Annals concerns the affairs of the Son of Heaven: where the five punishments were not applied, it pronounced the censure that was due. Once the siege of Cai had been lifted, the hegemon’s punitive expedition had succeeded, and the menace of Chu had abruptly subsided, Wu’s achievement in securing peace and repelling aggression certainly could not be slighted. Had Wu exercised restraint in attacking another state, rescued its people from suffering as grievous as fire and flood, and gathered them together again, what grounds would there have been for criticism? Instead, its aspirations fell short of greatness: it exploited distress and indulged in debauchery. The king of Wu lodged in the chambers of Chu’s ruler, and Zishan occupied the palace of its chief minister. They destroyed ancestral temples and removed ritual vessels, deepening the calamity. These were the ways of the barbarians, conduct impermissible for one who had advanced to the standing of the civilized Xia. If there were no condemnation here, evil would go unpunished, and those relying on minor achievements might be allowed to conceal the gravest faults. How, then, could wrongdoing be deterred? Thus, in recording the entry into Ying, the Annals demoted Wu by using only its state designation, writing simply “Wu.” This was no deliberate desire to disparage it, but the execution of Heaven’s punishment. Such was the impartiality of the Sage’s authority to punish evil.
Ah! It was the very same Viscount of Wu: when advanced, he was treated as the equal of the central states; when demoted, he was ranked with the barbarians. His merit was not obscured in the least, nor was his guilt pardoned in the least. How stern this was! Reward and punishment are, after all, the great prerogatives of the Son of Heaven. Even Yao and Shun could not have governed the world without them; how much more necessary were they in the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals! Yet right and wrong were not clearly distinguished, rewards and punishments were unjust, standards were corrupted, and desires indulged; “chong ri” [?]—all were about to sink together into ruin. Our Master lacked the position, but possessed the Way. He felt a compassion for his age and its people that he could not put aside. Thus he drew upon historical records to compile the Classic, using its authority to judge the rights and wrongs of the world’s affairs and to impose rewards and punishments upon them. Bringing disorder to an end and restoring what was right was also…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
世道之一治耳噫斧衮龍衡萬世而下司賞罰
者宜於是焉求之
禮記
愽聞强識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
考試官教諭范　批〔發明君子知行兼盡處殆無餘藴必老學之士麈戰文塲當一皷而得雋矣〕
考試官教授田　批〔曲禮一題似易而實難塲屋之士多爲窘筆獨此篇發明詳盡且詞氣充蔚〕
〔優於衆作宜録之以爲後學式〕
===
盡君子之道全君子之名蓋君子之道不外乎
知行也於此而兼盡焉則誠得全君子之名也
豈不宜哉且夫君子以求道爲本而求道以知
行爲先彼聞識所以致知也不能博强則所知
爲有限矣故凡天下事理之極蓋必無所不聞
而聞焉欲致其博不局局於孤陋無所不識而
識焉欲致其彊不拘拘於膚淺然又慮之以讓
雖知而若未知歉然自視而不足初無矜已傲
punctuated:
世道之一治耳。噫！斧衮龍衡，萬世而下司賞罰者，宜於是焉求之。

禮記
愽聞强識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。

考試官教諭范　批〔發明君子知行兼盡處，殆無餘藴，必老學之士。麈戰文塲，當一皷而得雋矣。〕
考試官教授田　批〔曲禮一題，似易而實難，塲屋之士多爲窘筆。獨此篇發明詳盡，且詞氣充蔚。〕〔優於衆作，宜録之以爲後學式。〕

盡君子之道，全君子之名。蓋君子之道不外乎知行也，於此而兼盡焉，則誠得全君子之名也，豈不宜哉？且夫君子以求道爲本，而求道以知行爲先。彼聞識所以致知也，不能博强，則所知爲有限矣。故凡天下事理之極，蓋必無所不聞，而聞焉欲致其博，不局局於孤陋；無所不識，而識焉欲致其彊，不拘拘於膚淺。然又慮之以讓，雖知而若未知，歉然自視而不足，初無矜已傲
translation_en:
…was simply another restoration of order to the world. Ah! The axe of punishment, the ceremonial robe of reward, and the “dragon balance” [?]: those who administer rewards and punishments in all generations to come should seek their guidance here.

Record of Rites
“To be widely informed and strong in retention, yet modest; to be earnest in good conduct and never slacken: this is what is called being a gentleman.”

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔The explanation of how the gentleman fully accomplishes both knowing and acting leaves almost nothing unexplored. The author must be a mature scholar. Contending in the examination arena [?], he should gain distinction at the first beat of the drum.〕
Comment by Examiner Tian, Professor: 〔This topic from “Summary of the Rules of Propriety” seems easy but is actually difficult; candidates in the examination hall often find themselves at a loss to write about it. This essay alone explains it thoroughly, and its language and spirit are rich and vigorous.〕〔Superior to the other compositions, it should be recorded as a model for later students.〕

Fulfill the way of the gentleman, and fully deserve the name of gentleman. The gentleman’s way encompasses nothing beyond knowing and acting. If one fully accomplishes both, one truly deserves the name of gentleman. Is this not fitting? The gentleman takes seeking the Way as his foundation, and in seeking the Way gives priority to knowing and acting. Learning through hearing and retaining what one learns are the means of extending knowledge. Unless these are broad and strong, one’s knowledge will be limited. Thus, regarding the utmost principles of all affairs under Heaven, there must be nothing one does not hear of; in hearing, one seeks breadth, without remaining confined within narrow learning. There must be nothing one does not retain; in retaining, one seeks firmness, without remaining confined to superficial understanding. Yet one also considers this with modesty: though knowing, one acts as though one did not yet know, humbly regarding oneself as inadequate, never showing self-conceit or arrogance…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
物之矣焉善行所以为行也不能敦篤則所行
爲有歉矣故凡天下道德之懿蓋必如孝如弟
務在措之於躬行不徒事乎誦說如忠如信務
在施之於實踐不徒事乎言論然又濟之以勤
継行而若未能行發然自勵而不怠初無進鋭
退速之患焉夫知行之事兼盡其功則君子之
道克盡於已若斯人也吾知篤實無僞而本之
立者望必隆輿論以之攸歸非違道干譽者之
可比謂之君子夫何愧謹厚有餘而實之大者
===
聲必宏鄉評以之同許非務外好名者之可倫
謂之君子夫何忝吁君子成名而必由於知行
盡道如此然則欲學爲君子者烏可外是以他
求哉大抵知行二事君子之先務也自常情觀
之孰不以爲學者粗近之跡殊不知希賢之階
作聖之功一皆以此而爲始耳苟能從事於斯
無少間斷則由粗而可以入精由近而可以到
遠何患不與聖賢同歸也噫有志求道者當以
知行爲標準
punctuated:
物之矣焉。善行所以为行也，不能敦篤，則所行爲有歉矣。故凡天下道德之懿，蓋必如孝如弟，務在措之於躬行，不徒事乎誦說；如忠如信，務在施之於實踐，不徒事乎言論。然又濟之以勤，継行而若未能行，發然自勵而不怠，初無進鋭退速之患焉。夫知行之事兼盡其功，則君子之道克盡於已。若斯人也，吾知篤實無僞而本之立者，望必隆，輿論以之攸歸，非違道干譽者之可比，謂之君子，夫何愧？謹厚有餘而實之大者，聲必宏，鄉評以之同許，非務外好名者之可倫，謂之君子，夫何忝？

吁！君子成名，而必由於知行盡道如此，然則欲學爲君子者，烏可外是以他求哉？大抵知行二事，君子之先務也。自常情觀之，孰不以爲學者粗近之跡？殊不知希賢之階、作聖之功，一皆以此而爲始耳。苟能從事於斯，無少間斷，則由粗而可以入精，由近而可以到遠，何患不與聖賢同歸也？噫！有志求道者，當以知行爲標準。
translation_en:
…disdain for others [?]. Good conduct is the means of putting knowledge into practice; without earnestness and steadfastness, one’s practice will be deficient. Thus, among all the excellences of virtue in the world, filial piety and brotherly deference must be embodied in one’s own conduct, rather than merely recited and explained; loyalty and trustworthiness must be put into actual practice, rather than merely discussed. Yet these must also be reinforced by diligence: continuing to act while regarding oneself as not yet capable of acting [?], vigorously encouraging oneself without flagging, and never suffering the fault of advancing impetuously only to retreat swiftly. When one fully accomplishes the work of both knowing and acting, the Way of the gentleman can be fully realized in oneself. Of such a person I know this: being sincere and free of pretense, with his foundations established, he will surely enjoy high esteem, and public opinion will converge upon him. He cannot be compared with those who violate the Way to seek praise. What cause would he have for shame in being called a gentleman? Being abundantly circumspect and generous, with substantial inner virtue, his reputation will surely spread widely, and the judgments of his community will concur in approving him. He cannot be ranked with those who pursue outward appearances and delight in fame. How would he disgrace the name of gentleman?

Ah! A gentleman establishes his reputation precisely by fully realizing the Way through knowing and acting in this manner. How, then, could anyone wishing to learn to become a gentleman seek elsewhere? Knowing and acting are, indeed, the gentleman’s foremost concerns. Viewed from an ordinary perspective, who would not regard them as merely the elementary and immediate activities of a learner? Yet people fail to understand that the steps toward worthiness and the work of becoming a sage all begin here. If one can devote oneself to these without the slightest interruption, one can advance from the elementary to the refined, and from what is near to what is distant. Why worry that one will not reach the same destination as the sages and worthies? Ah! Those resolved to seek the Way should take knowing and acting as their standard.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
昔者舜作五絃之琴以歌南風
考試官教諭范　批〔舜琴制作之工歌詠之美形容殆盡令人讀之不覺一倡三嘆〕
考試官教授田　批〔場中作此題者率多億度於作歌二字處全欠體貼獨此篇考據真切發揮通暢說出虞舜制樂宣詩爲民顒望之意宛然在目〕
姜健表
===
觀前聖之制樂必咏詩以協樂蓋琴乃樂之器
而詩則樂之章也前聖制樂而咏詩以協之寧
不有所爲哉樂記君子謂夫想昔大舜以濬哲
文明之德享揖遜雍熙之治因天瑞之迭應感
臣工之交歡於是表乎一代之制成夫五絃之
琴宮商角徵羽之清濁高下翕然有聲寓其中
雅稱乎嶧桐之裁製也君臣民事物之尊卑大
小隱然有象存其内足備乎虞廷之和鳴也當
斯時也既歌曰南風之薰兮可以解吾民之愠
兮愠以風解蓋將資乾坤景大之氣所以噓拂
punctuated:
昔者舜作五絃之琴，以歌南風。

考試官教諭范　批〔舜琴制作之工，歌詠之美，形容殆盡，令人讀之不覺一倡三嘆。〕

考試官教授田　批〔場中作此題者，率多億度於作歌二字處，全欠體貼。獨此篇考據真切，發揮通暢，說出虞舜制樂宣詩、爲民顒望之意，宛然在目。〕

姜健表

觀前聖之制樂，必咏詩以協樂。蓋琴乃樂之器，而詩則樂之章也。前聖制樂，而咏詩以協之，寧不有所爲哉？《樂記》，君子謂：夫想昔大舜，以濬哲文明之德，享揖遜雍熙之治，因天瑞之迭應，感臣工之交歡，於是表乎一代之制，成夫五絃之琴。宮商角徵羽之清濁高下，翕然有聲寓其中，雅稱乎嶧桐之裁製也；君臣民事物之尊卑大小，隱然有象存其内，足備乎虞廷之和鳴也。當斯時也，既歌曰：「南風之薰兮，可以解吾民之愠兮。」愠以風解，蓋將資乾坤景大之氣，所以噓拂
translation_en:
“In ancient times, Shun made a five-stringed zither to sing the South Wind.”

Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔The craftsmanship of Shun’s zither and the beauty of his singing are described almost exhaustively. Reading this, one cannot help responding to a single song with three sighs of admiration.〕

Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔Most candidates in the examination who addressed this topic merely speculated about the two words “made” and “sang,” entirely failing to appreciate their meaning closely. This essay alone offers precise and sound textual substantiation and develops its argument fluently. It brings vividly before our eyes Yu Shun’s purpose in instituting music and giving voice to poetry, and his earnest hopes for the people.〕

Jiang Jianbiao

When we consider how the sages of old instituted music, we find that they invariably chanted poetry to harmonize with it. For the zither is the instrument of music, while poetry supplies its verses. When the sages of old instituted music and chanted poetry to harmonize with it, could they have done so without a purpose? The gentleman in the Record of Music says [?]: Consider the great Shun of antiquity. Through his profound wisdom and luminous refinement, he enjoyed a reign of concord and prosperity attained through deferential yielding. Responding to Heaven’s successive auspicious signs and moved by the shared joy of his ministers, he established the musical institutions of his age by making the five-stringed zither. The clear and deep, high and low sounds of gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu blended within it, admirably befitting an instrument fashioned from the paulownia of Mount Yi. The relative rank and importance of ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things were subtly represented within it, fully providing for the harmonious music of Shun’s court.

At this time he sang: “The balmy south wind can dispel my people’s resentment.” In dispelling resentment through the wind, he sought to draw upon the vast and mighty vital force of Heaven and Earth, whose breath wafts …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎雖方者欲其潛消乎抑欝而納民於歡暢仁
壽之鄉不但景星呈祥徒起人之鑒賞而已又
歌曰南風之時兮可以阜吾民之財兮以風
阜蓋將藉天地長養之氣所以播盪乎午位者
欲其熙熙相乎品彙而驅民於豐裕飽煖之天不
但卿雲表瑞徒快人之瞻仰而已琴必應歌于
以播絲聲於寫懷之際是非獨樂也一惓惓爲
民之盛心也歌必協琴于以發人聲於宣志之
頃是非自娛也一切切爲民之實意也吁大舜
===
之用歌樂如此此其所以神人以和而超出於
萬物之表也歟抑論之人生天地眇然一身其
形之大小固甚懸絕然亦未始有不相爲流通
者故天地日月星辰四時萬物之理莫不畢備
於吾身人有德者使其一歌而直已以陳之則
天地以應四時以和星辰以理萬物以育自有
不期然而然者矣况乎大舜聖人德盛位尊尚
爾留心於爲民宜乎民樂其樂而有不自知之
者故曰王者之民皡皡如也併而觀之益信
punctuated:
乎雖方者，欲其潛消乎抑欝，而納民於歡暢仁壽之鄉，不但景星呈祥，徒起人之鑒賞而已。又歌曰：「南風之時兮，可以阜吾民之財兮。」以風阜，蓋將藉天地長養之氣，所以播盪乎午位者，欲其熙熙相乎品彙，而驅民於豐裕飽煖之天，不但卿雲表瑞，徒快人之瞻仰而已。琴必應歌，于以播絲聲於寫懷之際，是非獨樂也，一惓惓爲民之盛心也。歌必協琴，于以發人聲於宣志之頃，是非自娛也，一切切爲民之實意也。吁！大舜之用歌樂如此，此其所以神人以和，而超出於萬物之表也歟！
抑論之，人生天地，眇然一身，其形之大小固甚懸絕，然亦未始有不相爲流通者。故天地、日月、星辰、四時、萬物之理，莫不畢備於吾身。人有德者，使其一歌而直已以陳之，則天地以應，四時以和，星辰以理，萬物以育，自有不期然而然者矣。况乎大舜，聖人德盛位尊，尚爾留心於爲民，宜乎民樂其樂，而有不自知之者。故曰：「王者之民皡皡如也。」併而觀之，益信。
translation_en:
…in the quarter designated as “sui” [?], wishing that it might quietly dispel oppression and melancholy and bring the people into a realm of joy, benevolence, and longevity. It was not merely an auspicious star displaying a favorable omen and prompting people’s admiration. He also sang: “When the south wind comes in season, it can increase my people’s wealth.” To bring increase through the wind meant drawing upon the nurturing breath of Heaven and Earth that sweeps through the southern quarter, wishing that it might joyously assist the myriad kinds of things and lead the people into a world of abundance, ample food, and warmth. It was not merely auspicious clouds displaying a favorable portent and delighting those who gazed upward. The zither must answer the song, spreading the sound of its strings as feelings are poured forth. This was no solitary pleasure: it was a great heart devoted earnestly to the people. The song must harmonize with the zither, giving forth the human voice as intentions are declared. This was no self-amusement: it was a sincere and ardent concern for the people. Ah! Such was the great Shun’s use of song and music. Was this not why spirits and people were brought into harmony, and why he rose above all things?
To consider the matter further: a person born between Heaven and Earth is but one tiny body. In physical size, the disparity between them is indeed immense; yet they have never ceased to communicate with one another. Thus the principles of Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, the stars, the four seasons, and the myriad things are all fully present within our own persons. If a person of virtue were to sing a single song, setting himself upright [?] and expressing these principles, Heaven and Earth would respond, the four seasons would harmonize, the stars would follow their proper order, and the myriad things would flourish. Such effects would occur of themselves, without being deliberately sought. How much more so with the great Shun, a sage of abundant virtue and exalted station, who still devoted such care to serving the people! It was fitting that the people should rejoice in his joy without themselves knowing how this came about. Thus it is said: “The people of a true king are broad and untroubled.” Considered together, these things make that saying all the more credible.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
聖人以天下才治天下事
夏良勝
同考試官教諭范　批〔魯齋立言之意本自明白然場中作者多不知旨且剽掠陳言令人厭觀獨此篇深得本旨況下筆滚滚千餘言有議論有波瀾有光燄無一語不自胷中流出真得作論之三昧取冠多士鄉評帖然〕
===
考試官教諭范　批〔此卷三塲俱優而一論命意遣詞尤操縱有法所謂行於其所當行而止於其所當止者吾於子見之得士如此主司寧不爲科目慶哉〕
考試官教授田　批〔一篇平平說去而中間旨趣自高其桂林一枝崑山片玉者歟場中諸士見之當退避三舍明春南宮遝捷而發然出色者余切有望於子〕
論曰有高世之見者必不恃一己之能而
自足以理一世之務焉何則一己之能有
punctuated:
第貳場

論

聖人以天下才治天下事

夏良勝

同考試官教諭范　批〔魯齋立言之意，本自明白。然場中作者多不知旨，且剽掠陳言，令人厭觀。獨此篇深得本旨，況下筆滚滚千餘言，有議論，有波瀾，有光燄，無一語不自胷中流出，真得作論之三昧。取冠多士，鄉評帖然。〕

考試官教諭范　批〔此卷三塲俱優，而一論命意遣詞，尤操縱有法。所謂行於其所當行，而止於其所當止者，吾於子見之。得士如此，主司寧不爲科目慶哉！〕

考試官教授田　批〔一篇平平說去，而中間旨趣自高。其桂林一枝、崑山片玉者歟？場中諸士見之，當退避三舍。明春南宮遝捷，而發然出色者，余切有望於子。〕

論曰：有高世之見者，必不恃一己之能，而自足以理一世之務焉。何則？一己之能有
translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse

The Sage Employs the Talents of All under Heaven to Govern the Affairs of All under Heaven

Xia Liangsheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔The intention behind Luzhai’s statement is perfectly clear in itself. title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
限而一世之務無窮以有限應無窮難矣
人惟不見其難則將恃一已之能而緦緦
然欲以理一世之務吾知其徒敝精神而
無益矣惟夫聖人有高世之見則必不恃
一已之能而用一世之能以中以公無人
我無作爲則自足以理一世之務而不見
其難矣此聖人之所以爲聖人豈常人之
所可及哉先儒許衡有見於此而曰聖人
以天下〻〻治天下事夫天下舉一世而言
===
聖人則人之至而才者人之能也有一家
之事有一國之事有天下之事巨者細者
精者粗者紛紛藉藉日至乎吾前者此天
下之事也我能之人亦能之一已能之一
世亦能之有自然而無勉强者此天下之
才也聖人生而知安而行五百年而一出
億萬人而一人此所以爲人之至也惟夫
聖人有高天下之見以中道以公道無我
無人無作爲以天下之才治天下之事因
punctuated: 限，而一世之務無窮，以有限應無窮，難矣！人惟不見其難，則將恃一已之能，而緦緦然欲以理一世之務，吾知其徒敝精神而無益矣。惟夫聖人有高世之見，則必不恃一已之能，而用一世之能，以中以公，無人我，無作爲，則自足以理一世之務，而不見其難矣。此聖人之所以爲聖人，豈常人之所可及哉？先儒許衡有見於此，而曰：「聖人以天下〻〻治天下事。」夫天下，舉一世而言；聖人，則人之至；而才者，人之能也。有一家之事，有一國之事，有天下之事，巨者細者，精者粗者，紛紛藉藉，日至乎吾前者，此天下之事也。我能之，人亦能之；一已能之，一世亦能之。有自然而無勉强者，此天下之才也。聖人生而知，安而行，五百年而一出，億萬人而一人，此所以爲人之至也。惟夫聖人有高天下之見，以中道，以公道，無我無人，無作爲，以天下之才治天下之事，因
translation_en:
…is limited, whereas the affairs of an age are inexhaustible. To meet the inexhaustible with what is limited is difficult indeed! Only because people fail to perceive this difficulty do they rely on their own abilities and, engrossed in their efforts [?], seek to manage all the affairs of an age. I know that they merely exhaust their mental energies to no benefit. The sage alone possesses insight surpassing his age. He therefore never relies solely on his own abilities, but employs the abilities of the whole age. Through balance and impartiality, making no distinction between others and himself and engaging in no contrived action, he is fully able to manage the affairs of an age without finding them difficult. This is what makes the sage a sage. How could ordinary people attain it? The earlier Confucian scholar Xu Heng perceived this and said: “The sage uses the talents of all under Heaven [?] to govern the affairs of all under Heaven.”

“All under Heaven” refers comprehensively to the entire age; a “sage” is the highest realization of humanity; and “talent” means human ability. There are the affairs of a household, the affairs of a state, and the affairs of all under Heaven: great and small, subtle and coarse, coming before us daily in bewildering profusion. These are the affairs of all under Heaven. What I can do, others can also do; what one individual can do, people throughout the age can also do. Such abilities arise naturally, without forced effort: these are the talents of all under Heaven. The sage knows from birth and acts with ease. He appears once in five hundred years, one person among countless millions. This is why he represents the highest realization of humanity. The sage alone possesses insight surpassing all under Heaven. Following the way of balance and the way of impartiality, making no distinction between self and others and engaging in no contrived action, he uses the talents of all under Heaven to govern the affairs of all under Heaven, drawing upon…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
才以治其事隨事以應其才而已抑何容
心哉自夫天下有智者出則見其才之敏
而恃之以治天下之事矣有勇者出則見
其才之雄而恃之以治天下之事矣有巧
者出則見其才之奇而恃之以治天下之
事矣天下之智者勇者巧者各恃其一已
之□以治一世之事甚至治一事也輒分
人我設□倒如而治人何如而治藐一世
之人以爲不我若而凡事矯揉造作一任
===
其已私爲之天下之事本易也而執之使
難天下之事本卑也而抗之使高天下之
事本淺也而鑿之使深縱横繆戾紛紜舛
錯非惟不足以治天下之事而反有以敗
天下之事矣惟夫聖人之才未嘗不敏也
才敏而不恃有以高天下智者之見矣未
嘗不雄也才雄而不恃有以高天下勇者
之見矣未嘗不奇也才奇而不恃有以高
天下巧者之見矣灼見夫有天下之事必
punctuated:
才以治其事，隨事以應其才而已，抑何容心哉？自夫天下有智者出，則見其才之敏，而恃之以治天下之事矣；有勇者出，則見其才之雄，而恃之以治天下之事矣；有巧者出，則見其才之奇，而恃之以治天下之事矣。天下之智者、勇者、巧者，各恃其一已之□，以治一世之事，甚至治一事也，輒分人我，設□倒如而治，人何如而治，藐一世之人，以爲不我若，而凡事矯揉造作，一任其已私爲之。天下之事本易也，而執之使難；天下之事本卑也，而抗之使高；天下之事本淺也，而鑿之使深。縱横繆戾，紛紜舛錯，非惟不足以治天下之事，而反有以敗天下之事矣。
惟夫聖人之才，未嘗不敏也，才敏而不恃，有以高天下智者之見矣；未嘗不雄也，才雄而不恃，有以高天下勇者之見矣；未嘗不奇也，才奇而不恃，有以高天下巧者之見矣。灼見夫有天下之事，必
translation_en:
…according to their abilities, to manage the affairs suited to them, and to match abilities to affairs as circumstances require—that is all. What room is there for imposing one's own intentions? When an intelligent man emerges in the world, he recognizes the quickness of his abilities and relies on it to manage the world's affairs. When a courageous man emerges, he recognizes the strength of his abilities and relies on it to manage the world's affairs. When a skillful man emerges, he recognizes the ingenuity of his abilities and relies on it to manage the world's affairs. The intelligent, courageous, and skillful each rely on their own individual [?] to manage the affairs of an entire age. Even in managing a single affair, they immediately distinguish between others and themselves, setting up [?] ways of governing and asking how others govern [?]. They disdain the people of their age, considering them inferior to themselves, and handle everything with contrivance and artifice, giving free rein to their own selfish wishes. The world's affairs are inherently easy, yet their rigid grasp makes them difficult; inherently lowly, yet they raise them up high; inherently shallow, yet they dig into them and make them deep. With confusion and perversity in every direction, with disorder and error everywhere, they are not merely incapable of managing the world's affairs: they actually bring those affairs to ruin.
The sage's abilities, by contrast, have never lacked quickness. Yet he does not rely presumptuously on that quickness, and thus his insight surpasses that of the world's intelligent men. His abilities have never lacked strength. Yet he does not rely presumptuously on that strength, and thus his insight surpasses that of the world's courageous men. His abilities have never lacked ingenuity. Yet he does not rely presumptuously on that ingenuity, and thus his insight surpasses that of the world's skillful men. He clearly perceives that, wherever there are affairs in the world, there must…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
有天下之才人之所爲即我之所爲也而
人與我之何分事之所在即才之所在也
而才與事之何間操事之柄運才之用爛
熟於胷中而流動於施爲之間一本之中
道而已何偏之有一本之公道而已何私
之有一本之自然而已何矯揉造作之有
故不恃一已之才治天下之事必以天下
之才治天下之事而天下之事眞見其有
不難治矣盍不觀諸舜禹乎天下之事莫
大於治曆舜不恃已之才治曆而察璣衡
政以曆之才治曆曆之事治矣若夫何承
天之所爲則非惟不足以治曆而反有以
惑於世可乎天下之事莫難於治水禹不
恃已之才治水而順性殺勢以水之才治
水水之事治矣若夫白圭之所爲則非惟
不足以治水而反有以病於隣可乎遠考
二聖下俟百世則夫聖人治天下之事何
嘗有外於天下之才哉抑何嘗恃乎一已
punctuated: 有天下之才。人之所爲，即我之所爲也，而人與我之何分？事之所在，即才之所在也，而才與事之何間？操事之柄，運才之用，爛熟於胷中，而流動於施爲之間，一本之中道而已，何偏之有？一本之公道而已，何私之有？一本之自然而已，何矯揉造作之有？故不恃一已之才治天下之事，必以天下之才治天下之事，而天下之事眞見其有不難治矣。盍不觀諸舜禹乎？天下之事莫大於治曆，舜不恃已之才治曆，而察璣衡政，以曆之才治曆，曆之事治矣。若夫何承天之所爲，則非惟不足以治曆，而反有以惑於世，可乎？天下之事莫難於治水，禹不恃已之才治水，而順性殺勢，以水之才治水，水之事治矣。若夫白圭之所爲，則非惟不足以治水，而反有以病於隣，可乎？遠考二聖，下俟百世，則夫聖人治天下之事，何嘗有外於天下之才哉？抑何嘗恃乎一已
translation_en: …there must be capacities throughout the world to meet them. What others do is what I do: what distinction is there between others and myself? Wherever there are affairs, there are capacities to address them: what separation is there between capacities and affairs? Holding the reins of affairs and bringing capacities into use, the sage has thoroughly mastered these within his breast, and they flow freely through his actions. He grounds everything in the balanced Way: what partiality could there be? He grounds everything in the impartial Way: what selfishness could there be? He grounds everything in what is natural: what contrivance or artificiality could there be? Thus he does not rely on his own capacities alone to manage the world's affairs, but necessarily employs the capacities of the whole world to manage them. Then it truly becomes apparent that the world's affairs need not be difficult to manage. Why not consider Shun and Yu? Among the world's affairs, none is greater than regulating the calendar. Shun did not rely on his own capacities to regulate it, but examined the astronomical instruments [?]. By using the capacities inherent in calendrical phenomena to regulate the calendar, he brought calendrical affairs into order. As for what He Chengtian did, it was not merely inadequate to regulate the calendar, but instead served to mislead the world. Could that be acceptable? Among the world's affairs, none is more difficult than controlling water. Yu did not rely on his own capacities to control water, but followed its nature and diminished its force. By using water's own capacities to control water, he brought water management into order. As for what Bai Gui did, it was not merely inadequate to control water, but instead brought harm to neighboring states. Could that be acceptable? Looking far back to examine these two sages, and awaiting the judgment of a hundred generations to come, when has the sage's management of the world's affairs ever gone beyond the capacities of the world? Or when has he ever relied on his own alone…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之才哉如天下之事有禮樂焉能序能和
者天下禮樂之才也聖人以天下禮樂之
才治天下禮樂之事何容心於禮樂乎天
下之事有政刑焉能脩能明者天下政刑
之才也聖人以天下政刑之才治天下政
刑之事何容心於政刑乎天下之事有甲
兵焉而能致其堅利有錢穀焉而能謹於
出納天下甲兵錢穀之才也聖人以天下
甲兵錢穀之才治天下甲兵錢穀之事何
容心於甲兵錢穀乎以至治一事以一事
===
之才治萬事以萬事之才而巨細精粗莫
不皆然人見其天下之事熈熈然莫不就
治以爲聖人之才有以治之也而不知聖
人治之以天下之才一中道自然應之而
已人見其天下之事秩秩然莫不嚮治以
爲聖人之才有以治之也而不知聖人治
之以天下之才一公道自然應之而已此
聖人之見所以爲獨髙於一世之見而非
punctuated: 之才哉？如天下之事有禮樂焉，能序能和者，天下禮樂之才也。聖人以天下禮樂之才，治天下禮樂之事，何容心於禮樂乎？天下之事有政刑焉，能脩能明者，天下政刑之才也。聖人以天下政刑之才，治天下政刑之事，何容心於政刑乎？天下之事有甲兵焉，而能致其堅利；有錢穀焉，而能謹於出納：天下甲兵錢穀之才也。聖人以天下甲兵錢穀之才，治天下甲兵錢穀之事，何容心於甲兵錢穀乎？以至治一事以一事之才，治萬事以萬事之才，而巨細精粗，莫不皆然。人見其天下之事熈熈然莫不就治，以爲聖人之才有以治之也，而不知聖人治之以天下之才，一中道自然應之而已。人見其天下之事秩秩然莫不嚮治，以爲聖人之才有以治之也，而不知聖人治之以天下之才，一公道自然應之而已。此聖人之見所以爲獨髙於一世之見，而非
translation_en: …his own abilities? Among the affairs of the world, for example, are rites and music. The capacity to establish order and produce harmony is the inherent capacity of rites and music throughout the world. The sage uses these capacities to manage the affairs of rites and music throughout the world. What need has he to impose his own intentions upon them? Among the affairs of the world are government and punishments. The capacity to bring good order and clarity is the inherent capacity of government and punishments throughout the world. The sage uses these capacities to manage the affairs of government and punishments throughout the world. What need has he to impose his own intentions upon them? Among the affairs of the world are armor and weapons, which can be made sturdy and sharp, and money and grain, whose receipt and disbursement can be carefully managed: these are the capacities pertaining to armor and weapons, money and grain throughout the world. The sage uses these capacities to manage their corresponding affairs. What need has he to impose his own intentions upon armor and weapons, money and grain? Thus he manages a single affair through the capacity appropriate to that affair, and the myriad affairs through the capacities appropriate to them. Whether great or small, refined or coarse, all are handled in this way. People see the affairs of the world flourishing, all brought into good order, and suppose that the sage’s own abilities have sufficed to govern them. They do not understand that the sage governs them through the capacities of the world, simply responding to them spontaneously through the single principle of the Mean. People see the affairs of the world proceeding in orderly fashion, all tending toward good order, and suppose that the sage’s own abilities have sufficed to govern them. They do not understand that the sage governs them through the capacities of the world, simply responding to them spontaneously through the single principle of impartiality. This is why the sage’s insight stands uniquely above the insight of his age, and is not…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
常人之所能及也歟雖然治事而本乎中
公者固聖人之恒事治事而造乎精微者
實聖人之能事恒事人之所可及
而能事抑豈常人之所可企而及之哉故
曰聖人人之至也嗚呼泰山北斗爲世具
瞻景星鳳凰天下快覩草野之士俾得立
玉階寸地侍
丹扆一班尚當以許衡之言爲今日
聖天子頌謹論
===
表
擬纂修
孝宗敬皇帝實錄成
進呈表
同考試官教諭范　批〔表語不專尚乎纖麗而〕
鋪張
神功聖德歷歷可紀非究心於
昭代之事業者不能故録之以爲作四六者式
punctuated:
常人之所能及也歟？雖然，治事而本乎中公者，固聖人之恒事；治事而造乎精微者，實聖人之能事。恒事，人之所可及，而能事抑豈常人之所可企而及之哉？故曰：「聖人，人之至也。」嗚呼！泰山北斗，爲世具瞻；景星鳳凰，天下快覩。草野之士，俾得立玉階寸地，侍丹扆一班，尚當以許衡之言爲今日聖天子頌。謹論。

表

擬纂修《孝宗敬皇帝實錄》成進呈表

同考試官教諭范，批〔表語不專尚乎纖麗而〕鋪張神功聖德，歷歷可紀。非究心於昭代之事業者不能，故録之以爲作四六者式。
translation_en:
…within the reach of ordinary people? Nevertheless, to conduct affairs on the basis of centrality and impartiality is the sage’s habitual practice; to conduct affairs with the utmost refinement and subtlety is the sage’s distinctive accomplishment. Habitual practice is something others can attain, but how could ordinary people hope to reach such accomplishment? Thus it is said: “The sage is the highest realization of humanity.” Ah! Like Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper, he is looked up to by all the world; like an auspicious star and a phoenix, he is joyfully beheld by all under Heaven. Were a scholar from the countryside such as myself allowed even a foot of space upon the jade steps and a place among those attending the imperial throne, I would offer Xu Heng’s words in praise of the sage Son of Heaven of our own day. Respectfully submitted as a discourse.

Memorial

A hypothetical memorial presenting the completed compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Xiaozong Jing.

Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔The language of this memorial does not prize delicate elegance alone, but〕 expansively sets forth the divine achievements and sagely virtue, recording them distinctly, one by one. Only someone who has devoted careful attention to the accomplishments of this illustrious reign could achieve this. I have therefore recorded it here as a model for writers of four-and-six parallel prose.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭范　批〔渾厚典雅可嘉〕

撰乾闡坤萬世仰
聖神之德業
繼離出震四方瞻

而文謨斯顯顧事功莫盛於
先帝但揄揚尤賴於
===

玉牒雲裁恭惟
孝宗建天明道誠純中正聖文神武至仁大德
敬皇帝

translation_en:
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: 〔Commendable for its substantial, restrained, and classically elegant style.〕
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔It achieves the style of parallel prose.〕
We humbly submit: Giving expression to Heaven and elucidating Earth [?], his sagely and divine virtue and achievements command the admiration of ten thousand generations; continuing the radiance of Li and emerging in Zhen, the successor draws the gaze of the four quarters to the splendor of his continuation and creation. For when Shun’s virtue accorded with Yao’s, the Canon of Yao was completed; when King Wu’s glorious achievements were carried forward, King Wen’s counsels were thereby made manifest. Indeed, no achievements surpass those of the late emperor, yet their celebration depends especially upon his imperial successor. Truly, this is a book for an entire reign, serving to make plain a mirror for a hundred kings. The metal-bound coffer is opened by Heaven; the jade records are fashioned from clouds.
We reverently reflect upon Xiaozong, the Reverent Emperor, who Established Heaven and Made Manifest the Way, was Sincere and Pure, Central and Correct, Sagely in Civil Accomplishment and Divine in Martial Prowess, Supremely Benevolent and Great in Virtue. His dragon virtue stood at the sun’s zenith; his phoenix bearing displayed Heaven’s majesty. The year that inaugurated the Hongzhi era corresponded to the year when the Hongwu Emperor ascended the throne. His learning fathomed the imperial exemplar [?], and he grasped the essential Way transmitted from mind to mind among emperors and kings; ascending the great throne, he upheld…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗保治之弘規寡慾清心聲色不邇凝神合
道輿馬不親昭格一誠重感通於
郊祀日勤三至隆孝養於
慈宮集
大明會典之書人文丕著修宣尼闕里之廟儒
道攸崇竄方士斥緇流屏息乎邪術建
王封定
廟制篤厚乎彝倫非惟文事之留心抑且武功
之注意
===
天兵一臨而南蠻就殄
王師再舉而北虜成擒四海九州悉歌詠於鳳
儀獸舞之内普天率土咸樂育於鳶飛魚
躍之中及夫
在御日深閱世滋久
臨朝歲晚保治彌堅心切忠賢俯勞乎
清問
躬親刑賞大奮乎
乾剛如我
punctuated: 祖宗保治之弘規。寡慾清心，聲色不邇；凝神合道，輿馬不親。昭格一誠，重感通於郊祀；日勤三至，隆孝養於慈宮。集《大明會典》之書，人文丕著；修宣尼闕里之廟，儒道攸崇。竄方士，斥緇流，屏息乎邪術；建王封，定廟制，篤厚乎彝倫。非惟文事之留心，抑且武功之注意。天兵一臨，而南蠻就殄；王師再舉，而北虜成擒。四海九州，悉歌詠於鳳儀獸舞之内；普天率土，咸樂育於鳶飛魚躍之中。及夫在御日深，閱世滋久，臨朝歲晚，保治彌堅。心切忠賢，俯勞乎清問；躬親刑賞，大奮乎乾剛。如我
translation_en: …the grand principles by which his ancestors preserved good government. He restrained his desires and purified his mind, keeping away from sensual music and beauty; he concentrated his spirit and accorded with the Way, taking no pleasure in carriages and horses. With wholehearted sincerity he reached the spirits, placing great weight on communion with them in the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. Diligently making three visits each day, he showed the utmost filial care at the palace of the empress dowager. He compiled the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian), bringing civil culture into brilliant prominence; he restored the temple of Confucius at Queli, exalting the Confucian Way. He banished masters of esoteric arts and expelled Buddhist monks, suppressing heterodox practices; he established princely enfeoffments and settled the regulations for ancestral temples, strengthening the constant bonds of human relations. He devoted his attention not only to civil affairs but also to military achievements. When the imperial troops advanced, the southern barbarians were annihilated; when the royal army marched again, the northern foes were taken captive. Throughout the Four Seas and Nine Provinces, all sang praises amid harmony such as that in which phoenixes appeared and beasts danced; everywhere under Heaven and throughout the land, all delighted in being nurtured, like kites soaring and fish leaping. As his reign lengthened and his experience of the world deepened, in his later years at court he grew ever more resolute in preserving good government. Deeply concerned for loyal and worthy men, he graciously exerted himself in enlightened inquiry; personally overseeing punishments and rewards, he vigorously exercised the firm authority of Heaven. Such was our…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
孝宗皇帝者誠大有爲之君而真不世出之主
也豈意
宮車晏駕臣民慟切於烏號幸而
神器早歸宇宙喜登於黃道仰惟
皇上軫諒陰之慼與繼述之懷渙發
綸音特頒
温詔謂大孝在顯親必有昭示而信史貴傳
遠當謹編摩簡勳戚以監修集儒臣而纂
錄筆札給
===
上方之具膳羞供
御府之珍事跡每貫於討論義例一遵乎
指授言足爲法繁簡不遺事有可師巨細必
載一十八年之政煥若日星百千萬卷之
文浩如烟海事皆錄實書匪傳疑〔臣〕等身
覲
日華面承
天語班聯玉筍愧乏遷固之長才籍占金閨希
效左狐之直筆飲江河雖滿其腹繪
punctuated:
孝宗皇帝者，誠大有爲之君，而真不世出之主也。豈意宮車晏駕，臣民慟切於烏號！幸而神器早歸，宇宙喜登於黃道。仰惟皇上軫諒陰之慼與繼述之懷，渙發綸音，特頒温詔，謂大孝在顯親，必有昭示，而信史貴傳遠，當謹編摩。簡勳戚以監修，集儒臣而纂錄。筆札給上方之具，膳羞供御府之珍。事跡每貫於討論，義例一遵乎指授。言足爲法，繁簡不遺；事有可師，巨細必載。一十八年之政，煥若日星；百千萬卷之文，浩如烟海。事皆錄實，書匪傳疑。
〔臣〕等身覲日華，面承天語。班聯玉筍，愧乏遷固之長才；籍占金閨，希效左狐之直筆。飲江河雖滿其腹，繪
translation_en:
…Emperor Xiaozong was indeed a sovereign of great accomplishment, truly a ruler such as rarely appears in the world. Who could have imagined that the imperial carriage would depart so late—His Majesty passing away—and that officials and people would grieve as bitterly as those who cried after the departed Yellow Emperor! Fortunately, the sacred vessel of sovereignty soon found its rightful holder, and all beneath heaven rejoiced at the auspicious imperial accession.
We reverently consider how Your Majesty, moved by the grief of mourning and the desire to carry forward your predecessor’s work, issued your imperial words far and wide and specially promulgated a gracious edict. It declared that the highest filial piety lies in making one’s parent illustrious, which requires a manifest record, and that trustworthy history is prized for its transmission to distant generations, so its compilation must be undertaken with care. You selected meritorious nobles and imperial relatives to supervise the compilation and assembled scholarly officials to compile the record. Brushes and writing materials were supplied from the imperial workshops, and meals furnished with delicacies from the palace stores. The events were continually examined through discussion [?], and the principles and conventions of compilation followed your instructions throughout. Words worthy of serving as standards were omitted neither for their length nor their brevity; deeds that offered lessons were invariably recorded, whether great or small. The government of eighteen years shines like the sun and stars; the writings in hundreds, thousands, and myriads of volumes stretch as vast as a sea of mist. Every event is recorded truthfully; the history does not transmit doubtful accounts.
We, your servants, have personally beheld the imperial radiance and received your august words face to face. Ranked among the worthy courtiers, arrayed like jade shoots, we are ashamed to lack the great talents of Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Our names entered among the palace officials, we hope to emulate the uncompromising pens of Zuo and Hu [?]. Though drinking from the rivers may fill our bellies, to depict …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天地固難爲容幸覩成編恭呈
睿覽
九重罔極之恩斯慰百世不刊之典以成伏願
不愆不忘等弦韋於簡冊是儀是式弘熙
皞於家邦臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表隨
進以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官訓導吳　批〔五策皆條答而此篇揄揚我〕
文皇心學之製尤爲詳整他日
大廷之對吁
閶闔而呈琅玕者端有望於子
punctuated:
天地，固難爲容。幸覩成編，恭呈睿覽。九重罔極之恩斯慰，百世不刊之典以成。伏願不愆不忘，等弦韋於簡冊；是儀是式，弘熙皞於家邦。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表隨進以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
同考試官訓導吳　批〔五策皆條答，而此篇揄揚我〕文皇心學之製，尤爲詳整。他日大廷之對，吁閶闔而呈琅玕者，端有望於子。
translation_en:
…Heaven and Earth—it is indeed difficult to depict their full form. Fortunate to behold the completed compilation, we respectfully submit it for Your Majesty’s perusal. Thus may we requite the boundless grace of the imperial throne and complete an authoritative record that will remain unaltered for a hundred generations. We humbly wish that, by neither erring nor forgetting, Your Majesty may find in these written records the admonitory guidance of bowstring and leather; and, taking them as a standard and model, may extend radiant harmony throughout the dynasty and realm. Your servants, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your sacred person, are overwhelmed with fervent emotion and reverent trepidation. We respectfully submit this memorial together with the compilation for Your Majesty’s attention.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Assistant Instructor: 〔All five policy essays answer the questions point by point, but this essay’s praise of our〕 Emperor Wen’s work on the learning of the mind is especially detailed and well ordered. In a future response at the imperial court, we may indeed look to you to call at the gates of Heaven and present precious jade—that is, to offer worthy counsel to the throne.
