Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: 〔Skillful in expansive exposition.〕 … This essay is especially fine [?]. Among the many candidates in the autumn examination, it should place you a head above the rest.

Imperial compositions, blossoms of heaven, shine forth between Heaven and Earth, and thus the work Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) was composed. Lustrous volumes and precious scrolls [?] spread throughout the realm, and thus the book Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning was transmitted. For in the learning pursued by sage kings, nothing is more essential than the methods of the mind. Yet without its composition in earlier times, however admirable it might be [?], how could it be transmitted? Without its transmission to later generations, however splendid it might be, how could it become manifest? I respectfully received the policy questions that you, honored examiners, issued for the autumn examination, taking first as your subject …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
太宗文皇帝所製聖學心法爲問大哉問乎愚
生不敏敢不敬述以對粤自聖王心學之
傳其來尚矣堯之授舜曰允執厥中舜之
授禹曰惟精惟一蓋中者不偏不倚無過
不及原於天命而見於人心必精以察夫
理欲之辨必一以全其本體之真則所謂
中者其庶幾矣乎自古聖王之言心學莫
加於此爲君而不知此則失其所以爲君
爲臣而不知此則失其所以爲臣第作於
===
前者欲以傳於後何自成周以下杳乎其
未聞也如高祖之歌大風武帝之詠天馬
氣亦雄矣然一則尚威猛而殊無和平之
氣象一則内多欲而徒施仁義之美觀其
戾於中者亦夥矣安在其有關於心學乎
太宗之著帝範真宗之論崇儒詞亦偉矣
然一則言若可取而行甘天倫之瀆一則
名雖可尚而心信天書之詐其叛於中者
亦多矣尚望其有補於心學乎
punctuated: 太宗文皇帝所製《聖學心法》爲問，大哉問乎！愚生不敏，敢不敬述以對？粤自聖王心學之傳，其來尚矣。堯之授舜曰：「允執厥中。」舜之授禹曰：「惟精惟一。」蓋中者，不偏不倚，無過不及，原於天命而見於人心。必精以察夫理欲之辨，必一以全其本體之真，則所謂中者，其庶幾矣乎！自古聖王之言心學，莫加於此。爲君而不知此，則失其所以爲君；爲臣而不知此，則失其所以爲臣。第作於前者，欲以傳於後，何自成周以下，杳乎其未聞也？如高祖之歌《大風》，武帝之詠《天馬》，氣亦雄矣。然一則尚威猛，而殊無和平之氣象；一則内多欲，而徒施仁義之美觀。其戾於中者亦夥矣，安在其有關於心學乎？太宗之著《帝範》，真宗之論《崇儒》，詞亦偉矣。然一則言若可取，而行甘天倫之瀆；一則名雖可尚，而心信天書之詐。其叛於中者亦多矣，尚望其有補於心學乎？
translation_en:
…made the Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa), composed by Emperor Taizong Wen, the subject of your question. How momentous a question! Though I, an unworthy student, am slow of understanding, dare I fail to offer a respectful account in reply? The transmission of the sage-kings’ learning of the mind has a long history indeed. Yao instructed Shun, saying, “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean.” Shun instructed Yu, saying, “Be discerning; be single-minded.” The Mean inclines to neither side and admits neither excess nor deficiency; it originates in Heaven’s mandate and manifests itself in the human mind. One must be discerning to perceive the distinction between principle and desire, and single-minded to preserve intact the true original substance of the mind. Only then may one approach what is called the Mean! Nothing the sage-kings have said since antiquity about the learning of the mind surpasses this. A ruler who does not understand it loses that by which he is a ruler; a minister who does not understand it loses that by which he is a minister. Yet what was set forth by earlier sages was intended for transmission to later generations. Why, then, has scarcely anything been heard of it since the Zhou dynasty?

Consider Gaozu’s Song of the Great Wind and Wudi’s ode to the Heavenly Horse: their spirit was certainly heroic. Yet the former exalted martial might and entirely lacked an air of peace and harmony; the latter harbored many desires within and merely made an attractive outward display of benevolence and righteousness. Their departures from the Mean were numerous indeed. How could these works have any bearing on the learning of the mind? Taizong’s composition of the Model for Emperors (Difan) and Zhenzong’s discourse on Exalting Confucian Learning were likewise grand in their language. Yet the former’s words might seem worthy of adoption, while in his conduct he willingly violated the natural bonds of kinship; the latter’s professed purpose might be admirable, while in his heart he believed the fraudulent heavenly writings. Their deviations from the Mean were also numerous. Could one still hope that their works would contribute to the learning of the mind?

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天啓
皇明文運亨泰肆惟我
太宗文皇帝德由天縱學本日新
萬幾之暇
親灑宸翰製爲聖學心法一書叙古帝王心學
之要至詳且備固非諸生風簷寸晷之下
所能殫述請舉其大者言之伏覩
聖製所載君道之大者有四不過乎曰敬天曰
法祖曰用人曰理財四事而已臣道之大
===
者亦有四不過乎曰忠曰勤曰廉曰謹四
德而已蓋人君之所畏者天故著欽崇天
道永保天命之說人君之所嗣者祖故示
監于成憲其永無愆之言三德有家而六
德有邦用人之要法也庶土交征而三壤
咸則理財之令典也君之道不止於此而
此非其大者乎人臣當致身而欲其如易
之匪躬人臣當效勞而欲其如詩之匪懈
惟貨其吉貪饕之戒昭如也居寵思辱謹
punctuated:
天啓皇明，文運亨泰。肆惟我太宗文皇帝，德由天縱，學本日新。萬幾之暇，親灑宸翰，製爲《聖學心法》一書，叙古帝王心學之要，至詳且備，固非諸生風簷寸晷之下所能殫述。請舉其大者言之。伏覩聖製所載，君道之大者有四，不過乎曰敬天、曰法祖、曰用人、曰理財四事而已。臣道之大者亦有四，不過乎曰忠、曰勤、曰廉、曰謹四德而已。
蓋人君之所畏者天，故著「欽崇天道，永保天命」之說；人君之所嗣者祖，故示「監于成憲，其永無愆」之言。「三德有家，而六德有邦」，用人之要法也；「庶土交征，而三壤咸則」，理財之令典也。君之道不止於此，而此非其大者乎？人臣當致身，而欲其如《易》之「匪躬」；人臣當效勞，而欲其如《詩》之「匪懈」。「惟貨其吉」，貪饕之戒昭如也；「居寵思辱」，謹
translation_en:
Heaven inaugurated our august Ming, and literary accomplishment flourished. Our Emperor Taizong Wen, endowed by Heaven with virtue, grounded his learning in daily renewal. In moments of leisure amid the myriad affairs of government, he personally wielded the imperial brush to compose the Essential Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa). Its exposition of the essentials of the ancient emperors’ and kings’ learning of the mind is exceedingly detailed and comprehensive. Certainly we examination candidates, beneath these wind-swept eaves and with so little time, cannot exhaustively recount it. Allow me to discuss its principal points. Humbly reading this imperial composition, I find four principal aspects of the ruler’s way: revering Heaven, emulating the ancestors, employing men, and managing wealth. There are likewise four principal aspects of the minister’s way: loyalty, diligence, integrity, and circumspection.
What the ruler holds in awe is Heaven; hence the work sets forth the teaching, “Reverently honor Heaven’s way and preserve Heaven’s mandate forever.” Those whom the ruler succeeds are his ancestors; hence it offers the injunction, “Look to the established statutes, and you will forever be without fault.” “Those possessing three virtues may govern a household, and those possessing six virtues may govern a state”: this is an essential rule for employing men. “The various lands contribute their levies, and the three grades of soil all follow their prescribed assessments”: this is an excellent standard for managing wealth. The ruler’s way extends beyond these matters, but are these not its principal aspects? A minister should devote himself utterly to service, aspiring to the Book of Changes’ ideal of “taking no thought for oneself.” A minister should expend his efforts in service, aspiring to the Book of Odes’ ideal of “never flagging.” “Wealth alone brings good fortune”: the warning against avarice is manifest. “While enjoying favor, think of disgrace”: the instruction on cautious…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
飭之訓煥如也臣之道不止於此而此非
其大者乎堯舜之言簡而約蓋以總其綱
文皇之言詳而博蓋以著其目心法之要信乎
蔑以加矣夫作於後者必有啓於先何自
勝國以前茫乎其未見也漢唐宋英君誼
辟若高祖太宗藝祖亦有可稱者惜其於
心學之傳槩未之聞故大綱正者或失其
用萬目舉者或遺其體僅能綱舉目張者
或未造其極君道非不能行但行之而不
===
純耳不然則治世之休當不減於唐虞矣
名臣碩輔若蕭曹房杜韓范亦有可紀者
惜其心學之傳畧不之講故建治功者或
雜於術䇿勞勩者或離於正飭行檢巖操
持者或不免於才臣道非不能盡但盡之
而未善耳不然則致君之績當不下於皐
夔矣於戲
典則之貽貴有得於身心治理之效實有賴
於纘述惟我
punctuated:
飭之訓煥如也。臣之道不止於此，而此非其大者乎？堯舜之言簡而約，蓋以總其綱；文皇之言詳而博，蓋以著其目。心法之要，信乎蔑以加矣！夫作於後者，必有啓於先，何自勝國以前，茫乎其未見也？漢唐宋英君誼辟，若高祖、太宗、藝祖，亦有可稱者，惜其於心學之傳，槩未之聞。故大綱正者，或失其用；萬目舉者，或遺其體；僅能綱舉目張者，或未造其極。君道非不能行，但行之而不純耳。不然，則治世之休，當不減於唐虞矣。
名臣碩輔，若蕭、曹、房、杜、韓、范，亦有可紀者，惜其心學之傳，畧不之講。故建治功者，或雜於術；䇿勞勩者，或離於正；飭行檢、巖操持者，或不免於才。臣道非不能盡，但盡之而未善耳。不然，則致君之績，當不下於皐、夔矣。於戲！典則之貽，貴有得於身心；治理之效，實有賴於纘述。惟我
translation_en:
…the instruction to exercise care and self-discipline shines forth clearly. The way of a minister extends beyond these things, but are these not its principal concerns? The words of Yao and Shun are brief and concise, serving to gather together the main principles; the words of Emperor Wen are detailed and extensive, serving to set out their particulars. Truly, nothing could surpass this distillation of the essential teaching of the mind! Now, whatever arises later must have had some antecedent inspiration. Why, then, is there scarcely any trace of this before and during the preceding dynasty? Among the outstanding rulers and righteous sovereigns of the Han, Tang, and Song, such as Gaozu, Taizong, and Yizu, there were indeed men worthy of praise. Regrettably, they had generally never heard of the transmission of the learning of the mind. Thus, those who set the main principles right sometimes failed in their application; those who attended to the myriad particulars sometimes neglected the underlying substance; and those who just managed to establish the principles and set out the particulars sometimes failed to reach the highest attainment. It was not that they could not practice the way of the ruler, but that their practice was not pure. Otherwise, the excellence of their orderly reigns should have been no less than that of Tang and Yu—the ages of Yao and Shun.
Among celebrated ministers and eminent counsellors, such as Xiao He, Cao Shen, Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Han Qi, and Fan Zhongyan, there were also men whose deeds deserve recording. Regrettably, they scarcely studied the transmission of the learning of the mind. Thus, those who achieved good government sometimes mingled their work with expedient techniques; those who exerted themselves in arduous service [?] sometimes departed from what was right; and those who disciplined their conduct and held firmly to their principles sometimes remained confined to mere talent [?]. It was not that they could not fulfill the way of the minister, but that their fulfillment of it was not yet good. Otherwise, their achievements in bringing their sovereigns to excellence should have been no less than those of Gao Yao and Kui. Ah! The value of bequeathing standards and rules lies in their being personally assimilated in body and mind; the efficacy of government truly depends on carrying forward and elaborating what has been handed down. It is our…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
列聖躬行於上群臣效法於下四海承平百有
餘年寔我
文皇貽謀之善有以啓之也大哉堯言萬世之
如見卓乎周禮千古之所崇愚生竊伏草
茅莊誦
聖製爲有年矣謹撫其槩以復執事儻不鄙而
與進之俾得對于
帝庭尚當以洋洋之
聖謨爲我
===
明天子獻
第二問
同考試官訓導陳　批〔此卷五策皆善答而求將一篇尤條整可觀且篇終有志於自効蓋書生而能知〕
兵者他日禦侮敵愾其挍幟先登者乎
考試官教諭范　批〔此卷三場皆佳而策學尤華贍必奇士也刻求將一篇以槩其餘猶恨不能〕
盡録耳
punctuated:
列聖躬行於上，群臣效法於下，四海承平百有餘年，寔我文皇貽謀之善有以啓之也。大哉，堯言，萬世之如見；卓乎，周禮，千古之所崇！愚生竊伏草茅，莊誦聖製爲有年矣。謹撫其槩，以復執事。儻不鄙而與進之，俾得對于帝庭，尚當以洋洋之聖謨爲我明天子獻。

第二問

同考試官訓導陳批〔此卷五策皆善答，而求將一篇尤條整可觀，且篇終有志於自効，蓋書生而能知〕兵者，他日禦侮敵愾，其挍幟先登者乎？

考試官教諭范批〔此卷三場皆佳，而策學尤華贍，必奇士也。刻求將一篇，以槩其餘，猶恨不能〕盡録耳。
translation_en:
…our successive sage emperors have personally put these principles into practice above, while their ministers have followed their example below. All within the Four Seas has enjoyed peace for more than a hundred years. Truly, the excellence of the plans bequeathed by our Emperor Wen helped bring this about. How great are the words of Yao, as though present before our eyes for ten thousand generations! How lofty are the Rites of Zhou, revered throughout the ages! This humble student, dwelling in obscurity, has reverently recited the imperial composition for many years. I have respectfully surveyed its main outlines to answer you, the examiners. If you do not disdain me but permit me to advance, allowing me to answer at the imperial court, I shall yet offer to our enlightened Son of Heaven these abundant counsels of the sage emperor.

Second Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: “All five policy essays in this script answer their questions well. The essay on seeking generals is particularly well organized and worth reading. Moreover, its conclusion expresses a determination to render service. Surely a scholar who understands military affairs will one day resist foreign aggression and share his sovereign’s wrath against the enemy—perhaps bearing the standard [?] and being first to scale the enemy’s walls?”

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: “This script is excellent in all three sessions, and the learning displayed in its policy essays is especially rich and ample. Its author must be an exceptional man. We print the essay on seeking generals to represent the others, yet still regret that we cannot record them all.”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授田　批　求將一策筆勢翩翩歷
數古之爲將者而歸結於所以求將之術可謂博古
通今之士朱衣暗裏寧不爲之首肯耶
金符日曜鳥隼風生人皆曰將而不知將
之所以爲將者在乎勇玉帳霜寒龍旂雲
擁人皆曰將而不知將之所以爲將者在
乎謀謀而不奇勇而不驍謀勇而不能兼
全過人者則失其所以爲將者矣此論將
者必以是爲優劣而選將者必以是爲進
===
退也歟執事試文士而詢以武將豈不以
章縫之士亦有飽諳將畧者乎而愚也非
其人雖然明問不可以虛請誦其陳迹而
求決擇焉嗟夫天下無必勝之兵而有不
可敗之將此古之用武者不以馭兵爲急
而以選將爲先豈不有由然哉武經論將
以智仁信勇嚴爲五德可尚矣而心書之
所謂八弊則貪而無厭詐而心怯妬賢嫉
能信讒好佞料彼不自料猶豫不自決荒
punctuated:
考試官教授田批：求將一策，筆勢翩翩，歷數古之爲將者，而歸結於所以求將之術，可謂博古通今之士。朱衣暗裏，寧不爲之首肯耶？

金符日曜，鳥隼風生，人皆曰將，而不知將之所以爲將者在乎勇。玉帳霜寒，龍旂雲擁，人皆曰將，而不知將之所以爲將者在乎謀。謀而不奇，勇而不驍，謀勇而不能兼全過人者，則失其所以爲將者矣。此論將者必以是爲優劣，而選將者必以是爲進退也歟？執事試文士而詢以武將，豈不以章縫之士亦有飽諳將畧者乎？而愚也非其人。雖然，明問不可以虛，請誦其陳迹而求決擇焉。嗟夫！天下無必勝之兵，而有不可敗之將。此古之用武者不以馭兵爲急，而以選將爲先，豈不有由然哉？《武經》論將，以智、仁、信、勇、嚴爲五德，可尚矣。而《心書》之所謂八弊，則貪而無厭，詐而心怯，妬賢嫉能，信讒好佞，料彼不自料，猶豫不自決，荒
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Tian, Professor: In this policy essay on seeking generals, the writing flows with grace. It enumerates the generals of antiquity and concludes with methods for seeking generals. Its author may well be called a scholar versed in antiquity and conversant with the present. Could the unseen red-robed figure [the spirit associated with examination success] fail to nod his approval?

Golden tallies gleam in the sunlight; bird-and-falcon banners stir in the wind. Everyone says, “A general!” Yet they do not know that what makes a general a general lies in courage. Frost chills the command tent; dragon banners cluster like clouds. Everyone says, “A general!” Yet they do not know that what makes a general a general lies in strategic judgment. If his planning lacks ingenuity, his courage lacks boldness, and he cannot unite strategic judgment and courage in full measure and surpass others, then he lacks what makes a general a general. Must not those who assess generals use these qualities to distinguish the superior from the inferior, and those who select generals use them to determine whom to advance or dismiss?

You, sir, are examining literary scholars yet ask about military commanders. Is this not because you believe that among those wearing scholars’ caps there are also men thoroughly versed in generalship? I, in my ignorance, am not such a man. Nevertheless, your discerning question cannot be left unanswered. Allow me to recount precedents and seek a basis for choosing among them.

Ah! There are no troops in the world certain of victory, yet there are generals who cannot be defeated. Surely there was a reason why those who employed military force in antiquity gave priority to selecting generals rather than treating the command of troops as their most pressing concern. In discussing generals, the Military Classics identify wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness as the five virtues. These are indeed worthy of esteem. But the eight defects spoken of in the Book of the Mind (Xinshu) are insatiable greed; deceitfulness coupled with cowardice at heart; jealousy of the worthy and envy of the capable; believing slander and delighting in flattery; assessing the enemy without assessing oneself; hesitation and inability to decide for oneself; dissipation…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
淫於酒色狂言而不以禮是也弊其可以
不革乎武經以善戰善守善攻爲三善可
姦矣而心書之所謂八惡則謀不能料是
非理不能任賢良政不能正刑法富不能
濟窮阨知不能備未形慮不能防微密達
不能舉所知敗不能無怨謗是也惡其可
以不去乎推轂而遣馮唐之告文帝蓋以
重命將之義登壇而拜高祖之用淮陰蓋
以崇大將之名時維鷹揚周之所謂尚父
===
呂望其人也飛將之名何足以狀其賢而
數奇之李廣則名之爲飛宜矣單騎見虜
唐之所謂尚父子儀其人也騎將之號何
足以盡其功而浪戰之馮敬則號之爲騎
當矣寇萊公謂智將不如福將意在出欽
若以定國是耳彼虎頭燕頷福如班超者
豈真先於運籌决勝之子房乎賀若弼謂
猛將不如謀將意在抑揚素以露已才耳
彼料敵設奇如曹操者豈真勞於擁盾直
punctuated: 淫於酒色，狂言而不以禮，是也。弊其可以不革乎？武經以善戰、善守、善攻爲三善，可姦矣。而心書之所謂八惡，則謀不能料是非，理不能任賢良，政不能正刑法，富不能濟窮阨，知不能備未形，慮不能防微密，達不能舉所知，敗不能無怨謗，是也。惡其可以不去乎？推轂而遣，馮唐之告文帝，蓋以重命將之義；登壇而拜，高祖之用淮陰，蓋以崇大將之名。「時維鷹揚」，周之所謂尚父，呂望其人也。飛將之名，何足以狀其賢？而數奇之李廣，則名之爲飛宜矣。單騎見虜，唐之所謂尚父，子儀其人也。騎將之號，何足以盡其功？而浪戰之馮敬，則號之爲騎當矣。寇萊公謂智將不如福將，意在出欽若以定國是耳。彼虎頭燕頷，福如班超者，豈真先於運籌决勝之子房乎？賀若弼謂猛將不如謀將，意在抑揚素以露已才耳。彼料敵設奇如曹操者，豈真勞於擁盾直
translation_en:
…indulgence in wine and women, and reckless speech without regard for ritual propriety: these are the remaining faults. Can such faults be left unreformed? The Military Classic identifies excellence in fighting, defending, and attacking as the three excellences—surely worthy of esteem [?]. But the eight evils listed in the Book of the Mind are these: in planning, being unable to judge right and wrong; in administration, being unable to employ worthy and capable men; in government, being unable to put punishments and laws in order; when wealthy, being unable to relieve those in distress; despite knowledge, being unable to prepare for what has not yet taken shape; despite forethought, being unable to guard against subtle and hidden dangers; when successful, being unable to recommend those whose abilities one knows; and when defeated, being unable to refrain from resentment and slander. Can such evils be left unremoved?

Pushing the chariot wheels to send a commander forth: Feng Tang’s account to Emperor Wen was intended to emphasize the solemn significance of commissioning a general. Ascending a platform to confer the appointment: Gaozu’s employment of the Marquis of Huaiyin was intended to exalt the standing of the commander-in-chief. “Then he soared like a hawk”: the man whom the Zhou called their Revered Father was Lü Wang. How could the name “Flying General” adequately describe his worth? Yet for the ill-fated Li Guang, the name “Flying General” was fitting. Riding alone to meet the enemy: the man whom the Tang called their Revered Father was Ziyi. How could the title “Cavalry General” encompass his achievements? Yet for Feng Jing, who fought recklessly, the title “Cavalry General” was appropriate.

Kou, Duke of Lai, said that a wise general was inferior to a fortunate general. His intention was merely to have Qinruo sent away and thereby settle the direction of state policy. Could someone with a tiger’s head and a swallow’s jaw, as fortunate as Ban Chao, truly take precedence over Zifang, who devised strategies and secured victory? He Ruobi said that a fierce general was inferior to a calculating general. His intention was merely to disparage Yang Su and display his own abilities. Could someone like Cao Cao, who assessed the enemy and devised surprise tactics, truly have labored more than [?] the man who, shield in hand, charged straight …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
入之樊噲亦世將可用而爵位與聯王侯
綽以之趙括有長平之坑則以其徒讀父
書耳儒將可用而雅歌投壺祭征虜以之
陸機有河陽之敗則以其徒工詞賦耳據
鞍上馬馬援之矍鑠可敬也何拘於將老
而怯之說邪棄繻請纓終軍之英妙可嘉
也何泥於將少而驕之言邪方
今文恬武熙仰
一人之有慶民安物阜欣四海之無虞第蠢茲
===
北虜時或跳梁而夷性桀驁自古爲然緩
之則豺噬豨勇干紀以自肆急之則鳥驚
魚散依險以自匿亦其恒態耳但我之自
治不可以不過而備之此廣求將材亦
今日之急務也夫求將之道不患無人以應
其求而患無術以求其人必也網羅之密
書幣之勤感之以忠激之以義本之以五
事試之以九徵訪之於巖穴之下搜之於
屠釣之中不專專於一途以取之閥閱可
punctuated:
入之樊噲？亦世將可用，而爵位與聯王侯，綽以之。趙括有長平之坑，則以其徒讀父書耳。儒將可用，而雅歌投壺，祭征虜以之。陸機有河陽之敗，則以其徒工詞賦耳。據鞍上馬，馬援之矍鑠可敬也，何拘於將老而怯之說邪？棄繻請纓，終軍之英妙可嘉也，何泥於將少而驕之言邪？
方今文恬武熙，仰一人之有慶；民安物阜，欣四海之無虞。第蠢茲北虜，時或跳梁，而夷性桀驁，自古爲然。緩之，則豺噬豨勇，干紀以自肆；急之，則鳥驚魚散，依險以自匿，亦其恒態耳。但我之自治，不可以不過而備之。此廣求將材，亦今日之急務也。
夫求將之道，不患無人以應其求，而患無術以求其人。必也網羅之密，書幣之勤，感之以忠，激之以義，本之以五事，試之以九徵，訪之於巖穴之下，搜之於屠釣之中，不專專於一途以取之。閥閱可
translation_en:
…Fan Kuai, who charged straight in carrying a shield? Men from hereditary military families, too, can be employed as generals; their ranks and positions place them alongside kings and marquises [the following phrase, 綽以之, is unclear: ?]. Zhao Kuo brought about the burial of the troops at Changping only because he merely read his father’s military writings. Scholarly generals can be employed: General Who Subdues the Caitiffs Ji Zun exemplified this, singing refined songs and playing pitch-pot. Lu Ji suffered defeat at Heyang only because his accomplishments were confined to literary compositions. Bracing himself against the saddle and mounting his horse, Ma Yuan displayed admirable vigor. Why be bound by the claim that generals grow timid with age? Discarding his silk travel credential and requesting a cord with which to bind the enemy, Zhong Jun displayed praiseworthy youthful brilliance. Why cling to the assertion that young generals are arrogant?
At present, civil and military affairs alike enjoy tranquility, thanks to the blessings enjoyed by the One Man, the emperor. The people are secure and goods abundant, and we rejoice that all within the Four Seas is free from anxiety. Yet these unruly northern foes sometimes run rampant. The defiant nature of these outsiders has been such since antiquity. If pressure upon them slackens, they bite like jackals and charge like wild boars, violating order and indulging themselves without restraint. If pressed hard, they scatter like startled birds and fish, hiding in difficult terrain. Such, too, is their habitual behavior. Nevertheless, in putting our own affairs in order, we must take more than ordinary precautions against them. Seeking broadly for men capable of serving as generals is therefore also an urgent task today.
In seeking generals, the concern is not that no men will answer the call, but that there may be no method for finding them. We must cast our net closely and send letters and gifts assiduously; move them through loyalty and rouse them through righteousness; ground our assessments in the five matters and test them through the nine signs; seek them among recluses dwelling in caves and search among butchers and fishermen. We must not confine recruitment to a single avenue. Men from distinguished hereditary families are acceptable…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
行伍亦可介冑可詩書亦可殆見奇謀驍
勇者項背相望而出分閫者有人秉鉞者
有人坐當一面者有人而邉庭指日臥鼓
矣區區北虜夫何慮雖然有文事者必有
武備此孔氏家法也安知白面書生不能
揮扇以却三軍投筆而取封於萬里哉孰
事幸勿以爲狂
第三問
===
同考試官訓導郭　批　明刑弼教之意敷暢殆盡
〔未復歸重於用人非學博識精不能到此固宜錄出〕
同考試官訓導胡　批　此卷五策皆有氣燄而敎
〔刑一篇尤爲詳瞻宜刻之以爲學者式〕
同考試官教諭范　批　讀此策知子他日效用必
〔先教後刑非倒行而逆施者也〕
考試官教諭范　批　先儒有云必有關雎麟趾
〔之意然後可以行周官之法度此策得之〕
考試官教授田　批　策場如此該博者不多
punctuated:
行伍亦可，介冑可，詩書亦可。殆見奇謀驍勇者項背相望而出，分閫者有人，秉鉞者有人，坐當一面者有人，而邉庭指日臥鼓矣。區區北虜，夫何慮？雖然，有文事者必有武備，此孔氏家法也。安知白面書生不能揮扇以却三軍，投筆而取封於萬里哉？孰事，幸勿以爲狂。
第三問
同考試官訓導郭批：明刑弼教之意，敷暢殆盡。〔未復歸重於用人，非學博識精不能到此，固宜錄出。〕
同考試官訓導胡批：此卷五策皆有氣燄，而敎〔刑一篇尤爲詳瞻，宜刻之以爲學者式。〕
同考試官教諭范批：讀此策，知子他日效用，必〔先教後刑，非倒行而逆施者也。〕
考試官教諭范批：先儒有云，必有關雎麟趾〔之意，然後可以行周官之法度。此策得之。〕
考試官教授田批：策場如此該博者不多。
translation_en:
…men from the ranks are also acceptable; those clad in armor are acceptable, as are those versed in the Odes and Documents. We would surely see men of extraordinary strategic ability and martial valor emerge one after another. There would be men to hold regional military commands, men to wield the battle-axe of command, and men to take charge of individual fronts. Before long, the drums along the frontier would lie silent. What need would there be to fear those paltry northern invaders? Nevertheless, those engaged in civil affairs must also make military preparations: this is the teaching handed down by Confucius. How can we know that a pale-faced scholar cannot wave his fan and repel whole armies, or cast aside his writing brush and win an enfeoffment ten thousand li away? You, sir [?], will, I hope, not consider this rash talk.
Third Question
Associate Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The meaning of making punishments clear to support moral instruction is expounded almost exhaustively. 〔The discussion again places the principal emphasis on employing the right men [?]. Without broad learning and precise understanding, one could not attain this insight. It certainly deserves to be selected for inclusion.〕”
Associate Examiner Hu, Assistant Instructor, comments: “All five policy essays in this script have vigor and brilliance, but the essay on moral instruction 〔and punishment is especially detailed and comprehensive [?]. It should be printed as a model for students.〕”
Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “Reading this policy essay, I know that when you enter service in the future, you will certainly 〔put moral instruction first and punishment afterward, and will not act perversely or contrary to the proper order.〕”
Examiner Fan, Instructor, comments: “An earlier Confucian scholar said that one must possess the spirit of ‘The Ospreys Cry’ (Guan ju) and ‘The Qilin’s Hooves’ (Lin zhi) 〔before one can put into practice the rules and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan). This policy essay grasps that principle.〕”
Examiner Tian, Professor, comments: “Few candidates in the policy-essay examination display learning as comprehensive as this.”

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
天之於物止於春而無待於秋可乎曰不
可也聖人之於人止於教而不俟於刑可
乎曰不可也使天而止於春則必無以久
運而成萬物使聖人而止於教則必無以
久治而育萬民蓋秋者所以成乎春也刑
者所以輔乎教也此則執事發策之意愚
請有以復焉昔者帝舜當水土既平之後
蒸民粒食之餘於是命契爲司徒以敷五
教命皋陶作士師以明五刑聖人豈不知
===
德禮之化民深而善教之得民心乃倡爲
是刑辟以虐天下哉蓋聖人盡出治之本
而猶悉輔治之具非若後世徒恃其末而
忘其本者也是則聖人之用五刑也所以
弼五教也非得已而用之也譬之於耘也
非去稼也去其害稼者也聖人之於刑正
所以爲教天之於秋正所以爲生天無一
時而非生陽舒陰慘皆大造之公也聖人
無一政而非教仁育義正皆大化之行也
punctuated:
天之於物，止於春而無待於秋，可乎？曰：不可也。聖人之於人，止於教而不俟於刑，可乎？曰：不可也。使天而止於春，則必無以久運而成萬物；使聖人而止於教，則必無以久治而育萬民。蓋秋者，所以成乎春也；刑者，所以輔乎教也。此則執事發策之意，愚請有以復焉。
昔者帝舜當水土既平之後，蒸民粒食之餘，於是命契爲司徒，以敷五教；命皋陶作士師，以明五刑。聖人豈不知德禮之化民深，而善教之得民心，乃倡爲是刑辟以虐天下哉？蓋聖人盡出治之本，而猶悉輔治之具，非若後世徒恃其末而忘其本者也。是則聖人之用五刑也，所以弼五教也，非得已而用之也。譬之於耘也，非去稼也，去其害稼者也。聖人之於刑，正所以爲教；天之於秋，正所以爲生。天無一時而非生，陽舒陰慘，皆大造之公也；聖人無一政而非教，仁育義正，皆大化之行也。
translation_en:
In its dealings with things, could Heaven stop at spring without awaiting autumn? The answer is no. In his dealings with people, could the sage stop at instruction without resorting to punishment? The answer is no. If Heaven stopped at spring, it would have no means of sustaining its workings and bringing the myriad things to completion; if the sage stopped at instruction, he would have no means of maintaining lasting order and nurturing the myriad people. Autumn brings spring’s work to completion; punishment supports instruction. This, then, is the intent behind the policy question you have posed. I venture to offer a reply.
In former times, after Emperor Shun had brought the waters and lands into order and the common people had grain to eat, he appointed Xie as Minister of Education to disseminate the five teachings, and Gao Yao as Chief Judge to make clear the five punishments. Could the sage have failed to understand how profoundly virtue and ritual transform the people, and how good instruction wins their hearts, and thus have instituted these penal laws to oppress all under Heaven? Rather, the sage fully established the foundations of government while also providing all the means that support it. He was unlike those of later ages who relied solely on secondary measures and forgot the foundations. Thus, the sage employed the five punishments to assist the five teachings, using them only when he could not do otherwise. It is like weeding: one does not remove the crops, but removes what harms them. The sage’s use of punishment serves precisely the purpose of instruction; Heaven’s autumn serves precisely the purpose of fostering life. There is no season in which Heaven does not foster life: the warmth of yang and the harshness of yin alike express the impartiality of the great creative process. There is no act of government by the sage that does not instruct: nurturing through benevolence and correcting through righteousness alike carry forward the great work of transformation.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
繫教刑之道始於唐虞而大備於周以教
言之大司徒目五物之民而施十有二教
一曰以禮記教敬二曰以陽禮教讓三曰
以陰禮教親四曰以樂禮教和五曰以儀
辨等六曰以俗教安七曰以刑教中八曰
以誓教恤九曰以度教節十曰以世事教
能十有一曰以賢制爵十有二曰以庸制
祿而又有三物之教一曰六德知仁聖義
中和二曰六行孝友睦婣任恤三曰六藝
===
禮樂射御書數其教不亦備乎以刑言之
大司徒以八刑糾萬民一曰不孝之刑二
曰不睦之刑三曰不婣之刑四曰不弟之
刑五曰不任之刑六曰不恤之刑七曰造
言之刑八曰亂民之刑既有八刑而小司
徒復以八辟麗邦法一曰議親二曰議故
三曰議賢四曰議能五曰議功六曰議貴
七曰議勤八曰議賓既有八辟而士師復
掌士之八成一曰邦約二曰邦賊三曰邦
punctuated: 繫教刑之道始於唐虞，而大備於周。以教言之，大司徒目五物之民而施十有二教：一曰以禮記教敬，二曰以陽禮教讓，三曰以陰禮教親，四曰以樂禮教和，五曰以儀辨等，六曰以俗教安，七曰以刑教中，八曰以誓教恤，九曰以度教節，十曰以世事教能，十有一曰以賢制爵，十有二曰以庸制祿。而又有三物之教：一曰六德，知、仁、聖、義、中、和；二曰六行，孝、友、睦、婣、任、恤；三曰六藝，禮、樂、射、御、書、數。其教不亦備乎？以刑言之，大司徒以八刑糾萬民：一曰不孝之刑，二曰不睦之刑，三曰不婣之刑，四曰不弟之刑，五曰不任之刑，六曰不恤之刑，七曰造言之刑，八曰亂民之刑。既有八刑，而小司徒復以八辟麗邦法：一曰議親，二曰議故，三曰議賢，四曰議能，五曰議功，六曰議貴，七曰議勤，八曰議賓。既有八辟，而士師復掌士之八成：一曰邦約，二曰邦賊，三曰邦
translation_en:
The way of linking education and punishment [?] began under Tang and Yu and reached its fullest development under the Zhou. As regards education, the Minister of Education classified the people into five categories [?] and applied twelve teachings: first, teaching reverence through records of ritual [?]; second, teaching deference through the yang rites; third, teaching affection through the yin rites; fourth, teaching harmony through musical rites; fifth, distinguishing ranks through ceremonial forms; sixth, teaching contentment through customary practices; seventh, teaching proper conduct through punishments; eighth, teaching solicitude through admonitory oaths; ninth, teaching restraint through standards; tenth, teaching competence through hereditary occupations; eleventh, determining rank according to worthiness; and twelfth, determining emoluments according to service. There were also three categories of instruction: first, the six virtues—wisdom, benevolence, sagacity, righteousness, balance, and harmony; second, the six forms of conduct—filial devotion, brotherly affection, concord among kin, amity among relatives by marriage, trustworthiness, and solicitude; and third, the six arts—ritual, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and mathematics. Was this education not comprehensive?

As regards punishment, the Minister of Education corrected the people through eight punishments: first, punishment for unfilial conduct; second, punishment for discord among kin; third, punishment for discord among relatives by marriage; fourth, punishment for disrespect toward elder brothers; fifth, punishment for untrustworthiness; sixth, punishment for lack of solicitude; seventh, punishment for fabricating rumors; and eighth, punishment for throwing the people into disorder. Besides these eight punishments, the Vice Minister of Education also applied the eight grounds for deliberation in adjudicating under the laws of the state: first, deliberation for relatives of the ruler; second, for his longstanding associates; third, for the worthy; fourth, for the able; fifth, for those of meritorious achievement; sixth, for those of high rank; seventh, for those diligent in service; and eighth, for guests of the state. Besides these eight grounds for deliberation, the Judicial Officer also administered the eight established categories of judicial cases: first, agreements of the state; second, those who harm the state; third, state …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
諜四曰犯邦令五曰矯邦令六曰爲邦盟
七曰爲邦悖八曰爲邦誣其刑不亦備乎
嗚呼聖人之立教制刑其詳如此是豈好
爲是瑣瑣者哉蓋周之時非若唐虞之時
也風氣大開則民僞日滋聖人慮其或潰
而蕩也曲防而預備之惟恐有不至況五
禮有三千之威儀而五刑亦有三千之條
例故出於禮者必入於刑出於刑者必入
於禮而聖人自亦不容已也夫聖人不容
===
已而爲之則知其所爲者一出於當然是
故聖人法天以爲治天以春而生物以秋
而歛物而物之具於覆載之間有大者小
者飛者潛者動者植者各有以生之歛之
不可以一齊也則夫立不一之教制不一
之刑獨不然哉桑之何有關雎麟趾之意
然後可以行周官之法度後世非不立教
也教其所教而非古之教汲汲焉月書季
考而已果古之教乎後世非不制刑也刑
punctuated:
諜，四曰犯邦令，五曰矯邦令，六曰爲邦盟，七曰爲邦悖，八曰爲邦誣。其刑不亦備乎？

嗚呼！聖人之立教制刑，其詳如此，是豈好爲是瑣瑣者哉？蓋周之時，非若唐虞之時也。風氣大開，則民僞日滋。聖人慮其或潰而蕩也，曲防而預備之，惟恐有不至。況五禮有三千之威儀，而五刑亦有三千之條例。故出於禮者必入於刑，出於刑者必入於禮，而聖人自亦不容已也。夫聖人不容已而爲之，則知其所爲者一出於當然。是故聖人法天以爲治。天以春而生物，以秋而歛物，而物之具於覆載之間，有大者、小者、飛者、潛者、動者、植者，各有以生之、歛之，不可以一齊也。則夫立不一之教，制不一之刑，獨不然哉？桑之何有？《關雎》《麟趾》之意，然後可以行《周官》之法度。後世非不立教也，教其所教，而非古之教，汲汲焉月書季考而已，果古之教乎？後世非不制刑也，刑
translation_en:
…spies against the state; fourth, violating the state's commands; fifth, falsifying the state's commands; sixth, making covenants within the state; seventh, committing acts of rebellion against the state; and eighth, making false accusations within the state. Were its penal provisions not comprehensive?

Alas! Such was the detail with which the sages established instruction and instituted punishments. Could it have been because they delighted in such minutiae? The age of Zhou was unlike the age of Tang Yao and Yu Shun. As prevailing customs developed and spread, deceit among the people increased daily. Fearing that people might break loose and abandon all restraint, the sages guarded against every contingency and made preparations in advance, concerned only that something might remain unprovided for. Moreover, the five categories of rites had three thousand rules of ceremonial deportment, and the five punishments likewise had three thousand provisions. Thus, whoever departed from ritual necessarily came within the scope of punishment, and whoever emerged from punishment necessarily returned to ritual. The sages themselves could not refrain from acting in this way.

Since the sages acted because they could not do otherwise, we know that everything they did proceeded entirely from what was fitting. Thus the sages modeled their governance on Heaven. Heaven brings things to life through spring and gathers them in through autumn. Among the things existing between sheltering Heaven and supporting Earth are the large and the small, those that fly and those that swim below the surface, those that move and those that grow rooted in place. Each requires its own means of being brought to life and gathered in; they cannot all be treated alike. Is it not the same with establishing varied forms of instruction and instituting varied punishments?

“What does the mulberry have?” [?] Only with the spirit of “The Ospreys” (Guan ju) and “The Qilin's Hooves” (Lin zhi) can one put into practice the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhou guan). It is not that later ages failed to establish instruction. They taught what they chose to teach, but it was not the instruction of antiquity. They busied themselves merely with monthly records and quarterly assessments. Was this truly the instruction of antiquity? It is not that later ages failed to institute punishments. They punish…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
其所刑而非古之刑弊弊焉文法凡格而
已果古之刑乎誠使後之爲教一皆敦性
分之實德察其行而後博求其文如文翁
之興學蜀郡也如胡瑗之教授蘇湖也後
之用刑一皆體天地之至公推原其情而
後裁斷以律如所謂刑期無刑辟以止辟
也如所謂以仁義行法律不以法律行仁
義也夫然則唐虞之陳跡不必蹈也而美
意攸存三代之故轍不必循也而良法不
失尚何古之治不可復見也哉若探其本
而言之則教也刑也又在乎各得其人也
管見如斯惟執事以爲何如
第四問
考試官教諭范　批〔此卷五策皆佳而論文一篇筆端英氣横發且趣然欲追古作者其志亦可尚〕
考試官教授田　批〔策場敷衍問目者多此已得士如此主司寧不爲之慶幸〕
punctuated:
其所刑，而非古之刑，弊弊焉文法凡格而已，果古之刑乎？誠使後之爲教，一皆敦性分之實德，察其行而後博求其文，如文翁之興學蜀郡也，如胡瑗之教授蘇湖也；後之用刑，一皆體天地之至公，推原其情而後裁斷以律，如所謂刑期無刑，辟以止辟也，如所謂以仁義行法律，不以法律行仁義也。夫然，則唐虞之陳跡不必蹈也，而美意攸存；三代之故轍不必循也，而良法不失。尚何古之治不可復見也哉？若探其本而言之，則教也、刑也，又在乎各得其人也。管見如斯，惟執事以爲何如？

第四問

考試官教諭范　批〔此卷五策皆佳，而論文一篇，筆端英氣横發，且趣然欲追古作者，其志亦可尚。〕

考試官教授田　批〔策場敷衍問目者多，此已得士如此，主司寧不爲之慶幸？〕
translation_en:
…those whom they punish, yet theirs are not the punishments of antiquity. They merely toil away over legal technicalities and routine regulations [?]; are these truly the punishments of antiquity? If only those who teach in later ages would all cultivate the substantial virtues inherent in human nature, examining people's conduct before seeking broadly for literary accomplishment—as Wen Weng did when he promoted learning in Shu Commandery, and as Hu Yuan did when he taught in Suzhou and Huzhou. If only those who administer punishments in later ages would all embody the perfect impartiality of Heaven and Earth, investigating the underlying circumstances before deciding cases according to the statutes—as expressed in the sayings, “The aim of punishment is to dispense with punishment,” and “Punish wrongdoing to stop wrongdoing”; and again, “Apply laws through benevolence and righteousness, rather than apply benevolence and righteousness through laws.” Then there would be no need to retrace the footsteps of Tang and Yu, yet their admirable intentions would endure; no need to follow the old tracks of the Three Dynasties, yet their good institutions would not be lost. Why, then, could the good government of antiquity not be seen again? To probe the root of the matter, however, both teaching and punishment depend on finding the right people for each. Such is my limited view. What do you, honored examiner, think of it?

Fourth Question

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔All five policy essays in this script are excellent. In the discourse on literary composition, a heroic spirit bursts forth from the tip of his brush; moreover, he eagerly seeks to emulate the writers of antiquity. His ambition, too, merits esteem.〕

Comment by Examiner Tian, Professor: 〔Many candidates in the policy-essay session merely elaborate on the wording of the questions. Here we have already obtained a scholar of such quality [?]; how could the presiding examiners fail to rejoice in their good fortune?〕

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
卷五策皆條答無遺而論文一策品第諸家之作確
有定見吾知子馳價文場蓋有年矣置之高選孰
謂翕然
雲霞燦若鉛槧是拈為文亦工矣然不可
以徒為而當根本於六經藻鑑洞然品題
是負論文亦精矣然不可以泛論而當折
衷於六經甚矣六經載道之文萬世文章
之祖也為文而不根本於是則雖詞如錦
織一梭何以得文體之妙論文而不折衷
===
於六經則雖口如懸河千里抑何以服文
人之心哉執事應聘與文而以文策士且
欲論諸子之文而求折衷於六經之文矣
復叩以所願學者執事之意則深矣顧愚
膚淺敢不摭拾以對嗟夫為文無定體本
之六經有定體論文無定法本之六經有
定法粤自六經一變而漢登名文章之錄
者如對賢良之策而擢上第推王命之論
以歸炎劉公孫班彪之作非不馳聲於藝
punctuated:
卷五策皆條答無遺，而論文一策，品第諸家之作，確有定見。吾知子馳價文場，蓋有年矣。置之高選，孰謂翕然？

雲霞燦若，鉛槧是拈，為文亦工矣；然不可以徒為，而當根本於六經。藻鑑洞然，品題是負，論文亦精矣；然不可以泛論，而當折衷於六經。甚矣，六經載道之文，萬世文章之祖也！為文而不根本於是，則雖詞如錦織一梭，何以得文體之妙？論文而不折衷於六經，則雖口如懸河千里，抑何以服文人之心哉？執事應聘與文，而以文策士，且欲論諸子之文，而求折衷於六經之文矣。復叩以所願學者，執事之意則深矣。顧愚膚淺，敢不摭拾以對？嗟夫！為文無定體，本之六經有定體；論文無定法，本之六經有定法。粤自六經一變而漢，登名文章之錄者，如對賢良之策而擢上第，推王命之論以歸炎劉，公孫、班彪之作，非不馳聲於藝
translation_en:
…The paper’s five policy essays answer every point without omission, while the essay on literary composition ranks the works of the various writers with firm and considered judgment. I know that you have enjoyed a distinguished reputation in the literary arena for years. Who would call placing you among the highest selections mere conformity with others [?]?

Brilliant as clouds at sunset, one takes up writing implements and composes with skill. Yet one must not write merely for writing’s sake: one must take the Six Classics as one’s foundation. With penetrating literary discernment, one assumes the responsibility of appraisal and discusses writing with refinement. Yet one must not discuss it in generalities: one must judge it by the Six Classics. How supremely the Six Classics, writings that convey the Way, stand as the ancestors of literary composition for all ages! If one writes without this foundation, then even if one’s phrases resemble brocade woven by a shuttle, how can one attain the subtleties of literary form? If one discusses writing without judging it by the Six Classics, then even if one’s eloquence pours forth like a river cascading for a thousand li, how can one win the assent of men of letters?

You, honored sir, have accepted an invitation to take part in literary assessment [?] and are testing candidates with a policy question on writing. You wish us to discuss the writings of the various masters and seek a standard of judgment in the writings of the Six Classics. You further ask whom we wish to emulate in our studies: your intention is indeed profound. Though my understanding is shallow, dare I fail to gather what I can in reply?

Alas! Composition has no fixed form, but when grounded in the Six Classics it has a fixed form; literary criticism has no fixed method, but when grounded in the Six Classics it has a fixed method. From the Six Classics, writing underwent a transformation that brought it to the Han. Among those whose names entered the literary rolls were one who answered a policy question addressed to the Worthy and Good and was placed in the highest rank, and another who expounded the royal mandate in a discourse, assigning it to the Liu house of Han, associated with the virtue of Fire. The works of Gongsun and Ban Biao certainly won renown in the literary…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
苑也然曲學阿世而殊無正大之論專言
祥瑞而雜以符命之妄戾於經多矣豈若
董子天人之三策乎蓋言更化善治同乎
惟時之易三聖一道同乎執中之書同乎
詩禮而有正誼明道之論同乎春秋而有
大一統之言故程子謂其有儒者氣象又
曰董子度越諸子爲是〔故也〕至若過秦有
論而攻守之是陳美新有文而功德之是
頌賈誼楊雄之作非不擅名於文場也然
===
年少氣英而爲術太疎含蓄蒙垢而事莽
無恥背於經甚矣豈若孔明出師之一表
乎蓋言鞠躬盡瘁合易匪躬之節開誠布
公合書啓心之旨合乎詩禮而有光先損
益之規合乎春秋而有親賢遠奸之說故
蘇文忠公稱其與說命相表裏又有稱其
有王佐之才爲此故也再變而唐稱名家
者孰不曰韓子柳子而韓子作毛穎傳柳
子讀之稱其捕龍蛇搏虎豹而巍然爲一
punctuated:
苑也。然曲學阿世，而殊無正大之論；專言祥瑞，而雜以符命之妄，戾於經多矣。豈若董子天人之三策乎？蓋言更化善治，同乎惟時之《易》；三聖一道，同乎執中之《書》；同乎《詩》《禮》，而有正誼明道之論；同乎《春秋》，而有大一統之言。故程子謂其有儒者氣象，又曰董子度越諸子，爲是〔故也〕。

至若過秦有論，而攻守之是陳；美新有文，而功德之是頌。賈誼、楊雄之作，非不擅名於文場也。然年少氣英，而爲術太疎；含蓄蒙垢，而事莽無恥，背於經甚矣。豈若孔明出師之一表乎？蓋言鞠躬盡瘁，合《易》匪躬之節；開誠布公，合《書》啓心之旨；合乎《詩》《禮》，而有光先損益之規；合乎《春秋》，而有親賢遠奸之說。故蘇文忠公稱其與《說命》相表裏，又有稱其有王佐之才，爲此故也。

再變而唐，稱名家者，孰不曰韓子、柳子？而韓子作《毛穎傳》，柳子讀之，稱其捕龍蛇、搏虎豹，而巍然爲一
translation_en:
…in the literary world. Yet they twisted learning to flatter their age, offering no upright and impartial arguments; they spoke exclusively of auspicious portents, mingling these with fanciful claims about signs of Heaven’s mandate. In many respects they contravened the Classics. How could they compare with Master Dong’s three policy essays on Heaven and humanity? His advocacy of reforming government to achieve good rule accords with the Book of Changes’ emphasis on timeliness; his assertion that the three sage kings followed one Way accords with the Book of Documents’ teaching of holding fast to the mean. In accord with the Book of Odes and the rites, he argued for setting righteousness aright and making the Way clear; in accord with the Spring and Autumn Annals, he spoke of honoring comprehensive unity. This is why Master Cheng said that he possessed the bearing of a Confucian scholar, and also said that Master Dong surpassed the other masters.

As for the discourse On the Faults of Qin, it sets forth matters of attack and defense; the essay In Praise of the Xin extols achievements and virtue. The works of Jia Yi and Yang Xiong certainly enjoyed renown in literary circles. Yet the former was young and spirited, while his methods were far too ill-considered; the latter concealed himself and endured disgrace [?], shamelessly serving Wang Mang. They departed gravely from the Classics. How could they compare with Kongming’s memorial On Dispatching the Army? His words about devoting himself utterly to his duties accord with the Book of Changes’ principle of disregarding personal interests; his openness and impartiality accord with the Book of Documents’ purpose of opening the ruler’s mind. In accord with the Book of Odes and the rites, he offered guidance on glorifying his predecessor and making appropriate reductions and additions; in accord with the Spring and Autumn Annals, he advocated drawing close to the worthy and keeping the treacherous at a distance. This is why Lord Su Wenzhong said that the memorial and the Charge to Yue complemented one another, and why others praised Kongming as having the talent to assist a true king.

With a further transformation, literature reached the Tang. Who, in naming its celebrated masters, would not name Master Han and Master Liu? Master Han wrote the Biography of Mao Ying. Master Liu read it and praised him as catching dragons and serpents and grappling with tigers and leopards, towering as a …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
代之山斗𡸁矣若論其意非模倣於六經
之步驟乎否則易許詩葩必不爲之自許
也柳子作鐃歌等篇史氏賛之言其軌漢
周凌晉宋而凜然爲一王之法當矣若究
其旨非依稀於六經之影響乎否則左氏
國語必不與之相類也三變而宋號專門
者孰不曰歐蘇王張而歐子李論之作蓋
攻時人之崇尚老佛而欲修正勝邪也蘇
子買燈之疏蓋諷時君之習爲奢靡而欲
===
務本節用也歐蘇醇正典雅質諸六經其
有合乎变止幾康之謨節以制度之說乎
待漏有院而王元之記之因文求道無非
忠君愛國之情六經有關而張伯玉記之
循名責實無非尊正黜邪之意王張醇正
典雅揆諸六經不有合乎爲德爲民之誥
尊王賤伯之旨乎嗟夫彩鳳吞聲而蟲禽
爲之鳴蛟龍隱迹而蝦鱔爲之舞聖人之
六經不作而諸子之文何𢎞三變然猶幸
punctuated: 代之山斗𡸁矣。若論其意，非模倣於六經之步驟乎？否則「易許詩葩」，必不爲之自許也。柳子作《鐃歌》等篇，史氏賛之，言其軌漢周、凌晉宋，而凜然爲一王之法當矣。若究其旨，非依稀於六經之影響乎？否則《左氏》《國語》，必不與之相類也。三變而宋，號專門者，孰不曰歐、蘇、王、張？而歐子《李論》之作，蓋攻時人之崇尚老佛，而欲修正勝邪也。蘇子《買燈》之疏，蓋諷時君之習爲奢靡，而欲務本節用也。歐、蘇醇正典雅，質諸六經，其有合乎「变止幾康」之謨、「節以制度」之說乎？待漏有院，而王元之記之，因文求道，無非忠君愛國之情；六經有關，而張伯玉記之，循名責實，無非尊正黜邪之意。王、張醇正典雅，揆諸六經，不有合乎爲德爲民之誥、尊王賤伯之旨乎？嗟夫！彩鳳吞聲，而蟲禽爲之鳴；蛟龍隱迹，而蝦鱔爲之舞。聖人之六經不作，而諸子之文何𢎞三變，然猶幸
translation_en:
…he stands loftily as the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of his age. If we consider his conception, did he not model his approach on the Six Classics? Otherwise, he surely would not have claimed for himself the qualities of “the Changes’ approval [?] and the Odes’ luxuriance.” Master Liu composed the “Martial Songs” and other pieces. The historian praised him, saying that he followed the tracks of the Han and Zhou and surpassed the Jin and Song; it was fitting that his work should stand imposing as a standard for a king’s rule. If we examine his purport, does it not faintly echo the Six Classics? Otherwise, the Zuo Commentary and the Discourses of the States would surely bear no resemblance to it.

With the third transformation, in the Song, who would not name Ou, Su, Wang, and Zhang as the acknowledged masters of distinctive schools? Master Ou’s “Discourse on Li” [?] attacked his contemporaries’ veneration of Laozi and the Buddha, seeking to cultivate orthodoxy and overcome heterodoxy. Master Su’s memorial on purchasing lanterns admonished the ruler of his time for his habitual extravagance, seeking to promote attention to fundamentals and economy in expenditure. Ou and Su were pure, correct, refined, and elegant. Measured against the Six Classics, did their writings accord with the counsel expressed in “变止幾康” [text unclear] and the teaching to “regulate expenditure through established institutions”?

There was a courtyard for officials awaiting the court audience, and Wang Yuanzhi wrote an account of it. Seeking the Way through his writing, he expressed nothing but loyalty to his ruler and love for his country. There was a gate of the Six Classics [?], and Zhang Boyu wrote an account of it. Examining whether substance fulfilled the name, he expressed nothing but the intention to honor orthodoxy and reject heterodoxy. Wang and Zhang were pure, correct, refined, and elegant. Judged against the Six Classics, did they not accord with the admonitions concerning virtue and the people, and with the principle of honoring true kings and disparaging hegemons?

Alas! When the colorful phoenix falls silent, insects and birds sing in its place; when the dragons withdraw from sight, shrimp and eels dance in their place. When the sages’ Six Classics were no longer being composed, how greatly the writings of the various masters underwent these three transformations [?]! Yet fortunately…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
其不甚背馳於經也下此則騁浮華而鬭
纖巧買櫝還珠特空文耳其害道亦弘矣
其去經亦遠矣有志於古作者寧不爲之
一慨哉愚生朝窓暮燈平日之所以習學
者文鵬摶鶚薦今日之所以取應者文然
於諸子之文則姑舍是而不能乃所願學
者則六經載道之文乎不識執事然之否
第五問
===
同考試官教諭范　批〔五策皆詳整而時務一篇尤見經濟之學秋闈高選舍子其誰〕
考試官教諭范　批〔此卷五策如行雲流水而治盜一篇尤有識見他日措之事業必有可觀得士如此可無負矣〕
考試官教授田　批〔時務一篇尤見學識來春大庭之對吾深有望於子〕
天下之患有伏於尋常之中而實有非常
之慮者不可不早計而預圖之也夫所謂
punctuated:
其不甚背馳於經也。下此，則騁浮華而鬭纖巧，買櫝還珠，特空文耳。其害道亦弘矣，其去經亦遠矣。有志於古作者，寧不爲之一慨哉？愚生朝窓暮燈，平日之所以習學者，文；鵬摶鶚薦，今日之所以取應者，文。然於諸子之文，則姑舍是而不能，乃所願學者，則六經載道之文乎？不識執事然之否？

第五問

同考試官教諭范　批〔五策皆詳整，而時務一篇尤見經濟之學。秋闈高選，舍子其誰？〕

考試官教諭范　批〔此卷五策如行雲流水，而治盜一篇尤有識見。他日措之事業，必有可觀。得士如此，可無負矣。〕

考試官教授田　批〔時務一篇尤見學識。來春大庭之對，吾深有望於子。〕

天下之患，有伏於尋常之中而實有非常之慮者，不可不早計而預圖之也。夫所謂
translation_en:
…that they did not diverge too greatly from the Classics. Below this level, however, writers flaunt superficial ornament and vie in minute cleverness. Like buying the casket and returning the pearl, this is merely empty writing. Great indeed is its harm to the Way, and far indeed has it departed from the Classics! Could anyone aspiring to write in the ancient manner fail to lament this?

I, an unworthy student, have studied writing in my daily practice, by the window in the morning and by lamplight at night. Now, aspiring to soar like the peng bird and to win recommendation like the osprey, it is through writing that I present myself for examination. As for the writings of the various masters, I would for the moment set them aside, yet cannot [?]; what I wish to study is surely the writing of the Six Classics, which conveys the Way. I do not know whether you, sir, approve.

Fifth Question

Comment by Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔All five policy essays are detailed and well ordered, while the essay on current affairs especially reveals learning in statecraft. For high selection in the autumn Provincial Examination, who could there be but you?〕

Comment by Examiner Fan, Instructor: 〔The five policy essays in this script flow like moving clouds and running water, while the essay on suppressing banditry shows particular insight. When this is put into practice in your future undertakings, there will surely be something worth seeing. Having obtained a scholar like this, we may feel that we have fulfilled our charge.〕

Comment by Examiner Tian, Professor: 〔The essay on current affairs especially reveals learning and insight. I have great hopes for your response before the imperial court next spring.〕

Among the troubles of the realm are some that lurk within the commonplace yet present truly extraordinary grounds for concern. We must consider them early and devise measures in advance. Now, what is meant by…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
患者何盜賊是已蓋天下之有盜賊猶居
室之有雀鼠其始也穿屋穴墻雖若無甚
大患然坐視而不爲之所將至於敝漏傾
圮而不可復支故善居室者必謹其苫蓋
而厚其垣墻則雖有雀鼠而不能爲之患
善治天下之盜賊者亦若是而已矣執事
發策謂今天下治平所事乎兵者惟夷狄
與盜賊且謂贛州南安盜賊嘯聚卒難撲
滅而求所以處之之術謂瑞州臨江盜賊
===
竊發民無寧居而求所以遏之之方愚不
敏何足以當此雖然不敢不有復也請誦
其所聞而執事擇焉夫治中國之盜與禦
夷狄之術不同彼夷狄者遠方異類其款
服也不足喜其侵叛也不足憂惟當謹守
吾之疆埸俟其來寇而拒之耳若夫盜賊
則不然險阻是憑抄奪是資亡命是聚宿
於肘腋之下而非有嚴邊絕塞之防雜於
編氓之中而易爲窮蹙動搖之變治之無
punctuated:
患者何？盜賊是已。蓋天下之有盜賊，猶居室之有雀鼠。其始也，穿屋穴墻，雖若無甚大患，然坐視而不爲之所，將至於敝漏傾圮而不可復支。故善居室者，必謹其苫蓋而厚其垣墻，則雖有雀鼠而不能爲之患。善治天下之盜賊者，亦若是而已矣。執事發策，謂今天下治平，所事乎兵者，惟夷狄與盜賊；且謂贛州、南安盜賊嘯聚，卒難撲滅，而求所以處之之術；謂瑞州、臨江盜賊竊發，民無寧居，而求所以遏之之方。愚不敏，何足以當此？雖然，不敢不有復也。請誦其所聞，而執事擇焉。

夫治中國之盜，與禦夷狄之術不同。彼夷狄者，遠方異類，其款服也不足喜，其侵叛也不足憂，惟當謹守吾之疆埸，俟其來寇而拒之耳。若夫盜賊則不然，險阻是憑，抄奪是資，亡命是聚，宿於肘腋之下，而非有嚴邊絕塞之防；雜於編氓之中，而易爲窮蹙動搖之變。治之無
translation_en:
…What is this menace? It is banditry. The presence of bandits in the realm is like that of sparrows and rats in a dwelling. At first they pierce the roof and burrow through the walls, seemingly causing no very great harm. Yet if one merely watches and takes no measures against them, the dwelling will eventually become dilapidated, leaky, and liable to collapse, beyond any possibility of shoring it up. Thus those who maintain a dwelling well take care over its thatching and make its walls thick. Then, even if sparrows and rats are present, they cannot cause harm. Those who deal well with bandits throughout the realm do just the same. In setting the policy question, you state that the realm is now peaceful and well governed, and that military action is required only against foreign peoples and bandits. You further state that bandits in Ganzhou and Nan’an have rallied together and are difficult to eradicate swiftly, and ask for methods of dealing with them; you state that bandits in Ruizhou and Linjiang have suddenly risen, leaving the people unable to live in peace, and ask for ways to check them. Dull-witted as I am, how could I be equal to this task? Nevertheless, I dare not leave it unanswered. Allow me to recount what I have learned, for you to judge.

The methods for dealing with bandits within China differ from those for resisting foreign peoples. Those foreign peoples are distant and of a different kind: their submission is insufficient cause for rejoicing, and their incursions and rebellions insufficient cause for anxiety. We need only guard our frontiers carefully, await their raids, and repel them. Bandits, however, are otherwise. They rely on difficult terrain, sustain themselves by plunder, and gather fugitives about them. They lodge close at hand, where there are no defenses such as fortified frontiers and remote border barriers; they mingle among the registered common people and can readily provoke upheaval when driven to desperation. If, in dealing with them, one lacks…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
術其爲患實有大於夷狄者是以古人於
此每致意焉昔元魏時兗州多盜刺史李
崇命村置一樓樓皆懸鼓盜發即擊俄頃
之間聲布百里由是發無不獲後周時新
鄭多盜竇儼請令鄉村團爲義營每有盜
發則鳴鼓舉火丁壯雲集盜少民多無能
脫者此二法者大畧相似然以愚意論之
用之魯鄭平原之地則可用之江西山谿
險阻之間恐亦未宜竇儼又嘗請令盜賊
自相糾告以其所告資產之半賞之又崔
安潛治盜出庫錢千五百緡分置三市榜
曰能告捕一盜賞五百緡於是諸盜相疑
散逃出境此二法者大意亦同然以愚意
評之賞以官錢恐不可繼不若就其資產
賞之似爲可常然古法有限事變無窮泥
古人之陳跡以爲今日治盜之良圖非執
事所以策愚意也益亦曰任人乎蓋得人
而任之則可以料敵制變可以隨事設謀
punctuated:
術，其爲患實有大於夷狄者。是以古人於此每致意焉。昔元魏時，兗州多盜，刺史李崇命村置一樓，樓皆懸鼓，盜發即擊，俄頃之間，聲布百里，由是發無不獲。後周時，新鄭多盜，竇儼請令鄉村團爲義營，每有盜發，則鳴鼓舉火，丁壯雲集，盜少民多，無能脫者。此二法者，大畧相似。然以愚意論之，用之魯、鄭平原之地則可，用之江西山谿險阻之間，恐亦未宜。

竇儼又嘗請令盜賊自相糾告，以其所告資產之半賞之。又崔安潛治盜，出庫錢千五百緡，分置三市，榜曰：「能告捕一盜，賞五百緡。」於是諸盜相疑，散逃出境。此二法者，大意亦同。然以愚意評之，賞以官錢，恐不可繼；不若就其資產賞之，似爲可常。

然古法有限，事變無窮，泥古人之陳跡，以爲今日治盜之良圖，非執事所以策愚意也。益亦曰任人乎？蓋得人而任之，則可以料敵制變，可以隨事設謀
translation_en:
…without an effective method, the harm they cause can indeed exceed that caused by the foreign peoples. For this reason, the ancients always gave this matter close attention. During the Northern Wei dynasty, when bandits were numerous in Yanzhou, Regional Inspector Li Chong ordered each village to erect a tower and hang a drum in it. Whenever bandits appeared, the drum was struck; within moments, the sound spread a hundred li. Thereafter, no bandit outbreak went without arrests. During the Later Zhou dynasty, when bandits were numerous in Xinzheng, Dou Yan proposed ordering villages to organize themselves into volunteer defense camps. Whenever bandits appeared, drums would be beaten and signal fires lit, and able-bodied men would gather like clouds. With few bandits and many villagers, none could escape. These two methods were broadly similar. In my humble judgment, however, they could be used on the plains of Lu and Zheng, but might not be suitable amid the rugged mountains and ravines of Jiangxi.

Dou Yan also once proposed having bandits inform against one another, rewarding each informer with half the property of the person he accused. Cui Anqian, too, when suppressing banditry, took fifteen hundred strings of cash from the treasury and divided them among three markets. He posted a proclamation stating: “Anyone who informs against a bandit and secures his capture will receive five hundred strings of cash.” The bandits consequently became suspicious of one another, scattered, and fled beyond his jurisdiction. These two methods likewise shared the same general principle. In my humble assessment, however, rewards paid from public funds might be unsustainable. It would be better to reward informers from the bandits’ own property; this would seem practicable as a lasting measure.

Yet ancient methods are finite, while changing circumstances are inexhaustible. To cling to the precedents left by the ancients and regard them as sound plans for suppressing banditry today is not what you intended when soliciting my humble views through this policy question. Might the answer simply be to appoint the right men [?]? For if the right men are found and entrusted with responsibility, they can assess the enemy and master changing circumstances, and devise plans suited to each situation…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
可以立奇功於萬全可以消大患於無跡
故不患有渤海之盗而患無龔遂不患有
朝歌之盗而患無虞詡不患有李順劉旰
之盗而患無張詠得如三人者而任之則
盗賊並起如渤海屯聚連年如朝歌賊衆
數十萬如西蜀尚不足慮而况於今日南
贛之嘯聚臨瑞之竊發也哉抑天下多盗
之故愚亦嘗求之矣蓋盗之未起也當有
以塞其源而其既起也當有以節其流何
===
謂塞其源孟子曰民無恒產則無恒心苟
無恒心放僻邪侈無不爲已故使民有恒
產者所以塞其源也何謂節其流夏書曰
殲厥渠魁脅從罔治舊染汚俗咸與維新
故誅止於首惡者所以節其流也其源既
塞則盗自不發其流既節則雖發而易除
所謂長策宜無過於此者不識今日司民
牧者當盗賊之未起能輕徭薄賦省刑罰
吏不肯肆其侵漁如孟子之意乎其不幸
punctuated:
可以立奇功於萬全，可以消大患於無跡。故不患有渤海之盗，而患無龔遂；不患有朝歌之盗，而患無虞詡；不患有李順劉旰之盗，而患無張詠。得如三人者而任之，則盗賊並起如渤海，屯聚連年如朝歌，賊衆數十萬如西蜀，尚不足慮，而况於今日南贛之嘯聚、臨瑞之竊發也哉！
抑天下多盗之故，愚亦嘗求之矣。蓋盗之未起也，當有以塞其源；而其既起也，當有以節其流。何謂塞其源？孟子曰：「民無恒產，則無恒心。苟無恒心，放僻邪侈，無不爲已。」故使民有恒產者，所以塞其源也。何謂節其流？夏書曰：「殲厥渠魁，脅從罔治。舊染汚俗，咸與維新。」故誅止於首惡者，所以節其流也。其源既塞，則盗自不發；其流既節，則雖發而易除。所謂長策，宜無過於此者。不識今日司民牧者，當盗賊之未起，能輕徭薄賦、省刑罰，吏不肯肆其侵漁，如孟子之意乎？其不幸
translation_en:
…can accomplish extraordinary feats with complete security and eliminate great dangers without leaving a trace. Thus the concern is not that there are bandits in Bohai, but that there is no Gong Sui; not that there are bandits in Chaoge, but that there is no Yu Xu; not that there are bandits such as Li Shun and Liu Gan, but that there is no Zhang Yong. If men like these three could be found and entrusted with responsibility, even bandits rising everywhere as in Bohai, gathering in strongholds for successive years as in Chaoge, or numbering several hundred thousand as in western Shu would give no cause for anxiety. How much less, then, the bands gathering today in Nan and Gan, or the outbreaks of banditry in Lin and Rui!
I have also sought to understand why bandits are so numerous throughout the realm. Before banditry arises, there must be means to stop up its source; once it has arisen, there must be means to check its flow. What does stopping up its source mean? Mencius says: “When the people lack a constant livelihood, they lack constant hearts. If they lack constant hearts, there is no dissoluteness, perversity, wickedness, or excess in which they will not engage.” Thus, ensuring that the people have a constant livelihood is the means of stopping up its source. What does checking its flow mean? The Book of Xia says: “Destroy their ringleaders; do not punish those compelled to follow. Allow all those formerly tainted by corrupt customs to renew themselves.” Thus, confining execution to the chief malefactors is the means of checking its flow. Once its source is stopped up, banditry will naturally not arise; once its flow is checked, even if it arises, it will be easy to eliminate. No enduring strategy should surpass this. I wonder whether those who govern and shepherd the people today, before banditry arises, can lighten labor service, reduce taxes, and lessen punishments, with officials refusing to indulge in predatory exactions, in accordance with Mencius’s intent. If, unfortunately, …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
而至於盜起又能長慮却顧簡節疏目不
歷及其支黨如夏書所云乎於此而究心
焉治盜之功當不在龔遂虞詡張詠三人
之下臆說如斯執事進而教之幸甚
punctuated: 而至於盜起，又能長慮却顧，簡節疏目，不歷及其支黨，如《夏書》所云乎？於此而究心焉，治盜之功當不在龔遂、虞詡、張詠三人之下。臆說如斯，執事進而教之，幸甚。
translation_en: …and banditry does arise, can they then consider the long term and look back carefully, simplify restrictions and loosen the mesh of enforcement, without extending punishment to every subsidiary adherent, as the Documents of Xia says? If they devote their minds to this, their achievements in suppressing banditry should be no less than those of Gong Sui, Yu Xu, and Zhang Yong. Such are my tentative views. I would be most fortunate if you, sir, would offer further instruction.

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試録後序
正德丁卯之秋天下當大比
取士江西省內諸臣舉行如
制録成考試官教授田〔楨〕序于其
端者悉矣〔邦彥〕當有以識其
後竊惟盈天地之間者惟萬
物而代天理物者惟君爲君
===
分理者惟臣明明在朝穆穆
布列皆臣也非廣求人才何
以充之然人才必由教養而
成必由選舉而得選舉者就
其教養之有成者而取之也
大則棟梁小則榱桷咸於是
乎集而萬物之所以育天地
punctuated:
江西鄉試録後序

正德丁卯之秋，天下當大比取士，江西省內諸臣舉行如制。録成，考試官教授田〔楨〕序于其端者悉矣。〔邦彥〕當有以識其後。

竊惟盈天地之間者惟萬物，而代天理物者惟君，爲君分理者惟臣。明明在朝，穆穆布列，皆臣也。非廣求人才，何以充之？然人才必由教養而成，必由選舉而得。選舉者，就其教養之有成者而取之也。大則棟梁，小則榱桷，咸於是乎集，而萬物之所以育、天地
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the dingmao year of the Zhengde reign (1507), the empire was due to hold the triennial examination to select scholars. The officials within Jiangxi Province conducted it according to the prescribed regulations. When the record was completed, the Examiner, Professor Tian Zhen 田楨, provided a comprehensive preface at its beginning. I, Bangyan 邦彥, should therefore add some remarks at its end.

I humbly reflect that what fills the space between Heaven and Earth is the myriad things; it is the ruler who orders them on Heaven’s behalf, and his ministers who share in their governance on his behalf. Those who stand illustrious at court and are solemnly arrayed in their ranks are all ministers. Without seeking talented men far and wide, how could these posts be filled? Yet talent must be developed through education and nurture, and obtained through selection. Selection means choosing from among those whose education and nurture have borne fruit. The greater talents serve as ridgepoles and beams, the lesser as rafters; all are assembled through this process. And the means by which the myriad things are nurtured, and Heaven and Earth …

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
之所以位
宗社之所以靈長吾
君之所以安富尊榮而克享盛名
於天下後世者悉於是乎有
賴人才之在天下可不重哉
凡司選才之任者可不慎哉
而凡得以才與在選列者又
可不知所自重哉重其身所
以重吾
===
國也自重之道則諸士子業之
有素矣其慎無忘哉夫自鄉
舉里選之法既遠天地正氣
所鍾鮮有不自科目進者大
而調元贊化次而建功立事
punctuated: 之所以位，宗社之所以靈長，吾君之所以安富尊榮而克享盛名於天下後世者，悉於是乎有賴。人才之在天下，可不重哉？凡司選才之任者，可不慎哉？而凡得以才與在選列者，又可不知所自重哉？重其身，所以重吾國也。自重之道，則諸士子業之有素矣，其慎無忘哉！夫自鄉舉里選之法既遠，天地正氣所鍾，鮮有不自科目進者。大而調元贊化，次而建功立事，
translation_en: …are established in their proper places; the enduring vitality of the ancestral temples and the altars of state; and our ruler’s security, wealth, dignity, and glory, enabling him to enjoy great renown throughout the realm and among later generations—all depend upon this. Can men of talent in the world be regarded lightly? Can those charged with selecting talent fail to exercise care? And can all those whose talents earn them a place among the selected fail to understand how to value themselves? To value oneself is to value our state. You scholars have long cultivated the way of valuing yourselves: take care never to forget it! Now that the system of recommendation from the districts and selection from the villages belongs to the distant past, few of those endowed with the upright vital force of Heaven and Earth have advanced except through the examinations. At the highest level, they harmonize the primal forces and assist the work of transformation; at the next, they render meritorious service and accomplish undertakings…

title: 正德二年江西鄉試錄
text:
在古在今班班炳炳蓋亦不
待一一稱引而可知已孰非
知所重而篤念
君父之所以涵育造就之恩者哉
嗚呼
君父之恩大矣
君父之望深矣臣子之所重矣
直隸河間府任丘縣儒學教
諭范邦彥謹序
punctuated:
在古在今，班班炳炳，蓋亦不待一一稱引而可知已。孰非知所重而篤念君父之所以涵育造就之恩者哉？嗚呼！君父之恩大矣！君父之望深矣！臣子之所重矣！
直隸河間府任丘縣儒學教諭范邦彥謹序。
translation_en:
…in antiquity and in the present, their achievements are conspicuous and brilliant; surely they are known without needing to cite each one. Which of them did not understand what they must hold in esteem and cherish a profound sense of gratitude for the nurturing and formation bestowed by their sovereign and father? Alas! Great is the grace of our sovereign and father! Profound are his expectations! Weighty indeed are the responsibilities of his servants and subjects!
Respectfully prefaced by Fan Bangyan, Instructor in the Confucian School of Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region (Zhili).
